events.headline: CBSL reviews lenders’ early settlement fees and parate auctions after complaints pile up
events.summary: CBSL reviewed early settlement and parate practices in the first half of 2026 No findings or new rules have been disclosed yet The Central Bank of Sri Lanka (CBSL) carried out targeted reviews of how lenders charge borrowers for settling term loans early and how banks seize mortgaged property under parate execution, following a “significant volume of consumer complaints” in both areas, the Central Bank revealed. The thematic reviews, conducted in the first half of 2026, covered the early settlement practices of licensed banks and finance companies on term loans and the parate execution process of licensed banks.

sources.headline: CBSL reviews lenders’ early settlement fees and parate auctions after complaints pile up
CBSL reviews lenders’ early settlement fees and parate auctions after complaints pile up

events.headline: Sampath Bank’s Rs. 10 b debenture issue oversubscribed by 22.7%
events.summary: Sampath Bank PLC’s debenture issue was oversubscribed and closed at its maximum of Rs. 10 billion, having drawn applications worth Rs. 12.27 billion, with a small number of large-value payments made through Real Time Gross Settlement (RTGS) transfers and Letters of Guarantee accounting for nearly the entire amount. According to the Registrars to the issue, Central Depository Systems Ltd., the bank received 31 applications for 122.66 million debentures as at 22 October, against a maximum of 100 million debentures on offer, oversubscribing the issue by 22.7%. Excess demand amounted to Rs. 2.27 billion, or 22.66 million debentures.

sources.headline: Sampath Bank’s Rs. 10 b debenture issue oversubscribed by 22.7%

events.headline: BOC opens largest ever Debenture Issue on November 3, 2026
events.summary: Bank of Ceylon (BOC) is set to create another milestone in the country’s capital market with the launch of Sri Lanka’s largest-ever listed debenture issue, with a maximum issue size of LKR 30 billion. The Bank proposes to initially raise LKR 10 billion, with an option to increase the issue to LKR 20 billion in the event of an oversubscription of the initial tranche and a further option to increase the total issue size up to LKR 30 billion, making it the largest listed debenture issue undertaken in Sri Lanka. The proposed issue comprises Basel III compliant, Tier 2, Listed, Rated, Unsecured, Subordinated, Redeemable debentures with a non-viability write-down feature.

sources.headline: BOC opens largest ever Debenture Issue on November 3, 2026
BOC to raise up to Rs. 30 b in Sri Lanka’s largest-ever listed debt issue

events.headline: Stock market rattled by oil supply chain disruptions
events.summary: Senewiratne A Brent crude oil price increase due to supply chain disruptions in the Middle East owing to Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabian targets, negatively impacted the CSE yesterday. Most foreign and local investors were worried over a probable oil price hike in Sri Lanka that would impact the manufacturing and production sectors in the country. The All Share Price Index went down by 11.06 points, while the S and P SL20 went up by 0.56 points. Turnover stood at Rs 656 million with two crossings. Those crossings were: Access Engineering 1 million shares crossed to the tune of Rs 74.5 million and its shares traded at Rs 74.50 and Commercial Bank 303,000 shares crossed for Rs 59 million; its shares traded at Rs 195.

sources.headline: Stock market rattled by oil supply chain disruptions

events.headline: Amana Bank opens 50th Self Banking Centre in Grandpass
events.summary: The new Self Banking Centre was officially unveiled by Amana Bank Managing Director/CEO Mohamed Azmeer together with Senior Vice President - Chief Compliance Officer Ajmal Naleer, Senior Vice President - Business Banking Irshad Iqbal, Vice President – Retail Banking and Marketing Siddeeque Akbar and other senior officials of the Bank Amana Bank has further expanded its customer location network with the opening of its 50th Self Banking Centre in Grandpass, Colombo, marking another significant milestone as the Bank celebrates its 15th Anniversary. With this opening, Amana Bank’s footprint has grown to 83 customer locations, including 33 fully fledged branches.

sources.headline: Amana Bank opens 50th Self Banking Centre in Grandpass

events.headline: Union Assurance-NTB strengthen bancassurance partnership
events.summary: Union Assurance PLC and Nations Trust Bank PLC (NTB) have renewed their long-standing exclusive bancassurance partnership, further strengthening an alliance that has played a pivotal role in expanding access to financial protection solutions for the customers across the country. The renewed partnership reflects the shared commitment of both organisations to delivering holistic financial solutions that seamlessly combine banking convenience with life insurance protection. Through this collaboration, the customers will continue to have convenient access to solutions designed to help safeguard their financial futures while supporting their evolving aspirations and life goals. Over the years, the partnership has evolved into one of Sri Lanka’s leading bancassurance collaborations, underpinned by a strong focus on customer centricity, innovation and service excellence.

sources.headline: Union Assurance-NTB strengthen bancassurance partnership

events.headline: HNB FINANCE-Toyota Lanka expand vehicle-leasing solutions
events.summary: Manager Ruwan Indika HNB FINANCE PLC and Toyota Lanka (Private) Limited have entered into a strategic partnership to offer competitive leasing solutions for the customers purchasing brand-new Toyota vehicles and Toyota Sure Certified Used Vehicles. The partnership was recently formalised through a memorandum of understanding (MoU), reinforcing the commitment of both parties to collaborate on this initiative. Under the agreement, HNB FINANCE will provide leasing facilities for eligible Toyota customers, combining access to formal financing with a package of after-sales and ownership benefits offered by Toyota Lanka. HNB FINANCE Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer Chaminda Prabhath said, “Reliable access to vehicle finance is important not only for individual mobility but also for business activity and broader economic participation.

sources.headline: HNB FINANCE-Toyota Lanka expand vehicle-leasing solutions
HNB FINANCE, Toyota Lanka forge partnership to expand vehicle-leasing solutions

events.headline: Seylan Bank-Fairway Latitude make home ownership more accessible
events.summary: Seylan Bank PLC has entered into a strategic partnership with Fairway Latitude, a subsidiary of Fairway Holdings, one of Sri Lanka’s leading real estate and property development companies, to provide tailored home loan solutions to the customers purchasing luxury apartments from Fairway Latitude. The partnership was formalised through the signing of a memorandum of understanding, marking the beginning of a collaborative effort to make property ownership more accessible through flexible financing options, personalised support and faster processing times. Under the partnership, the eligible customers purchasing property directly from Fairway Latitude can access Seylan Bank’s housing loan facilities with exclusive benefits, including repayment periods of up to 25 years and loan approvals processed within seven days.

sources.headline: Seylan Bank-Fairway Latitude make home ownership more accessible

events.headline: CBSL stresses public trust in AI adoption
events.summary: Sri Lanka (CBSL) has stressed that public trust must remain central to the adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) as the technology increasingly influences institutional decision-making, CBSL Governor Dr P Nandalal Weerasinghe said at its 76th Anniversary Oration on Friday (23). Speaking at the event, held under the theme The Intelligent Central Bank: Building Trust in the Age of AI , Dr Weerasinghe said: “As we embrace emerging technologies, we must ensure that innovation strengthens rather than diminishes trust. AI is rapidly transforming the way institutions generate insights, make decisions, deliver services, and manage risk.” “The Central Bank’s trust has always been our most valuable asset.

sources.headline: CBSL stresses public trust in AI adoption

events.headline: Sri Lanka managing the tide amid global commodity volatility, CBSL data shows
events.summary: Sri Lanka’s economic recovery continues to encounter a complex global landscape, successfully balancing domestic stabilisation against mounting external pressures and commodity volatility. As latest data from the Central Bank of Sri Lanka illustrates, the nation’s economic machinery is holding a resilient course even as international headwinds test its buffers. Global commodity markets have introduced renewed friction, most notably through sharp movements in energy prices. Amid supply concerns stemming from ongoing geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, crude oil prices trended upward during October 2026, with Brent crude touching a five-month high. For an import-dependent economy, such volatility directly impacts external trade accounts.

sources.headline: Sri Lanka managing the tide amid global commodity volatility, CBSL data shows

events.headline: Bond market yields open steady to higher on selected tenors
events.summary: The secondary Bond market yesterday kicked off the fresh trading week with yields holding broadly steady across majority of the yield curve. However, selective selling pressure on the 2033 and 2034 tenors saw yields push higher. Market activity and transaction volumes remained at moderate levels, ahead of an auction packed week. The week will see back-to-back primary auctions, with a Rs. 100 billion Treasury Bill auction scheduled for tomorrow (28), followed by a Rs. 100 billion Treasury Bond auction on Thursday (29). The 15.02.28 maturity traded at the rate of 10.45%. The 01.08.30 and 15.10.30 maturities traded at the rates of 11.50% and 11.55%-11.54% respectively.

sources.headline: Bond market yields open steady to higher on selected tenors

events.headline: PDMO rejects all Domestic Dollar Bond bids; market says bid rates too high
events.summary: - Turns down every bid at 23 Oct. auction for $ 100 m issue, which had option to raise up to $ 300 m - Notice cites only issuer’s right to accept or reject any application; no other details given The Public Debt Management Office (PDMO) has rejected all bids received at its Domestic Dollar Bond auction held on 23 October, with market sources indicating that demand was encouraging, but the rates bid were too high. The issue was for $ 100 million, with the option of raising up to $ 300 million. Pursuant to Section 6 of the Offer Document, which reserves the Issuer’s right to accept or reject any application, in whole or in part, the Issuer has decided not to accept any bids received under this auction,” the PDMO said in its notice, giving no further details.

sources.headline: PDMO rejects all Domestic Dollar Bond bids; market says bid rates too high

events.headline: CSE starts week in red, down 0.23%
events.summary: The Colombo stock market yesterday opened the week in red, extending losses into a sixth consecutive session. The ASPI was down 0.23% or 44.35 points at 19,640.56 and the active S&P SL20 fell 0.21% or 11.76 points to 5,601.87. Market turnover was nearly Rs. 666.3 million on 29.7 million shares traded. Foreign investors were net sellers on a net outflow of Rs. 6.6 million. With 123 counters ending in red against 80 gainers, the top contributors to the ASPI decline were CARS, COMB, LAMB, DIST and HAYL. First Capital Research said the bourse opened on a positive note but failed to sustain its early momentum, with continued fluctuations throughout the first half of the session before ultimately closing in negative territory.

sources.headline: CSE starts week in red, down 0.23%

events.headline: Medium Term Revenue Strategy: Tax weaknesses to be in focus
events.summary: Sri Lanka can expect to see greater focus on addressing weaknesses in broadening its tax base and increasing tax compliance within the Medium Term Revenue Strategy (MTRS), which is to include the consultative input of the International Monetary Fund (IMF), IMF Resident Representative to Sri Lanka Martha Tesfaye Woldemicheal said in a recently published (24) exclusive webinar held by CT Smith last month. These two points: broadening the tax base and addressing compliance and so on, are best addressed also in a holistic manner in the development of a Medium-Term Revenue Strategy (MTRS) and this is something very important that we are discussing with the authorities and also providing support on,” she said.

sources.headline: Medium Term Revenue Strategy: Tax weaknesses to be in focus

events.headline: PM tells CNN IMF priorities align with Govt.’s own
events.summary: Prime Minister Dr. Harini Amarasuriya - Says IMF approachable, Govt. able to raise concerns on governance, corruption, fiscal discipline - Economic stability among immediate priorities after election Prime Minister Dr. Harini Amarasuriya has told CNN that several of the International Monetary Fund’s (IMF) priorities align with the Government’s own objectives, underpinning its decision to continue Sri Lanka’s IMF program despite her party’s earlier opposition. Dr. Amarasuriya said the Government had been able to discuss its concerns with the IMF, particularly on governance, corruption, and fiscal discipline. When we came into power, the IMF agreement was already signed and we started working with them, and we found them approachable,” she told CNN’s Richard Quest of ‘Quest Means Business.’ Maintaining economic stability was among the administration’s immediate priorities following the election, she said, adding that the country had made considerable progress since the 2022 crisis.

sources.headline: PM tells CNN IMF priorities align with Govt.’s own

events.headline: Sustainable solutions to emotive issues
events.summary: It has had to face down demands from sections of the Buddhist clergy and Opposition parties to release the General Secretary of the nationalist Sinhala grouping, the Bodu Bala Sena, Ven. Galagoda Aththe Gnanasara Thera from his prison sentence for contempt of court. The Government had to face a protest march organised by Buddhist monks and the Opposition parties. Its supporters organised an even bigger march to support the Government’s position. It is notable that the general population did not get involved in either march in any substantial number. The issue has now become a test of whether the Government will uphold its commitment to apply the law equally, irrespective of a person’s position or status, even when doing so brings it into conflict with powerful nationalist and religious sentiments.

sources.headline: Sustainable solutions to emotive issues

events.headline: ‘All-inclusive Constitution’: Harini’s statement in CNN interview draws criticism
events.summary: News Published on By Share Tweet By Shamindra Ferdinando Former SLPP MP Gevindu Cumaratunga says the government should explain what Prime Minister Dr. Harini Amarasuriya has really meant by the all-inclusive new Constitution. The civil society activist said that the government owed an explanation as to how it intended to address the root causes of the war that was brought to a successful conclusion in May 2009. Cumaratunga said so when The Island sought his response to PM Amarasuriya declaration, in an interview with Richard Quest, on CNN. Responding to queries pertaining to constitutional reforms, PM Amarasuriya, while declaring serious flaws in the country’s supreme law, made reference to the 22 Amendments enacted over the years.

sources.headline: ‘All-inclusive Constitution’: Harini’s statement in CNN interview draws criticism

events.headline: ‘Sri Lanka turning page toward sustainable, long-term transformation’
events.summary: Moving decisively past the economic meltdown of recent years, Sri Lanka is positioning itself as a vibrant regional hub for trade, industry, technology, and investment. That was the core message delivered by Chathuranga Abeysinghe, Deputy Minister of Industry and Entrepreneurship Development, during a high-profile conversation at the NDTV World Summit 2026 in New Delhi. Participating in a session titled “Sri Lanka’s Economic Reset: Recovery, Resilience and the Road Ahead,” the Deputy Minister expressed profound gratitude to the government and people of India for standing firmly by Sri Lanka during its severe economic crisis in 2022.

sources.headline: ‘Sri Lanka turning page toward sustainable, long-term transformation’

events.headline: “Trust a National Asset”: IMF Chief Information Officer
events.summary: Marking a milestone in the history of financial governance, the Central Bank of Sri Lanka (CBSL) celebrated its 76th anniversary on October 23 with a forward-looking oration delivered by the International Monetary Fund’s Chief Information Officer, Shirin Hamid. Addressing leaders, policymakers, and technologists, her keynote speech bridged the lessons of Sri Lanka’s arduous economic recovery with the pressing, high-stakes challenges of the artificial intelligence era. Tracing the institution’s origins back to 1950, Hamid reminded the audience that central banks were founded not merely as economic policy bodies, but as foundational institutions of trust, security, and public confidence.

sources.headline: “Trust a National Asset”: IMF Chief Information Officer
Central Bank of the future needs to be intelligence-driven public institution, says IMF CIO

events.headline: Minister highlights new investment opportunities ahead of SL EXPO 2027
events.summary: Sri Lanka made a direct pitch to British investors at a special Business and Investment Forum in London, presenting the island as a stable, reform-driven economy ready for deeper partnership with the United Kingdom. Held under the patronage of Trade Minister Wasantha Samarasinghe, the forum drew business leaders, investors and industry representatives from both countries. Sri Lanka’s delegation included High Commissioner Nimal Senadheera, UK Trade Envoy Lord Hannett, Ministry of Industry and Entrepreneurship Development Secretary Thilaka Jayasundara, EDB Chairman/CEO Mangala Wijesinghe and Board of Investment (BOI) representatives. Strong participation from British firms in IT, real estate, energy and food processing, the Minister said, “Clearly reflects their keen interest in expanding trade and investment cooperation with Sri Lanka,” He noted that the UK is among Sri Lanka’s most important trading partners and its third-largest export market.

sources.headline: Minister highlights new investment opportunities ahead of SL EXPO 2027

events.headline: Policy priorities to achieve durable growth in Sri Lanka
events.summary: S ustaining Sri Lanka’s post-crisis macroeconomic stability requires productivity-enhancing reforms to achieve durable and inclusive growth. Against this backdrop, the Institute of Policy Studies of Sri Lanka (IPS) hosted a roundtable discussion on 14 October 2026 on its flagship publication, Sri Lanka State of the Economy 2026, to discuss policy priorities to rebuild the country’s economic foundations amidst ongoing domestic and global uncertainties. IPS Research Fellows Dr Asanka Wijesinghe and Dr Lakmini Fernando presented key findings, followed by interventions from Dr Yashodha Senadheera, Deputy Director of the Economic Research Department of the Central Bank of Sri Lanka (CBSL); Dr Liliya Aleksanyan, Senior Country Economist for Sri Lanka at the Asian Development Bank (ADB); Mr. Sanjaya Ariyawansa, Senior Economist at Sampath Bank; and other invited parties.

sources.headline: Policy priorities to achieve durable growth in Sri Lanka
Beyond recovery: Policy priorities to achieve durable growth in Sri Lanka

events.headline: Over half of NBFI household borrowers in high-risk bands as Stage 2 loans nearly double
events.summary: Some 52.4% of household borrowers at finance companies fall in high or very high risk bands, compared with 24.1% at banks Stage 2 loans at finance companies rose 92.1% in a year, while gold-backed Stage 2 loans jumped 279.2% More than half of the households borrowing from finance companies fall in the high or very high risk categories based on their Credit Information Bureau (CRIB) scores, over twice the share among bank borrowers, as early signs of stress build up in the sector’s vehicle and gold-backed loan books, as per CBSL data. As at end June 2026, 52.4 percent of household borrowers of non-bank financial institutions (NBFIs), comprising finance companies and a specialised leasing company whose registration was cancelled in June, fell within the high or very high risk categories, compared with 24.1 percent at banks.

sources.headline: Over half of NBFI household borrowers in high-risk bands as Stage 2 loans nearly double
Over half of NBFI household borrowers in high-risk bands as Stage 2 loans nearly double

events.headline: Fitch assigns ‘A-(EXP)(lka)’ rating to Asia Asset Finance’s proposed debentures
events.summary: Fitch Ratings yesterday assigned Asia Asset Finance PLC’s (AAF) proposed Sri Lankan rupee-denominated subordinated listed debentures of up to Rs. 3 billion an expected National Long-Term Rating of ‘A-(EXP)(lka)’. AAF is rated ‘A+(lka)’ with a Stable Outlook. The debentures are likely to have a five-year maturity and will be listed on the Colombo Stock Exchange (CSE). AAF plans to use the proceeds to strengthen its Tier 2 capital base, the secondary layer of regulatory capital, and to support loan-book expansion. The final rating is subject to Fitch receiving final documentation that conforms to information already received.

sources.headline: Fitch assigns ‘A-(EXP)(lka)’ rating to Asia Asset Finance’s proposed debentures

audit.headline: Flood warning issued for Kelani River Basin
audit.summary: Latest News Published on By Share Tweet Significant rainfall has been recorded in the upper catchment areas of the Kelani River Basin. Based on the prevailing rainfall conditions and the analysis of water levels recorded at the river gauging stations maintained by the Department of Irrigation within the Kelani River Basin, there is a risk of minor flooding occurring within the next 24 hours from now in the low-lying areas of the Kelani River Valley falling within the Divisional Secretariat Divisions of Ruwanwella, Seethawaka, Dompe, Dehiowita, Eheliyagoda, Yatiyantota and Bulathkohupitiya. The public residing in these areas and motorists travelling through these areas are requested to exercise extreme caution in view of this situation.

Meanwhile, the Commanding Officers of the visiting ships called on the Commander Western Naval Area Rear Admiral Harsha De Silva at the Western Naval Command Headquarters today.

audit.headline: IPL 2027 auction to be held on December 16
audit.summary: Latest News Published on By Share Tweet The IPL auction for the 2027 season will take place on December 16 in Goa. The day-long mini-auction will be held on the same day as the second ODI between India and Sri Lanka in Bengaluru. The auction will take place nearly a month after the reten deadline, which the IPL recently informed the franchises will be November 15. Soon after that, the IPL will send the franchises the registered pool of players to shortlist from before the final list is sent out, along with the order of the sets, in the week leading into the auction. The IPL trade window has seen just two trades since the 2026 season ended. According to the IPL rules, the trade window starts a month after a season ends, stays open up to a week before the auction date, and then continues up until a month before the start of the next season.
audit.body: Latest News Published on By Share Tweet The IPL auction for the 2027 season will take place on December 16 in Goa. The day-long mini-auction will be held on the same day as the second ODI between India and Sri Lanka in Bengaluru. The auction will take place nearly a month after the reten deadline, which the IPL recently informed the franchises will be November 15. Soon after that, the IPL will send the franchises the registered pool of players to shortlist from before the final list is sent out, along with the order of the sets, in the week leading into the auction. The IPL trade window has seen just two trades since the 2026 season ended. According to the IPL rules, the trade window starts a month after a season ends, stays open up to a week before the auction date, and then continues up until a month before the start of the next season. In June, Lucknow Super Giants swapped their captain Risbah Pant to Delhi Capitals (DC) in return for wristspinner Kuldeep Yadav. Recently, DC also traded fast bowler T Natarajan to Sunrisers Hyderabad for uncapped legspinner Zeeshan Ansari. The IPL has not yet finalised the dates for the 2027 season. But, in 2024, while announcing the dates for the following three seasons, it had chalked out the window between March 14 and May 30. However, in September this year, post the BCCI’s AGM, board secretary Devajit Saikia had indicated that the tournament could start in March-end. This is the last mini-auction in the IPL’s current cycle, with a mega auction scheduled ahead of the 2028 season. The next mega auction will kick-off the IPL’s next media rights cycle, though the BCCI is yet to release the tender. In 2022, the IPL joined the ivy league of global sport after the media rights were sold for an astronomical sum of INR 48,390.5 crore (US$ 6.2 billion approx.). (Cricinfo)

audit.headline: Mecca defence alliance members in Tehran to defuse Iran-US, Yemen tensions
audit.summary: Latest News Published on By Share Tweet Ministers and senior security officials from Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye – the three nations that signed the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement – are in Tehran to discuss regional security issues amid threats of new US strikes on Iran. Saudi Defence Minister Khalid bin Salman Al Saud, Pakistani military chief Asim Munir and Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin met Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian and will discuss tensions with security chief Mohsen Rezaei. The meetings are among the highest-profile dialogues held in Tehran in recent months. While there is still little information on what might be discussed, the meetings come amid a flurry of diplomatic activity to deal with a new escalation between the United States and Iran.
audit.body: Latest News Published on By Share Tweet Ministers and senior security officials from Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye – the three nations that signed the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement – are in Tehran to discuss regional security issues amid threats of new US strikes on Iran. Saudi Defence Minister Khalid bin Salman Al Saud, Pakistani military chief Asim Munir and Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin met Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian and will discuss tensions with security chief Mohsen Rezaei. The meetings are among the highest-profile dialogues held in Tehran in recent months. While there is still little information on what might be discussed, the meetings come amid a flurry of diplomatic activity to deal with a new escalation between the United States and Iran. But analysts broadly believe the visit to Tehran by the three signatories of the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement, a regional defence alliance, will be enough to prevent a new outbreak in violence between the US and Iran. “The Mecca pact’s 11th-hour visit to Tehran is an attempt to tip the balance in favour of those willing to compromise before the guns start blazing again,” said Ali Vaez, deputy director of the Middle East and North Africa Program at the International Crisis Group. “But unless they arrive with a credible formula to bridge the US-Iran divide, they may find themselves with little more than goodwill in a race against the clock.” (Aljazeera)

audit.headline: Part of Antarctica named after former BBC science correspondent
audit.summary: Latest News Published on By Share Tweet Part of Antarctica has been named after former BBC science correspondent Jonathan Amos. A stretch of water between Rothschild Island and Alexander Island in the west of the White Continent is now called the Amos Channel. Amos was given the honour for his “exceptional and influential role in bringing Antarctic research to the forefront of public understanding” during his 38-year career at BBC News, the naming committee said. The channel is a new feature in Antarctica that appeared when a chunk of ice that connected Rothschild and Alexander Islands disintegrated. The melting ice sheets of this remote continent are just one of many aspects of polar science that Amos reported on while at the BBC. He also covered colossal icebergs, the fate of penguin colonies and a BBC exclusive about the discovery of Ernest Shackelton’s lost ship, the Endurance .
audit.body: Latest News Published on By Share Tweet Part of Antarctica has been named after former BBC science correspondent Jonathan Amos. A stretch of water between Rothschild Island and Alexander Island in the west of the White Continent is now called the Amos Channel. Amos was given the honour for his “exceptional and influential role in bringing Antarctic research to the forefront of public understanding” during his 38-year career at BBC News, the naming committee said. The channel is a new feature in Antarctica that appeared when a chunk of ice that connected Rothschild and Alexander Islands disintegrated. The melting ice sheets of this remote continent are just one of many aspects of polar science that Amos reported on while at the BBC. He also covered colossal icebergs, the fate of penguin colonies and a BBC exclusive about the discovery of Ernest Shackelton’s lost ship, the Endurance . “It’s absolutely incredible – what an extraordinary accolade. I’m so touched that there’s a little bit of Antarctica named after me,” Amos said. Despite his fascination with the South Pole, he has not yet travelled to the continent. “I’ve written about it so often, but always from my desk – this is quite the incentive to go and visit. “Antarctica is the front line of the biggest news story on planet Earth – climate change,” he added. The naming of geographical features in Antarctica follows strict rules. The Amos Channel was recommended by the UK Antarctic Place Names Committee, which looks after names for sites within the British Antarctic Territory, as well as South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands. Athena Dinar, from the British Antarctic Survey, said: “Jon’s passion for Antarctica and engaging journalism offers something for every reader, viewer or listener. “The naming of an Antarctic place in his honour is a fitting recognition of his outstanding contribution to the promotion of Antarctic research.” Amos joined the BBC in 1986 as a local radio reporter in Cambridge. He was part of the team that launched the BBC News website in 1997, and ran the online science desk for many years. He later worked as a BBC science correspondent across TV, radio and online, before leaving the organisation in 2024. “Jon consistently highlighted the importance of Antarctic research, explaining not only what science is being done there, but why it matters for society, climate understanding and the global environment,” said Fiona Fox, from the Science Media Centre. (BBC)

audit.headline: Schools closed tomorrow (27)
audit.summary: Latest News Published on By WEATHER FORECAST FOR 27 October 2026 Issued at 5.30 a.m. on 27 October 2026 by the Department of Meteorology The Severe Cyclonic Storm “Arnab” over the West central Bay of Bengal intensified into a ‘Very Severe Cyclonic Storm’ and lay centered at 02.30 a.m. today, the 27th October, 2026 over the near latitude 15.9°N and longitude 85.4°E about 890 km to the north-east of Kankasanthurai. It is very likely to continue to move west-northwestwards till 05.30 p.m. of 27th October and thereafter, it is very likely to move northwestwards and cross the Indian land through Andhra Pradesh coast as a very severe cyclonic storm by 11.30 a.m. of 28th October, 2026.

Latest News Published on By Ministers and senior security officials from Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye – the three nations that signed the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement – are in Tehran to discuss regional security issues amid threats of new US strikes on Iran. Saudi Defence Minister Khalid bin Salman Al Saud, Pakistani military chief Asim Munir and Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin met Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian and will discuss tensions with security chief Mohsen Rezaei. The meetings are among the highest-profile dialogues held in Tehran in recent months. While there is still little information on what might be discussed, the meetings come amid a flurry of diplomatic activity to deal with a new escalation between the United States and Iran. But analysts broadly believe the visit to Tehran by the three signatories of the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement, a regional defence alliance, will be enough to prevent a new outbreak in violence between the US and Iran. “The Mecca pact’s 11th-hour visit to Tehran is an attempt to tip the balance in favour of those willing to compromise before the guns start blazing again,” said Ali Vaez, deputy director of the Middle East and North Africa Program at the International Crisis Group. “But unless they arrive with a credible formula to bridge the US-Iran divide, they may find themselves with little more than goodwill in a race against the clock.” (Aljazeera) Latest News Published on By Part of Antarctica has been named after former BBC science correspondent Jonathan Amos. A stretch of water between Rothschild Island and Alexander Island in the west of the White Continent is now called the Amos Channel. Amos was given the honour for his “exceptional and influential role in bringing Antarctic research to the forefront of public understanding” during his 38-year career at BBC News, the naming committee said. The channel is a new feature in Antarctica that appeared when a chunk of ice that connected Rothschild and Alexander Islands disintegrated. The melting ice sheets of this remote continent are just one of many aspects of polar science that Amos reported on while at the BBC. He also covered colossal icebergs, the fate of penguin colonies and a BBC exclusive about the discovery of Ernest Shackelton’s lost ship, the Endurance . “It’s absolutely incredible – what an extraordinary accolade. I’m so touched that there’s a little bit of Antarctica named after me,” Amos said. Despite his fascination with the South Pole, he has not yet travelled to the continent. “I’ve written about it so often, but always from my desk – this is quite the incentive to go and visit. “Antarctica is the front line of the biggest news story on planet Earth – climate change,” he added. The naming of geographical features in Antarctica follows strict rules. The Amos Channel was recommended by the UK Antarctic Place Names Committee, which looks after names for sites within the British Antarctic Territory, as well as South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands. Athena Dinar, from the British Antarctic Survey, said: “Jon’s passion for Antarctica and engaging journalism offers something for every reader, viewer or listener. “The naming of an Antarctic place in his honour is a fitting recognition of his outstanding contribution to the promotion of Antarctic research.” Amos joined the BBC in 1986 as a local radio reporter in Cambridge. He was part of the team that launched the BBC News website in 1997, and ran the online science desk for many years. He later worked as a BBC science correspondent across TV, radio and online, before leaving the organisation in 2024. “Jon consistently highlighted the importance of Antarctic research, explaining not only what science is being done there, but why it matters for society, climate understanding and the global environment,” said Fiona Fox, from the Science Media Centre. (BBC)

audit.headline: USS Canberra (LCS-30) makes port call in Colombo

audit.body: 26 Oct 2026 | PARTNER CONTENT Fintrex Finance PLC hosted its Investor Forum 2026 on 9 October at Cinnamon Grand Colombo, bringing together leading experts from the financial, digital payments and cybersecurity sectors to discuss protecting wealth from scams, deepfakes and financial fraud. Held under the theme “Trust in the Digital Age – Protecting Wealth from Scams, Deepfakes and Financial Fraud,” the forum explored emerging digital threats, responsible investment decisions and the importance of strengthening trust as financial services increasingly embrace technology and artificial intelligence. The keynote address was delivered by Dr. Dharmasri Kumaratunge, former Assistant Governor of the Central Bank of Sri Lanka and former Secretary to the Ministry of Technology. The panel, moderated by cybersecurity and digital trust expert Mr. Asela Waidyalankara, featured Mr. Murtaza Jafferjee, CEO of JB Securities Ltd and Chair of the Advocata Institute; Mr. Channa De Silva, CEO of LankaPay (Private) Limited; and Eng. Kushan Sharma, CEO of TechCERT. The discussion highlighted the growing risks of financial scams, impersonation and deepfake-enabled fraudemphasizing investor awareness, secure payment systems, strong institutional controls and timely incident response. The forum also reflected Fintrex Finance’s vision of building a technology-driven, customer-centric financial services business. Under the leadership of Chairman Mr. Ajit Gunewardene and CEO Mr. Jayathilake Bandara, the company is focused on moving beyond the conventional branch-intensive model towards a more agile, digitally enabled approach that enhances accessibility, efficiency and customer convenience. As a licensed finance company operating under the regulatory framework of the Central Bank of Sri Lanka, Fintrex Finance continues to provide financial solutions including fixed deposits, savings and financing facilities. Through the Investor Forum 2026, Fintrex Finance reaffirmed its commitment to responsible innovation, financial awareness and building lasting customer relationships founded on trust and transparency.

audit.headline: ‘Sententia.ai’ backed by Lankan investment banker, joins NVIDIA Inception Programme
audit.summary: Sententia.ai, an early-stage legal-tech venture backed by Sri Lankan investment banker Sanjana Fernando, has been accepted into the NVIDIA for Startups Inception accelerator. The move gives the cross-border transaction structuring platform access to the chipmaker’s technical resources, AI ecosystem and global startup network, the company announced. NVIDIA’s Inception programme supports startups building AI-driven technology and does not take an equity stake in its members. Instead, it offers preferential access to NVIDIA hardware and software, technical training and exposure to its venture capital network. For a pre-commercial venture still validating its first structuring corridor, membership is a useful credential when courting design-partner law firms and institutional investors.
audit.body: Sententia.ai, an early-stage legal-tech venture backed by Sri Lankan investment banker Sanjana Fernando, has been accepted into the NVIDIA for Startups Inception accelerator.  The move gives the cross-border transaction structuring platform access to the chipmaker’s technical resources, AI ecosystem and global startup network, the company announced. NVIDIA’s Inception programme supports startups building AI-driven technology and does not take an equity stake in its members. Instead, it offers preferential access to NVIDIA hardware and software, technical training and exposure to its venture capital network. For a pre-commercial venture still validating its first structuring corridor, membership is a useful credential when courting design-partner law firms and institutional investors. Fernando, Managing Director of Melbourne-based STF Corporate Advisory, joined Sententia.ai as Corporate Advisor in September and now serves as Investor and Board Advisor. His career spans HSBC Investment Banking, Dresdner Kleinwort and Goldman Sachs, with his work covering mergers and acquisitions, capital raising and cross-border mandates. The venture positions itself beyond conventional legal automation. It argues that the future of law and finance lies in systems capable of understanding transaction architecture and navigating regulatory complexity. “We are building a neural network for undertaking transactions, transforming complex cross-border requirements into structured investment models, fund structures, risk intelligence, and execution-ready workflows,” the company noted. “Our vision is to make global capital programmable,” it added. Sententia.ai was conceptualised by Shayant Bhattacharjee, a law student at Maharashtra National Law University (MNLU), Nagpur, whose paralegal work on FDI and cross-border M&A mandates at Tier-1 law firms shaped the founding premise. He is joined by fellow MNLU students Prakhar Mishra and Navya Y., while Sanidhya Jain, who studies at Drexel University, Philadelphia, leads the venture’s AI architecture as Chief Technology Officer. Cambridge-trained corporate and TMT lawyer Rupal Chhaya sits on its advisory board. Meanwhile, the company said the Inception membership would support its efforts as it continues building what it describes as “the intelligence layer for global transactions.”

audit.headline: Softlogic extends warrant conversion window to November
audit.summary: Softlogic Holdings PLC has extended the payment deadline for converting its warrants into shares to 19 November, giving remaining warrant holders additional time to take part in the conglomerate’s equity raising as it continues to strengthen its capital base and pare down debt, a stock filing showed. The last date for payment, previously set for 7 October, was moved following a request to the Colombo Stock Exchange on 19 October, with the company noting that the change would not affect warrant holders who have already paid. The new shares will be deposited on or before 4 December and begin trading on 8 December. The warrants were issued at zero cost alongside Softlogic’s 2024 rights issue, which raised Rs.2.02 billion at Rs.10 a share, with subscribers receiving three warrants for every five rights shares.
audit.body: Softlogic Holdings PLC has extended the payment deadline for converting its warrants into shares to 19 November, giving remaining warrant holders additional time to take part in the conglomerate’s equity raising as it continues to strengthen its capital base and pare down debt, a stock filing showed. The last date for payment, previously set for 7 October, was moved following a request to the Colombo Stock Exchange on 19 October, with the company noting that the change would not affect warrant holders who have already paid. The new shares will be deposited on or before 4 December and begin trading on 8 December. The warrants were issued at zero cost alongside Softlogic’s 2024 rights issue, which raised Rs.2.02 billion at Rs.10 a share, with subscribers receiving three warrants for every five rights shares. Each of the roughly 121.6 million warrants is convertible into one share at Rs.10.50. As per its annual report, the company had received Rs.498 million from the conversion, with major shareholders Chairman and Managing Director Ashok Pathirage and Samena Ceylon Holdings having exercised their warrants. A further Rs.777 million is expected, lifting total proceeds to Rs.1.27 billion, earmarked for settling debt and meeting working capital needs. The fresh equity complements a debt restructuring drive under which Softlogic has signed offer letters for close to Rs.60 billion of loans, securing grace periods of six to 18 months on capital repayments, while requests covering a further Rs.15.7 billion await lender approval. Pathirage told Mirror Business last month that only a small fraction of the group’s debt remained to be restructured, with negotiations with lenders underway. Group revenue rose 24 percent to Rs.129 billion in 2025/26, while EBITDA grew 43 percent to Rs.17.8 billion and operating cash flow climbed 60 percent to Rs.14 billion. Finance costs eased 15 percent to Rs.13.7 billion, helping narrow the loss after tax by 68 percent to Rs.3.59 billion.

audit.headline: CBSL reviews lenders’ early settlement fees and parate auctions after complaints pile up
audit.summary: CBSL reviewed early settlement and parate practices in the first half of 2026 No findings or new rules have been disclosed yet The Central Bank of Sri Lanka (CBSL) carried out targeted reviews of how lenders charge borrowers for settling term loans early and how banks seize mortgaged property under parate execution, following a “significant volume of consumer complaints” in both areas, the Central Bank revealed. The thematic reviews, conducted in the first half of 2026, covered the early settlement practices of licensed banks and finance companies on term loans and the parate execution process of licensed banks. However, the Central Bank did not disclose its findings, the number of institutions examined or any corrective action, while the major policy measures it listed from July 2025 to end July 2026 include no new rules on either issue.
audit.body: CBSL reviewed early settlement and parate practices in the first half of 2026 No findings or new rules have been disclosed yet The Central Bank of Sri Lanka (CBSL) carried out targeted reviews of how lenders charge borrowers for settling term loans early and how banks seize mortgaged property under parate execution, following a “significant volume of consumer complaints” in both areas, the Central Bank revealed. The thematic reviews, conducted in the first half of 2026, covered the early settlement practices of licensed banks and finance companies on term loans and the parate execution process of licensed banks. However, the Central Bank did not disclose its findings, the number of institutions examined or any corrective action, while the major policy measures it listed from July 2025 to end July 2026 include no new rules on either issue. Officials of the Central Bank’s Financial Consumer Relations Department wrote in June that complaints relating to fees and charges increased by approximately 40 percent between 2023 and 2025, particularly over items such as processing fees, documentation charges and early settlement fees. Licensed banks accounted for 79 percent of complaints over the period and finance companies for 21 percent, meaning banks drew nearly four times as many. Complaints over high lending rates, by contrast, declined significantly. The officials pointed out that lenders “may need to strengthen disclosure practices” and “simplify fee structures”. Early settlement charges fall under the Financial Consumer Protection Regulations No. 01 of 2023, in force since February 2024, which list “requiring payment of un-accrued (future) interest/ early settlement fees on credit facilities, exceeding the levels permitted by the Central Bank, if any” as an unfair business practice. Meanwhile, parate execution allows banks to auction mortgaged property on a board resolution, without going to court, under the Recovery of Loans by Banks (Special Provisions) Act No. 4 of 1990. After the power was suspended in 2024, the government phased out relief for small and medium enterprises (SMEs) last year, ending it on June 30, 2025 for loans above Rs.50 million, September 30 for loans of Rs.25 million to Rs.50 million and December 31 for smaller loans, for borrowers who had begun talks with their banks by March 31, 2025. The first half of 2026 was thus the first period since early 2024 without any SME relief window. Banks maintain the power is rarely used, with the Sri Lanka Banks’ Association stating in July 2025 that it was applied to only about 1 percent of non-performing loans between 2019 and 2023. Borrowers are also under greater pressure, with the Central Bank raising its policy rate in May 2026 and banks’ Stage 3 loans recording slight increases at the end of both the first and second quarters of 2026, following Cyclone Ditwah, higher fuel prices and the Middle East conflict.

audit.headline: Over half of NBFI household borrowers in high-risk bands as Stage 2 loans nearly double
audit.summary: Some 52.4% of household borrowers at finance companies fall in high or very high risk bands, compared with 24.1% at banks Stage 2 loans at finance companies rose 92.1% in a year, while gold-backed Stage 2 loans jumped 279.2% More than half of the households borrowing from finance companies fall in the high or very high risk categories based on their Credit Information Bureau (CRIB) scores, over twice the share among bank borrowers, as early signs of stress build up in the sector’s vehicle and gold-backed loan books, as per CBSL data. As at end June 2026, 52.4 percent of household borrowers of non-bank financial institutions (NBFIs), comprising finance companies and a specialised leasing company whose registration was cancelled in June, fell within the high or very high risk categories, compared with 24.1 percent at banks.
audit.body: Some 52.4% of household borrowers at finance companies fall in high or very high risk bands, compared with 24.1% at banks Stage 2 loans at finance companies rose 92.1% in a year, while gold-backed Stage 2 loans jumped 279.2% More than half of the households borrowing from finance companies fall in the high or very high risk categories based on their Credit Information Bureau (CRIB) scores, over twice the share among bank borrowers, as early signs of stress build up in the sector’s vehicle and gold-backed loan books, as per CBSL data. As at end June 2026, 52.4 percent of household borrowers of non-bank financial institutions (NBFIs), comprising finance companies and a specialised leasing company whose registration was cancelled in June, fell within the high or very high risk categories, compared with 24.1 percent at banks. Nearly one in three, or 30.4 percent, sat in the very high risk band, more than double the 14.3 percent at banks, while only 31.6 percent were rated low or very low risk. NBFI household borrowers recorded an average CRIB score of 497.4, inside the very high risk band of 250 to 500 and 59.8 points below the bank average of 557.2, which falls in the average risk band. The overall household score improved to 538.2 from 511.6 a year earlier, although it remained in the high risk category. The Central Bank pointed out that NBFI scores had improved in recent quarters. The same divide held for businesses, with 53.9 percent of NBFI institutional borrowers in the two highest risk bands, against 21.6 percent at banks. “Nevertheless, the relatively larger share of higher risk in the NBFI sector remains an area warranting continued attention from a financial stability perspective,” the Central Bank cautioned. NBFIs are also gaining ground in household lending. Household credit grew 25.4 percent year-on-year at end June, up from 14.8 percent a year earlier, while NBFIs’ share of that lending rose to 37.5 percent from 35.5 percent. Repayment, however, improved, with loans carrying zero days in arrears rising to 67.7 percent of household exposures from 65.0 percent. Meanwhile, finance companies’ gross loans expanded 45.0 percent year-on-year, driven by vehicle-backed loans, which grew 46.3 percent, and gold-backed loans, which rose 59.8 percent. Together, the two accounted for 85.2 percent of the sector’s credit, up from 82.6 percent, a reliance the Central Bank flagged as a significant collateral concentration risk. However, the sector’s gross Stage 2 loans, which signal a significant rise in credit risk, jumped 92.1 percent, lifting the Stage 2 ratio to 15.4 percent from 11.6 percent. Stage 2 vehicle loans rose 75.5 percent, while Stage 2 gold-backed loans climbed 279.2 percent. Although the Stage 3 ratio fell to 5.1 percent from 8.3 percent, Stage 3 loans rose by Rs.23.6 billion in the second quarter alone, while Stage 3 impairment coverage slipped to 41.0 percent from 46.1 percent. The Central Bank attributed part of the Stage 2 increase to weaker repayment capacity among some borrowers following Cyclone Ditwah and the Middle East conflict. “The current uptick in Stage 2 loans reflects a potential buildup of credit risk within the sector and requires continuous monitoring and proactive risk mitigation by (finance companies),” it warned. Notably, the CRIB risk scores exclude gold-backed loans altogether, as CRIB is still incorporating pawning data and such data are not yet consistently reported by all financial institutions. This leaves out a segment that makes up 21.4 percent of finance company credit, and one in which Stage 2 loans have nearly quadrupled in a year. The Central Bank tightened loan-to-value limits on vehicle loans and introduced limits on gold-backed lending in May 2026, alongside a policy rate increase, and raised risk weights on gold-backed loans from September, measures it expects to slow credit growth in the sector in the coming quarters.

audit.headline: Jetstar captures Australian holiday growth as SriLankan eyes Perth
audit.summary: Jetstar has captured nearly a fifth of Australia’s tourist traffic to Sri Lanka in its first full month on the Melbourne-Colombo route, absorbing the bulk of the market’s growth while SriLankan Airlines, despite adding flights, carried roughly the same number of Australian tourists, as per SLTDA data. Airlines outside SLTDA’s list of named carriers accounted for 18.78 percent of the 10,951 Australian tourists who arrived in September, up from just 0.92 percent in July. While SLTDA does not list the Qantas Group’s low-cost arm separately, the jump coincides with Australian arrivals departing from Melbourne more than doubling to 4,256 from 2,111, and those routed through Singapore and Kuala Lumpur falling 19.6 percent and 32.1 percent respectively.
audit.body: Jetstar has captured nearly a fifth of Australia’s tourist traffic to Sri Lanka in its first full month on the Melbourne-Colombo route, absorbing the bulk of the market’s growth while SriLankan Airlines, despite adding flights, carried roughly the same number of Australian tourists, as per SLTDA data. Airlines outside SLTDA’s list of named carriers accounted for 18.78 percent of the 10,951 Australian tourists who arrived in September, up from just 0.92 percent in July. While SLTDA does not list the Qantas Group’s low-cost arm separately, the jump coincides with Australian arrivals departing from Melbourne more than doubling to 4,256 from 2,111, and those routed through Singapore and Kuala Lumpur falling 19.6 percent and 32.1 percent respectively. The passengers Jetstar has won appear to have come largely from Singapore Airlines and Malaysia Airlines, whose combined share of the market fell from 40 percent in July to 28.5 percent in September, equivalent to roughly 760 fewer passengers, based on Mirror Business calculations. However, SriLankan flew an estimated 4,720 Australian tourists in September, only marginally above 4,610 in July, despite raising its Colombo-Melbourne service from seven to 10 weekly flights from 2 August.  Its share of Australian arrivals consequently slipped from 47.55 percent to 43.11 percent, well below the 55.83 percent it held in September last year, when it carried around 5,080 Australians. Australians visiting for pleasure rose by about 1,210 between July and September, accounting for nearly all of the 1,250 increase in arrivals, while those visiting friends and relatives held steady at around 3,300, based on SLTDA data.  Although SLTDA does not break this down by airline, the pattern suggests Jetstar is bringing in leisure travellers, whereas SriLankan’s Australian traffic appears anchored in diaspora visits, which made up over a third of the market before Jetstar’s launch. SriLankan itself has cited Melbourne’s large Sri Lankan community among the reasons for its success on the route. Australian arrivals rose 20.3 percent in September when compared to the same month last year, accelerating from 6.4 percent growth in July and lifting Australia above the United Kingdom to become the island’s third-largest source market for the month. As reported earlier by Mirror Business, Jetstar Executive Manager Commercial Scott Zeglin noted that the thrice-weekly flights were running over 90 percent full in each direction, though he remained cautious on adding peak-season frequencies. Jetstar’s gains come as the Sri Lanka Tourism Promotion Bureau (SLTPB) runs a Rs.1.5 billion interim digital and public relations campaign through April, with Australia leading a six-month push on Meta, TikTok and YouTube, backed by a trade roadshow across Australia and New Zealand that concluded in Perth. However, according to industry sources, SriLankan has offered very little collaboration in supporting the country’s tourism promotion. Meanwhile, SriLankan Airlines Chief Executive Officer Vipul Misra told the media last week that the national carrier is studying a direct route to Perth, citing demand identified during a recent roadshow held jointly with the Tourism Ministry. “We see there is a strong demand in Perth,” he noted, adding that aircraft would have to be sourced from outside to deploy the capacity. Misra argued that the national carrier must take on routes that private airlines would deem commercially unattractive at the outset. “Nobody would bleed their money to open that route,” he observed. A Perth service would add a third Australian gateway alongside Melbourne and Sydney, tapping travellers who currently connect via Singapore, Kuala Lumpur or the Gulf. (NF)

audit.headline: Sri Lanka needs ‘hero’ luxury resort to reset market perception: Bawa Trust chief
audit.summary: Soneva and One&Only cited as projects that reshaped global perceptions of the Maldives Calls for sharper destination branding and a rethink of setback rules in building bylaws Bawa’s essential-only design, born of a weak economy, held up as a low-cost model for resort developers By Nishel Fernando Channa Daswatte Sri Lanka needs at least one ‘hero’ luxury resort of the kind that transformed global perceptions of the Maldives, along with sharper destination branding, to capitalise on a uniqueness that is its best asset, according to Geoffrey Bawa Trust Chairperson and MICD Associates Co-Founder Channa Daswatte. audit.body: Soneva and One&Only cited as projects that reshaped global perceptions of the Maldives Calls for sharper destination branding and a rethink of setback rules in building bylaws Bawa’s essential-only design, born of a weak economy, held up as a low-cost model for resort developers By Nishel Fernando  Channa Daswatte Sri Lanka needs at least one ‘hero’ luxury resort of the kind that transformed global perceptions of the Maldives, along with sharper destination branding, to capitalise on a uniqueness that is its best asset, according to Geoffrey Bawa Trust Chairperson and MICD Associates Co-Founder Channa Daswatte.  In conversation with Hotelivate-Savills Chief Strategy Officer Uttam Davé, Daswatte recently pointed to Soneva in the Maldives and the One&Only brand built under Sol Kerzner as projects whose influence reached well beyond their own islands.  “I think if there are some hero projects like resorts, luxury resorts, I think the way Soneva did in Maldives and the way Sol Kerzner did One&Only, it changed the perception of the market,” he observed. Soneva Fushi opened in 1995 as the Maldives’ first ‘castaway’ resort and pioneered back-to-nature luxury, while One&Only Reethi Rah, which opened in 2005, set the benchmark for the luxury resorts that followed. “Just one of those super luxury hero resorts changed the perception of the market,” Daswatte added, arguing that Sri Lanka already possesses the raw ingredients in its landscapes, people and food. “I think uniqueness is our best asset,” he remarked. Tourism earnings of US$ 3.2 billion in 2025 remained about 27 percent below the 2018 peak of US$ 4,381 million, even though arrivals last year surpassed 2018 levels. Earnings per tourist have consequently fallen from close to US$ 1,880 to roughly US$ 1,360, underlining the yield problem facing the industry. However, Daswatte did not regard regulation as a serious impediment, noting that much of Sri Lanka’s building bylaws are clear. He questioned whether setback requirements were excessive and left too little usable space, conceding that there was “definitely room for improvement there in terms of redefining the bylaws.” The larger gap, he argued, lay in how the country presents itself. “What I do see needs to be done to make the experience better is that there needs to be a little more destination branding,” he stressed. Daswatte traced the simplicity that defines Bawa’s work to the constraints of the economy in which he practiced.  “We had a really bad economy. So Bawa had the economy on his side,” he pointed out, explaining that Bawa felt no obligation to build anything beyond what was essential. Rather than ordering furniture from the latest catalogue, Bawa would design a chair himself using the simplest materials available, an approach that Daswatte noted cost practically nothing in the end. The same reliance on simple, basic and essential elements is what clients still associate with his own practice today, he added, adopted not as a stylistic choice but because it was appropriate. That thinking also shaped the Kandalama Hotel, which surprised many by carrying none of the traditional columns or decorative elements expected of an architect who was by then known, much to his dislike, as a vernacular architect. Daswatte recalled Bawa explaining to one of the directors that the whole place was scaled around looking at the horizon. Guests who spent their days amid 2,000 years of history and architecture, Bawa reasoned, should not return at night to be bombarded by yet more decoration. For Bawa, Daswatte explained, a hotel was a refuge for people arriving from completely stressed-out environments. Developers who keep guests sealed indoors, he cautioned, deny them the very place they have travelled to experience, leaving them “inside an air conditioning box looking at a view on the wall.” Good architecture, he maintained, should open up, close in and let the breeze through, so that guests experience the location they have chosen. Daswatte also warned against lifting a design element from one place and dropping it into another, insisting that context must lead. In taking Bawa’s legacy to a house he designed in Dubai, he retained ideas such as courtyards and interconnected spaces while responding to an entirely different environment and climate. Asked which principles he would embed in a resort built today, Daswatte said the core of the concept should draw on the country’s own history, while guests should always retain the option of peace and a holiday in nature. He noted that buildings Bawa designed some 50 years ago are now being restored, urging the industry to look after them. Bawa’s work has meanwhile drawn renewed international attention, with the Vitra Design Museum in Germany opening the first major retrospective of his work in two decades on 26 September, ahead of a run at M+ in Hong Kong from June 2027.

audit.headline: Indian Arrested at BIA with Rs. 51 Mn Worth of Kush
audit.summary: COLOMBO (News 1st); A major narcotics smuggling attempt was thwarted at the Bandaranaike International Airport in Katunayake after customs officials arrested an Indian national carrying a large consignment of Kush with an estimated street value of nearly Rs. 51 million. According to Customs, the suspect was taken into custody in the early hours of today after arriving in Sri Lanka on a Vietnam Airlines flight. The drugs were discovered during an inspection of the passenger's luggage, leading officers to uncover a significant quantity of Kush concealed among his belongings. Authorities said the seized stock weighed approximately 5 kilograms and 100 grams. The suspect, along with the seized drugs, has been handed over to the Police Narcotics Bureau for further investigations.

audit.headline: Venezuelan opposition leader María Machado returns after months in exile
audit.summary: Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado has returned home to a fraught political landscape after more than 10 months in exile. “I am here. With you,” Machado wrote on X on Sunday. Her return comes after repeated prior efforts to re-enter the country came to no avail. In January, a month after Machado left Venezuela on a speedboat under cover of darkness to accept the Nobel Peace Prize in Norway, the US seized her opponent, President Nicolás Maduro. The Trump administration then backed his deputy, Delcy Rodríguez, as leader and she was sworn in as interim president, later signing an oil deal which granted very favourable terms to the US. Machado was photographed on Sunday attending Mass at a church in the Venezuelan state of Lara, surrounded by supporters hugging her and clasping her hands. She then began travelling to the capital Caracas in a caravan of cheering supporters.
audit.body: Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado has returned home to a fraught political landscape after more than 10 months in exile. “I am here. With you,” Machado wrote on X on Sunday. Her return comes after repeated prior efforts to re-enter the country came to no avail. In January, a month after Machado left Venezuela on a speedboat under cover of darkness to accept the Nobel Peace Prize in Norway, the US seized her opponent, President Nicolás Maduro. The Trump administration then backed his deputy, Delcy Rodríguez, as leader and she was sworn in as interim president, later signing an oil deal which granted very favourable terms to the US. Machado was photographed on Sunday attending Mass at a church in the Venezuelan state of Lara, surrounded by supporters hugging her and clasping her hands. She then began travelling to the capital Caracas in a caravan of cheering supporters. More supporters have lined the route of her journey to the capital. She was photographed smiling as she leaned out of the sunroof of a car as she entered Caracas late on Sunday night. “Night of reunion in our Caracas. For the reunion of each family, for the Freedom of each political prisoner, for the Freedom of Venezuela,” she wrote on X. Her ally, former presidential candidate Edmundo González, confirmed her arrival, writing in a statement: “I am thrilled to announce to you that our leader, my dear María Corina, is on Venezuelan soil.” “Today is a very important day for Venezuelans. Our sovereign voice returns with her to lead and guide this process!” González said. He added that he will soon join Machado in Venezuela to advance the country “toward freedom”. An advisor to Machado said in September that over the previous few weeks Machado had attempted seven times to return to Venezuela, but was denied each time. There have been reports that the US was involved in delaying her return, which it has denied. It’s unclear what Machado plans to do next now that she’s back, but she has previously said she would run for president again if an election were held . Her ability to return to her country was always contingent on approval from the Trump administration, which it appears has now been granted. A staunch supporter of democracy, Machado won an independent presidential primary election – held outside the Maduro government’s official election authority – in 2023, earning more than 90% of the vote. Despite winning the primary, Maduro’s government barred Machado from running for office, accusing her of fraud and tax violations. Machado denied the allegations, calling them politically motivated. She spent her final days in the country hiding in safehouses before her fleeing to Norway to accept the Nobel Prize. In the 2024 election, Machado’s ally González ran in her place against Maduro. The electoral authority, which is closely aligned with the government, declared Maduro the winner without making detailed voting tallies public. The opposition argued that González won the election, not Maduro, uploading copies of the voting tallies as evidence. Maduro was removed from the country by US forces in January, and is currently jailed in New York where he faces drugs, weapons and torture charges. He has pleaded not guilty. A spokesman for Machado called her return “a major step toward a democratic transition and free, fair, and verifiable presidential elections in the near future”. “We thank President Donald Trump, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, the US Government, Congress, and allied governments for their continued leadership and support,” her spokesperson, David Smolansky, added. Speaking to reporters on Sunday, Trump said, “I don’t know anything about” her return, and added that he hoped she was “safe”. “I think she’s a very nice woman. She gave me her Nobel Prize, so how can I say anything else? And I hope she’s safe,” he said. In January, Machado visited the White House and gifted her Nobel prize award to Trump . The committee that issues the prize had said “it cannot be revoked, shared, or transferred to others”. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio praised his country’s role in securing her return through political reconciliation talks. “The conditions allowing for the safe return of Ms Machado to Venezuela is the direct result of the US supported reconciliation talks which has already seen hundreds of political prisoners freed and hundreds of political opposition figures return from exile,” he posted on X. He added: “We expect all political actors to support these talks which represent the best chance Venezuela has had in thirty years to peacefully achieve not just a free and fair election but an enduring democracy.” BBC

audit.headline: Sri Lanka Earns US$13.6 Bn in Exports in Just Nine Months
audit.summary: COLOMBO (News 1st); Sri Lanka’s export sector continued its upward trajectory in 2026, with total exports reaching US$13.61 billion during the first nine months of the year, marking a 5.04% increase compared to the corresponding period in 2025. The performance reflects steady growth across both merchandise and services exports, highlighting the resilience of the country's export industry despite challenging global market conditions. According to the latest export performance figures released by Sri Lanka Customs, together with estimates from the Export Development Board (EDB) for gems and jewellery and petroleum products, merchandise exports grew by 5.35% to US$10.76 billion, while services exports increased by 3.88% to US$2.85 billion during the January-September period.
audit.body: COLOMBO (News 1st); Sri Lanka’s export sector continued its upward trajectory in 2026, with total exports reaching US$13.61 billion during the first nine months of the year, marking a 5.04% increase compared to the corresponding period in 2025. The performance reflects steady growth across both merchandise and services exports, highlighting the resilience of the country's export industry despite challenging global market conditions. According to the latest export performance figures released by Sri Lanka Customs, together with estimates from the Export Development Board (EDB) for gems and jewellery and petroleum products, merchandise exports grew by 5.35% to US$10.76 billion, while services exports increased by 3.88% to US$2.85 billion during the January-September period. The strongest momentum came in September, when Sri Lanka recorded total exports of US$1.69 billion, representing a 17.23% year-on-year increase from September 2025. Merchandise exports drove much of that growth, rising 21.66% to US$1.39 billion, while services exports edged up 0.67% to US$306.17 million. Among the best-performing sectors in September were Electrical and Electronic Components, which surged 88.35%, Spices, Essential Oils and Oleoresins, which rose 73.19%, and Rubber and Rubber-Based Products, which increased 33.68%. Food and beverage exports also posted strong growth of 27.92%, reflecting continued international demand for Sri Lankan products. Pepper exports more than doubled, recording a remarkable 165.38% increase, while cinnamon exports climbed 68.27%, reinforcing Sri Lanka's position as a major supplier of premium spices to global markets. However, not all sectors recorded growth. Tea export earnings fell 1.38% in September, largely due to weaker demand from key Middle Eastern markets, including the United Arab Emirates, Iran and Iraq. Coconut-based products also recorded a decline of 8.88%, while ornamental fish exports dropped 35.15% during the month. The United States remained Sri Lanka's largest export destination, accounting for more than 20% of merchandise exports and recording an 18.06% increase in September. India strengthened its position as the country's second-largest export market, overtaking the United Kingdom, with exports to India increasing 29.65% in September and 12.3% during the first nine months of the year. Turkey emerged as one of the fastest-growing export destinations, with shipments increasing 64.22% in September and 94.01% during the January-September period. Exports to China also posted healthy growth, supported by strong demand for activated carbon and other value-added products.

audit.headline: Police Launch Investigation into Alleged Inciting Remarks by Balangoda Kassapa Thera
audit.summary: The Cinnamon Gardens Police has informed the Colombo Chief Magistrate's Court that an investigation has been launched into statements allegedly made by Venerable Balangoda Kassapa Thera during the Satyagraha held at Viharamahadevi Park, which are alleged to have incited the public and misled people. Police stated that the investigation was initiated following a complaint lodged by the headquarters of the National People's Power. A group including Venerable Balangoda Kassapa Thera staged a Satyagraha at Viharamahadevi Park in Colombo over the past several days, demanding the immediate release of Venerable Galagoda Aththe Gnanasara Thera, who is currently serving a prison sentence for contempt of court.
audit.body: The Cinnamon Gardens Police has informed the Colombo Chief Magistrate's Court that an investigation has been launched into statements allegedly made by Venerable Balangoda Kassapa Thera during the Satyagraha held at Viharamahadevi Park, which are alleged to have incited the public and misled people. Police stated that the investigation was initiated following a complaint lodged by the headquarters of the National People's Power. A group including Venerable Balangoda Kassapa Thera staged a Satyagraha at Viharamahadevi Park in Colombo over the past several days, demanding the immediate release of Venerable Galagoda Aththe Gnanasara Thera, who is currently serving a prison sentence for contempt of court. The Cinnamon Gardens Police informed court today that Jagath Basnayake, an organiser attached to the headquarters of the National People's Power (NPP), had lodged a complaint alleging that Venerable Balangoda Kassapa Thera had made false statements to the media during the protest that were capable of inciting the public, misleading people and undermining public confidence. Police further told Colombo Chief Magistrate Asanga S. Bodaragama that a statement made by Venerable Balangoda Kassapa Thera to the media on the 22nd of October, regarding two individuals who had allegedly arrived at Viharamahadevi Park carrying two knives, was entirely false and misleading. Police submitted that the dissemination of false statements constitutes a violation of Section 98 of the Police Ordinance and informed court that an investigation had been commenced into the remarks. Police also requested the court to direct media institutions to provide unedited footage relating to the statements. After considering the facts presented, the Magistrate ordered media institutions to provide the police with the unedited footage relating to the statement in question and further directed police to promptly report the progress of the investigation to the court.

audit.headline: Koggala Train-Bus Collision: Driver and Assistant Remanded Until November 4
audit.summary: COLOMBO (News 1st) – The bus driver and assistant arrested in connection with the collision between a bus and a train at the Koggala railway crossing yesterday, have been remanded until November 4. The two suspects were remanded after being produced before the Galle Additional Magistrate today. Police stated that six people injured in the accident are still receiving treatment in hospital. The accident occurred yesterday when a bus collided with a train at the Koggala railway crossing, injuring 13 children. The injured were among a group of students aged between 14 and 15 who were returning from a visit to the Martin Wickramasinghe Folk Museum in Koggala. The group had travelled from Kottawa, on an excursion. According to police, the bus crossed the railway line despite the railway warning signals being activated.

The accident occurred yesterday when a bus collided with a train at the Koggala railway crossing, injuring 13 children. The injured were among a group of students aged between 14 and 15 who were returning from a visit to the Martin Wickramasinghe Folk Museum in Koggala. The group had travelled from Kottawa, on an excursion. According to police, the bus crossed the railway line despite the railway warning signals being activated. Meanwhile, residents have raised concerns about the safety of the railway crossing, describing it as a hazardous location. They said that although warning signals are in place, the absence of a railway gate allows some drivers to cross without taking adequate precautions, putting road users at risk.

audit.headline: Cargills Bank introduces Sri Lanka’s first ocean plastic debit card
audit.summary: - Initiative to support marine conservation Cargills Bank has launched the Cargills Bank Ocean Plastic Debit Card, marking the first time such a product has been introduced to the Sri Lankan market. This initiative is a key part of the bank’s commitment to sustainable banking and serves as a practical step toward addressing the global challenge of marine pollution. The cards are produced using recycled ocean-bound plastic specifically sourced from the Indian Ocean region, including the Maldives, as well as the Dominican Republic. By transitioning to these recycled materials, Cargills Bank aims to raise meaningful awareness about the impact of plastic waste on our oceans while supporting the protection of coastal ecosystems.
audit.body: - Initiative to support marine conservation Cargills Bank has launched the Cargills Bank Ocean Plastic Debit Card, marking the first time such a product has been introduced to the Sri Lankan market. This initiative is a key part of the bank’s commitment to sustainable banking and serves as a practical step toward addressing the global challenge of marine pollution. The cards are produced using recycled ocean-bound plastic specifically sourced from the Indian Ocean region, including the Maldives, as well as the Dominican Republic. By transitioning to these recycled materials, Cargills Bank aims to raise meaningful awareness about the impact of plastic waste on our oceans while supporting the protection of coastal ecosystems.
