In the money market, the net liquidity surplus stood at Rs. 107.77 billion yesterday. Of this, Rs. 76.64 billion was deposited with the Central Bank through its Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) at 8.25%, while Rs. 0.61 billion was withdrawn through the Standing Lending Facility (SLF) at 9.25%. Meanwhile, the Domestic Operations Department (DOD) of the Central Bank absorbed further liquidity through an overnight repo auction, mopping up Rs. 31.75 billion at weighted average rate of 8.75%. The weighted average rates on overnight call money and repos were 9.02% and 9.07% respectively. Forex market The USD/LKR rate on spot contracts was seen closing the day depreciating to Rs. 332.25/332.40, as against its previous day’s close of Rs. 332.10/332.20. The total USD/LKR traded volume on 23 October was $ 110.25 million. (References: Public Debt Management Office - Ministry of Finance, Central Bank of Sri Lanka, Bloomberg E-Bond Trading Platform, Money Broking Companies)

audit.headline: CSE starts week in red, down 0.23%
audit.summary: The Colombo stock market yesterday opened the week in red, extending losses into a sixth consecutive session. The ASPI was down 0.23% or 44.35 points at 19,640.56 and the active S&P SL20 fell 0.21% or 11.76 points to 5,601.87. Market turnover was nearly Rs. 666.3 million on 29.7 million shares traded. Foreign investors were net sellers on a net outflow of Rs. 6.6 million. With 123 counters ending in red against 80 gainers, the top contributors to the ASPI decline were CARS, COMB, LAMB, DIST and HAYL. First Capital Research said the bourse opened on a positive note but failed to sustain its early momentum, with continued fluctuations throughout the first half of the session before ultimately closing in negative territory. HNW participation remained subdued, while retail participation was relatively higher, driven by margin selling.
audit.body: The Colombo stock market yesterday opened the week in red, extending losses into a sixth consecutive session. The ASPI was down 0.23% or 44.35 points at 19,640.56 and the active S&P SL20 fell 0.21% or 11.76 points to 5,601.87. Market turnover was nearly Rs. 666.3 million on 29.7 million shares traded. Foreign investors were net sellers on a net outflow of Rs. 6.6 million. With 123 counters ending in red against 80 gainers, the top contributors to the ASPI decline were CARS, COMB, LAMB, DIST and HAYL. First Capital Research said the bourse opened on a positive note but failed to sustain its early momentum, with continued fluctuations throughout the first half of the session before ultimately closing in negative territory. HNW participation remained subdued, while retail participation was relatively higher, driven by margin selling. The banking sector led the daily turnover with a share of 28%, followed by the capital goods, and diversified financials sectors collectively contributing 35%. NDB Securities said high net worth and institutional investor participation was noted in Access Engineering, Commercial Bank and John Keells Holdings. Mixed interest was observed in Sampath Bank, Panasian Power and Hayleys whilst retail interest was noted in Waskaduwa Beach Resort, Muller and Phipps and SMB Leasing. Foreign participation in the market activity remained at subdued levels with foreigners closing as net sellers. The banking sector was the top contributor to the market turnover due to Commercial Bank and Sampath Bank whilst the sector index edged up by 0.09%. The share price of Commercial Bank decreased by 75 cents to close at Rs. 195.25 and Sampath Bank ended flat at Rs. 138.50. The capital goods sector was the second highest contributor to the market turnover due to Access Engineering and John Keells Holdings whilst the sector index edged up by 0.11%. Access Engineering ended down 20 cents to Rs. 74.50 and John Keells Holdings gained 10 cents to Rs. 17.70. Panasian Power was also included amongst the top turnover contributors. The share price of Panasian Power fell 10 cents to close at Rs. 10.

audit.headline: OPA presents collective professional proposals for Budget 2027
audit.summary: The Organisation of Professional Associations of Sri Lanka (OPA), under the leadership of OPA President Jayantha Gallehewa, presented its proposals and recommendations for the Budget 2027 to Treasury Secretary Dr. Harshana Suriyapperuma at a meeting held on 6 October, 2026. The proposals represent the collective voice and professional expertise of the OPA’s 52 member associations, bringing together knowledge and perspectives from across Sri Lanka’s professional community. The initiative was undertaken through the National Issues Committee (NIC), chaired by OPA Vice President and NIC Chairman Bhanu Wijayaratne, with the active contribution of its members.
audit.body: The Organisation of Professional Associations of Sri Lanka (OPA), under the leadership of OPA President Jayantha Gallehewa, presented its proposals and recommendations for the Budget 2027 to Treasury Secretary Dr. Harshana Suriyapperuma at a meeting held on 6 October, 2026. The proposals represent the collective voice and professional expertise of the OPA’s 52 member associations, bringing together knowledge and perspectives from across Sri Lanka’s professional community. The initiative was undertaken through the National Issues Committee (NIC), chaired by OPA Vice President and NIC Chairman Bhanu Wijayaratne, with the active contribution of its members. The proposals were developed through consultations with the OPA’s member associations and focused on key areas of national importance, with the objective of providing constructive and evidence-informed recommendations to the national Budget process. Among the key areas addressed were fair taxation, export financing, elder care and social protection, research and innovation, the circular economy, the built environment and heritage, and measures to address the country’s professional brain drain. The proposals also reflected wider professional perspectives on strengthening economic resilience, improving productivity, encouraging investment and supporting sustainable national development. The OPA delegation was led by OPA President Jayantha Gallehewa and included General Secretary Eng. Ravi Rupasinghe, Vice President and NIC Chairman Bhanu Wijayaratne, NIC Member B.A.H.S. Preena, OPA Assistant Secretary Indika Ranaweera, Vice President and Career Guidance and Skills Development Committee Chairman V. Rameshkumar, NIC Member and Career Guidance and Skills Development Committee Convener Udesh I.W. Seneviratna and OPA Editor Priyantha Wickramarathna. Speaking on the occasion, Gallehewa emphasised the organisation’s commitment to placing the knowledge, experience and collective expertise of Sri Lanka’s professional community at the service of the nation. He noted that the OPA’s role extends beyond representing individual professions and includes contributing constructively to national policy and decision-making. The presentation of the Budget proposals marks another important step in the OPA’s continuing engagement with the Government. Through the NIC and its 52 member associations, the OPA continues to provide a platform for translating professional knowledge and experience into practical recommendations on matters of national importance. The OPA expressed its appreciation to the Finance, Planning and Economic Development Ministry for providing the opportunity to present its proposals and reaffirmed its readiness to continue contributing professional expertise to the national development and Budget process.

audit.headline: Sumathi Holdings celebrates 70 years of success
audit.summary: - From a single betting shop on Maliban Street in 1956 to 11 principal businesses and over 2,000 people Sumathi Holdings marked its 70th anniversary on 9 October, with a celebration at the Sangam Ballroom of ITC Ratnadipa, Colombo, attended by over 500 guests from Sri Lanka’s business, government, financial and media communities. Held under the theme “70 Years of Sumathi Legacy”, the evening looked back to 1956, when founder Mr. U.W. Sumathipala opened Sporting Star’s first betting shop on Maliban Street, Pettah – the business from which the Group grew. The evening opened with a drone show and fireworks over Galle Face.
audit.body: - From a single betting shop on Maliban Street in 1956 to 11 principal businesses and over 2,000 people Sumathi Holdings marked its 70th anniversary on 9 October, with a celebration at the Sangam Ballroom of ITC Ratnadipa, Colombo, attended by over 500 guests from Sri Lanka’s business, government, financial and media communities. Held under the theme “70 Years of Sumathi Legacy”, the evening looked back to 1956, when founder Mr. U.W. Sumathipala opened Sporting Star’s first betting shop on Maliban Street, Pettah – the business from which the Group grew. The evening opened with a drone show and fireworks over Galle Face. The program that followed included an address and toast by Chairman Jagath Sumathipala, the unveiling of the 70th anniversary logo, and addresses by Directors Chadu Sumathipala and Chathula Sumathipala, accompanied by a live orchestra and performances by vocalist Umara Sinhawansa, pianist and music director Soundarie David Rodrigo, and composer and singer Nadeeka Guruge. U.W. Sumathipala built Sporting Star into one of the country’s leading bookmakers and established it as the market leader. He also expanded into cinema, supporting the growth of the Sri Lankan film industry and into gems, representing the business at The World Gem and Jewellery Exhibition in Milan. His values of “Honesty and Integrity” remain the Group’s guiding principles today. After U.W. Sumathipala’s passing in 1979, Jagath Sumathipala joined the business at the age of 19, supported by his maternal uncle, Dharmasiri, who guided him in the horse racing operations. His first assignment was to create the Group’s own race paper, which he turned into a commercial printing company. He moved the main office from Maliban Street to Chatham Street and carried forward his father’s gem business. When his brother, Thilanga Sumathipala, returned from his studies in 1986, Jagath Sumathipala handed the racing operations over to him, and Thilanga Sumathipala built them further. In 1987 took a new step, Jagath Sumathipala opened Sri Lanka’s first race-by-race live commentary betting shop. Building on this, the Group began broadcasting races in 1992 and by 1998 was showing every race live across all its outlets. Today Sporting Star operates more than 200 outlets across the island and, since 2019, the online platform BetSS.com. Milina Sumathipala’s influence reached well beyond the business. She gave the entire profit of her film Ganga Addara (1980) to build a Neurosurgery Unit at the Colombo General Hospital, today’s National Hospital. In 1981, she began the blood donation drives and support for the Cancer Hospital through which more than 20,000 pints of blood have since been donated, and in 2001 she became the first woman President of the All Ceylon Buddhist Congress. Following a restructuring in 2017, Jagath Sumathipala, together with the third generation, has shaped Sumathi Holdings into a Group of 11 principal businesses employing more than 2,000 people, across betting and gaming, healthcare, information technology, restaurants, security, printing, renewable energy, investments and film. Much of today’s Group began as an answer to something Sporting Star needed. Security for its outlets became Lokx Security Services; printing for its racing papers became InPrint Solutions; and the technology behind its betting systems is now developed by Mainframe. Three Group companies mark milestones of their own this year: Great Wall Restaurants turns 35. Jagath Sumathipala set it up in 1991 on Chatham Street to bring authentic Chinese food to Colombo. Sumathi IT turns 25. It provides network infrastructure, data communications and geospatial engineering across Sri Lanka, and introduced DJI’s enterprise drones to the country. LifeServ turns 25. The healthcare distributor has been a leader in Sri Lanka’s drug-eluting stent market for two decades and opened an oncology division in 2025. A third generation now leads the Group alongside the Chairman. Chadu Sumathipala leads the Group’s IT sector: he founded Mainframe, brought the Group’s key systems in-house, built BetSS.com, and set up Sumathi IT’s drone division and its first research and development centre. Chathula Sumathipala leads the Group’s services cluster and grew LifeServ built Sumathi Energy, whose projects include the 5MW Wewila solar plant and battery storage at Monaragala and Wewila. The celebrations extended to the Group’s people. On 8 October, Sporting Star’s head office celebrated with its staff and presented long-service awards to more than 200 employees with ten or more years’ service, 31 of whom have been with the company for over 30 years. The longest-serving, R.V. Ghanasena of Anuradhapura, has been with Sporting Star for 40 years. On 10 October, Sporting Star outlets across the island held celebrations of their own for staff from Great Wall Restaurants and commemorative gifts for customers. Sumathi Holdings Chairman Jagath Sumathipala said: “Seventy years ago, my father opened a single shop on Maliban Street, built on his word and the trust of his customers. Honesty and integrity built this Group, and the more than 2,000 people who stand with us today carry those values forward. As we enter our eighth decade, our commitment is to build the businesses that will serve Sri Lanka for the next seventy years.”

audit.headline: Supreme Court enters decisive judgement in relation to jurisdiction of Commercial High Court
audit.summary: A bench of the Supreme Court comprising Justices Mahinda Samayawardhena, Dr. Sobhitha Rajakaruna, and K.M.G.H. Kulatunga delivered judgement overturning an order of the Commercial High Court on 21 October, by which the Commercial High Court had dismissed an action at the pre-trial stage on the basis that there was insufficient evidence to establish the claim to satisfy the minimum monetary threshold of the Commercial High Court to hear a case. According to the order of the Commercial High Court which was challenged, the position taken up by the Defendant that the Plaintiff’s claim had been artificially inflated to meet the jurisdictional threshold of the Commercial High Court was upheld by the Commercial High Court also with a finding that there was no evidence placed to support the claim.
audit.body: A bench of the Supreme Court comprising Justices Mahinda Samayawardhena, Dr. Sobhitha Rajakaruna, and K.M.G.H. Kulatunga delivered judgement overturning an order of the Commercial High Court on 21 October, by which the Commercial High Court had dismissed an action at the pre-trial stage on the basis that there was insufficient evidence to establish the claim to satisfy the minimum monetary threshold of the Commercial High Court to hear a case. According to the order of the Commercial High Court which was challenged, the position taken up by the Defendant that the Plaintiff’s claim had been artificially inflated to meet the jurisdictional threshold of the Commercial High Court was upheld by the Commercial High Court also with a finding that there was no evidence placed to support the claim. The Defendant in the case had initially raised a jurisdictional objection on the basis that the dispute was not a commercial dispute as there was no written contract or agreement between the parties. However, at the pre-trial stage, the Defendant had altered its objection and contended that the monetary threshold had not been met. Having considered the objections raised by the Defendant, the Commercial High Court dismissed the Plaintiff’s entire case in 2024. The Plaintiff-Appellant, Kish International Ltd., thereafter preferred an appeal to the Supreme Court, contending that the transaction between the parties was intended to be in USD and that, cumulatively, the sums claimed in the Plaint including demurrage, loss of profits, and interest exceeded the statutory threshold required to file the case in the Commercial High Court as demonstrated in the Plaint. It was the Plaintiff-Appellant’s position that the Commercial High Court could not lawfully dismiss the action at the pre-trial stage on the ground of an alleged lack of evidence as the pre-trial hearing is not the stage at which evidence is led or evaluated. The Appellant further contended that the High Court Judge ought not to have permitted the Defendant to reformulate a jurisdictional objection that had not been pleaded in the original defence. Justice Samayawardhena, in the judgement of the Supreme Court, specifically addressed, inter alia, the role of the pre-trial conference, which constitutes a pivotal stage in civil proceedings: “The purpose of the pre-trial conference is not to provide an opportunity for a party to introduce a new case outside the scope of the pleadings, to expand the scope of the dispute, or to prepare the case for a full-fledged trial.” The Supreme Court further held that “jurisdiction cannot ordinarily remain in suspense throughout the proceedings and ultimately depend upon the result of the very adjudication which the Court assumed jurisdiction to undertake. If jurisdiction is properly attached when the action was instituted, a subsequent finding on the merits that the Plaintiff has proved an amount less than that claimed does not, for that reason, retrospectively divest the Court of jurisdiction.” In addition, the Supreme Court, in its judgment, held that Parliament had used the word ‘including’, which should be given a wider interpretation, encompassing ‘commercial transactions’, and providing guidance as to the nature and breadth of the transactions that Parliament intended to bring within the jurisdiction of the Commercial High Court. It was held that the expression ‘commercial transactions’ must be given a broad and purposive interpretation, rather than being confined to the particular categories expressly enumerated in item 1 of the enacting act. The Supreme Court observed in its judgement that the Commercial High Court Judge had required the Plaintiff, at the pre-trial stage and before the action had even been fixed for trial, to establish by evidence the several components of its claim which the Supreme Court contended was a matter for determination upon the evidence at the trial. It was held that the absence of evidence establishing a particular component of the claim at the pre-trial stage could not justify the conclusion that such amount should be excluded in determining the pecuniary jurisdiction of the Court. The Supreme Court through this extensive judgement proceeded to set aside the impugned order of the Commercial High Court and awarded costs against the Defendant-Respondent in respect of both the proceedings before the Commercial High Court until the dismissal and the Supreme Court appeal. The Supreme Court further directed the Commercial High Court to proceed with the matter and to hear and conclude the case expeditiously. On behalf of the Plaintiff-Appellant, Kish International Ltd., Counsel Nishan Premathiratne appeared with Vikum Jayasinghe and Manith Dasanayake on the instructions of Gamindu Karunasena. The Commercial High Court was firstly established in 1996 by an Act of Parliament and it is presently holden in the Western Province to hear and determine disputes of a commercial nature above Rs. 50 million, including matters relating to intellectual property, admiralty, debt recovery and arbitral referrals.

audit.headline: Sajith discusses proposed anti-terrorism, organised crime laws with diplomatic corps
audit.summary: Opposition Leader Sajith Premadasa has met representatives of diplomatic missions and international organisations in Colombo to discuss concerns over proposed legislation targeting terrorism and organised crime. According to a statement issued by the Opposition Leader's office on 25 October, the discussions focused on the proposed Protection of the State from Terrorism Bill and the Prevention of Organised Crimes Bill, with particular attention to their potential impact on fundamental rights, judicial independence and constitutional protections. Former parliamentarian M.A. Sumanthiran, along with serving and former lawmakers, also expressed concerns about the proposed laws during the meeting.
audit.body: Opposition Leader Sajith Premadasa has met representatives of diplomatic missions and international organisations in Colombo to discuss concerns over proposed legislation targeting terrorism and organised crime. According to a statement issued by the Opposition Leader's office on 25 October, the discussions focused on the proposed Protection of the State from Terrorism Bill and the Prevention of Organised Crimes Bill, with particular attention to their potential impact on fundamental rights, judicial independence and constitutional protections. Former parliamentarian M.A. Sumanthiran, along with serving and former lawmakers, also expressed concerns about the proposed laws during the meeting. Premadasa said legislation to combat terrorism and organised crime was necessary, but stressed that such measures must be accompanied by effective judicial oversight and safeguards to prevent the misuse of executive powers. The discussions also addressed objections raised by the Human Rights Commission of Sri Lanka (HRCSL), which warned in a statement issued on 21 October that the proposed Prevention of Organised Crimes Bill was “wholly incompatible” with the fundamental rights provisions of the Constitution and the country’s international human rights obligations. The Commission cautioned that the proposed law could be more draconian than the Prevention of Terrorism Act of 1979 and called for its withdrawal and substantial revision. Key areas of concern included; provisions permitting confessions to senior Police officers, detention authorised by the executive, broad definitions of serious offences and limitations on judicial discretion in decisions concerning remand and bail. The HRCSL has separately called for revisions to the proposed terrorism legislation, urging the authorities to adopt a narrower definition of terrorism, ensure judicial supervision of detention orders, guarantee access to legal representation and strengthen safeguards governing bail. The Bar Association of Sri Lanka (BASL) has also called for the withdrawal of the proposed organised crime legislation and the withdrawal or amendment of the terrorism Bill in its current form. Premadasa urged the Government to make the recommendations of expert committees’ public and conduct broader consultations with the HRCSL, the BASL and other relevant stakeholders before proceeding with the legislation. He said constitutional safeguards were important not only for politicians and activists, but also for ordinary citizens who might come into contact with the criminal justice system.

audit.headline: UNP demands immediate presidential pardon for Gnanasara Thera
audit.summary: The United National Party (UNP) yesterday demanded an immediate presidential pardon for Ven. Galagodaaththe Gnanasara Thera, facilitated by the intervention of the Maha Nayake Theros of the Three Chapters, to resolve the ongoing crisis. In a statement, the party said the Sathyagraha, a non-violent sit-in protest, demanding the Thera’s release had been suspended following a notification by the Maha Nayake Theros. Citing former Chief Justice Sarath N. Silva, the UNP said the maximum prison sentence for contempt of court was 18 months, and that Gnanasara Thera had already served more than 10 months in prison for the offence. The party said steps had previously been taken to secure a presidential pardon for the Thera at the request of the Maha Nayake Theros, and claimed that the Supreme Court ruling had indicated another presidential pardon could be considered.

It further called for an investigation into those responsible for ordering the removal of the Thera’s robes.

audit.headline: Japan pledges over Rs. 600 m for Kelani River water quality project
audit.summary: Japan has pledged over Rs. 600 million for a five-year project to monitor and improve water quality in the Kelani River basin, with the first consignment of water testing equipment handed over to Environment Minister Dr. Dammika Patabendi yesterday. Implemented through the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) and the Japan Science and Technology Agency (JST) under the SATREPS program, the 2026-2030 project will set up a basin-wide monitoring network and an aquatic environment data platform to collect and analyse water quality information, supporting evidence-based Government policymaking. It will also develop policy frameworks, train personnel, engage technical experts and publish research findings. Japanese representatives handed over the equipment at a steering committee meeting at the Central Environmental Authority (CEA) auditorium.
audit.body: Japan has pledged over Rs. 600 million for a five-year project to monitor and improve water quality in the Kelani River basin, with the first consignment of water testing equipment handed over to Environment Minister Dr. Dammika Patabendi yesterday. Implemented through the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) and the Japan Science and Technology Agency (JST) under the SATREPS program, the 2026-2030 project will set up a basin-wide monitoring network and an aquatic environment data platform to collect and analyse water quality information, supporting evidence-based Government policymaking. It will also develop policy frameworks, train personnel, engage technical experts and publish research findings. Japanese representatives handed over the equipment at a steering committee meeting at the Central Environmental Authority (CEA) auditorium. It was then distributed among the CEA, the University of Moratuwa and General Sir John Kotelawala Defence University. The University of Moratuwa’s Aquatic Environment Data Operations Centre will play a key role in implementation. The 145 km Kelani River, with a basin of about 2,300 sq. km, is a major source of drinking water for Colombo and surrounding areas. Approximately one-fourth of Sri Lanka’s population lives in the basin, which has 14 major water treatment and distribution facilities and more than 5,400 industries, including CEA-authorised operations in the Biyagama and Seethawaka industrial zones. The river faces significant pollution from industrial wastewater, untreated sewage, agricultural waste, and sand and gem mining, while floods and droughts also affect water quality. There are no specific groundwater quality standards either, a concern as groundwater is a major source of drinking water for many Western Province households. Environment Ministry Secretary K.R. Uduwawala leads the steering committee, while Tohoku University Prof. So Kasama is principal investigator. The meeting was attended by JICA representatives, CEA Chairman Prof. Tilak Hewawasam, CEA Director General Kapila Rajapaksa, University of Moratuwa Department of Civil Engineering Prof. Lalith Rajapaksa, the Kaduwela Municipal Commissioner and Environment Ministry officials. The Department of Irrigation, the Water Resources Board and the Clean Sri Lanka Secretariat are also involved. The project aims to lay a scientific foundation for water quality management across the basin, with the goal of ensuring safer drinking water for the public by 2030.

audit.headline: Laugfs Gas weighs stake sale in Hambantota LPG terminal
audit.summary: Laugfs Gas PLC yesterday said it was in preliminary, informal discussions with interested parties on strategic options for its wholly owned subsidiary Laugfs Terminals Ltd., including the potential disposal of part or all of its shareholding. Laugfs Terminals owns and operates the 30,000 MT liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) terminal at the Hambantota International Port. The options under consideration include commercial collaboration, investment and a potential partial or full sale of the company’s stake in the subsidiary. No agreement has been reached on the structure or terms of any transaction, and no definitive transaction agreement has been entered into, the company said, adding that there was no certainty the discussions would result in a transaction. Accordingly, any financial impact could not be determined at this stage.

audit.headline: PDMO rejects all Domestic Dollar Bond bids; market says bid rates too high
audit.summary: - Turns down every bid at 23 Oct. auction for $ 100 m issue, which had option to raise up to $ 300 m - Notice cites only issuer’s right to accept or reject any application; no other details given The Public Debt Management Office (PDMO) has rejected all bids received at its Domestic Dollar Bond auction held on 23 October, with market sources indicating that demand was encouraging, but the rates bid were too high. The issue was for $ 100 million, with the option of raising up to $ 300 million. “Pursuant to Section 6 of the Offer Document, which reserves the Issuer’s right to accept or reject any application, in whole or in part, the Issuer has decided not to accept any bids received under this auction,” the PDMO said in its notice, giving no further details.
audit.body: - Turns down every bid at 23 Oct. auction for $ 100 m issue, which had option to raise up to $ 300 m - Notice cites only issuer’s right to accept or reject any application; no other details given The Public Debt Management Office (PDMO) has rejected all bids received at its Domestic Dollar Bond auction held on 23 October, with market sources indicating that demand was encouraging, but the rates bid were too high. The issue was for $ 100 million, with the option of raising up to $ 300 million. “Pursuant to Section 6 of the Offer Document, which reserves the Issuer’s right to accept or reject any application, in whole or in part, the Issuer has decided not to accept any bids received under this auction,” the PDMO said in its notice, giving no further details. The fixed rate of interest payable on the bonds, which are US dollar-denominated debt securities issued in the domestic market, was to be determined through competitive bidding. Market sources said the PDMO probably believed the bids did not factor in Fitch Ratings’ recent upgrade of Sri Lanka. In September, Fitch upgraded Sri Lanka’s Long-Term Issuer Default Rating to ‘B-’ from ‘CCC+’, with a Stable outlook. A higher rating typically lowers the risk premium investors demand over benchmark US Treasury yields, which together determine dollar bond pricing. Given the availability of funds and current global uncertainties, the PDMO may be willing to wait before returning to the market, the sources said. Accepting costlier bids could also have set a higher benchmark for future foreign currency borrowing. This was the second Domestic Dollar Bond issue since the debt crisis. In the first, in December 2025, the PDMO raised $ 50 million under a fixed-rate arrangement, recording firm demand for one- and two-year maturities. The one-year tranche drew $ 45.5 million in bids, of which $ 33 million was accepted at a weighted average fixed rate of 5.7%. The two-year tenor received $ 42.5 million in bids, with $ 17 million accepted at a weighted average rate of 6.1%. Only $ 1 million was bid for the three-year maturity, and no bids were accepted.

audit.headline: India says port expansions no zero-sum game for Colombo
audit.summary: - Indian maritime think tank head says MSC investing in both Colombo and Vizhinjam, India’s directly competing port - Says port connectivity, once a source of concern, is now ‘the most promising’ area for India-Sri Lanka maritime cooperation - Notes India’s SAGAR policy, Sagarmala port program were seen in some minds as pulling in opposite directions India’s drive to build its own transhipment hubs is not playing out at Colombo’s expense, a leading Indian maritime strategist said, pointing to global shipping lines now investing in ports on both sides of the Palk Strait. New Delhi-based National Maritime Foundation (NMF) Director General Vice Admiral Pradeep Chauhan said port connectivity, long a source of anxiety in Sri Lanka, had become the most promising area for maritime cooperation between the two countries.
audit.body: - Indian maritime think tank head says MSC investing in both Colombo and Vizhinjam, India’s directly competing port - Says port connectivity, once a source of concern, is now ‘the most promising’ area for India-Sri Lanka maritime cooperation - Notes India’s SAGAR policy, Sagarmala port program were seen in some minds as pulling in opposite directions India’s drive to build its own transhipment hubs is not playing out at Colombo’s expense, a leading Indian maritime strategist said, pointing to global shipping lines now investing in ports on both sides of the Palk Strait. New Delhi-based National Maritime Foundation (NMF) Director General Vice Admiral Pradeep Chauhan said port connectivity, long a source of anxiety in Sri Lanka, had become the most promising area for maritime cooperation between the two countries. He was speaking at the 50th webinar organised by the Daily FT, ACCA and the International Chamber of Commerce Sri Lanka, together with WIM, the Sri Lanka Institute of Directors, the MBA Alumni Association of the University of Colombo and Pioneer Institute of Business & Technology, on Saturday. The webinar was titled “In an Emerging New World Order, What Are Sri Lanka’s Options?” “In India and Sri Lanka, there has been a concern that as India develops its own transhipment hubs, will Colombo suffer?” Vice Admiral Chauhan said. Transhipment is the transfer of cargo from one vessel to another at an intermediate port en route to its final destination, and forms the core of the Port of Colombo’s business. He said the concern stemmed from how two Indian initiatives were viewed: the maritime policy encapsulated in the acronym SAGAR, and Sagarmala, which he described as India’s mega port connectivity initiative. For a while, in some minds, the two had pulled in opposite directions, with one seeking inclusivity and the other seen as excluding partner countries from the circulation of Indian money, he said. “But now I think that this is an area, peculiarly enough, which is the most promising for maritime cooperation, and it is already happening,” he said. Pointing to the major shipping lines, Vice Admiral Chauhan noted that Mediterranean Shipping Company (MSC) had decided to invest in both Colombo and Vizhinjam, which he described as the Indian port directly competing with Colombo. “This is not playing out as a zero-sum game. Far less is it playing out as a gloom and doom story,” he said, adding that it was an area in which a much greater amount of intellectual capital needed to be invested. Coastal shipping, he said, formed part of the same activity. His view was echoed by former Sri Lanka Navy Commander Admiral Jayantha Perera, who said Colombo, a global transhipment hub, drew about 80% of its transhipment cargo from India. “So there’s no competition with India. We have to cooperate with India and we must improve our level,” he said, adding that only then could Sri Lanka win the confidence of global shipping. Admiral Perera said Colombo handled about 9.9 million twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs), the standard measure of container volume, with capacity expected to reach about 11.1 million TEUs with the East and West terminals and about 15 million TEUs with expansion by 2028. Shipping density around Sri Lanka had risen sharply due to the Middle East conflict, with vessels at times having to wait outside port, he said. Beyond ports, Vice Admiral Chauhan identified disaster response as an area in which India and Sri Lanka were natural partners, “even if for no other reason than misery loves company”, and called for cooperation on human skilling so that human skills augmented rather than were threatened by AI, an area he said was receiving insufficient attention. He also urged a shift from treating the blue economy as a set of sectors to the “blueing” of the entire regional economy, saying Sri Lanka in many cases held the key, such as in converting shipping, a large polluter, into a greener mechanism by running smaller craft that ply between India and Sri Lanka on electricity rather than fossil fuels.

audit.body: Council for Business with Britain in Sri Lanka President Mark Surgenor In a groundbreaking achievement on the global business stage, Mark Surgenor, President of the Council for Business with Britain (CBB) in Sri Lanka (2023–2025), has been named the winner of the British Chambers of Commerce (BCC) International President’s Award 2026. Out of a competitive international network of more than 75 British Chambers of Commerce and Business Councils worldwide, this recognition marks a monumental milestone as the first time ever that Sri Lanka has received this prestigious award. The annual Chamber Awards celebrate the individuals and organisations that strengthen the global Chamber Network and drive international commerce. Mark... Surgenor was specifically honored for modernising the CBB during his two-year presidency (2023–2025), successfully transforming it from a traditional networking group into a high-value platform for commercial insight, trade access, and strategic connections. His tenure included hosting high-impact forums, engaging with over 200 member organisations, and founding CBB NextGen - a structured platform empowering the next generation of business leaders and entrepreneurs. Surgenor is CEO of HSBC Sri Lanka and Maldives. Additionally, he significantly strengthened bilateral partnerships with the British High Commission, the UK Department for Business and Trade, the Ceylon Chamber of Commerce, and peer councils. Commenting on the award, Surgenor said: «I›m honoured to receive the President›s Award and hugely grateful to everyone across the Council who has contributed to what we›ve achieved. Together we›ve worked to strengthen UK-Sri Lanka business links, bringing the next generation into our work and ensuring the Council offers real value to its members.» British Chambers of Commerce President Andy Haldane, CBE added: «Mark›s leadership shows the difference one individual can make to an entire business community. He has modernised the Council and created stronger practical connections between firms in the UK and Sri Lanka. This award is thoroughly deserved recognition of his energy, integrity and lasting contribution to the global Chamber Network.» Award supporter Quest CEO Des Shaw said: «Mark has combined strategic vision with practical delivery, creating lasting value for members and ensuring the Council is well placed for the future. We warmly congratulate him on his achievements.» To read the official announcement from the British Chambers of Commerce, visit: British Chambers of Commerce News

audit.body: - Subscription list for debentures opens 3 Nov. with Rs. 10 b initial offer and option to increase up to Rs. 30 b in two tranches - Four options: 5-year debentures offer fixed coupon of 12.75% or a floating rate of 1.5% above the 12-month Treasury Bill rate, while 7-year debentures offer 13% fixed or 1.75% above the Treasury Bill rate Bank of Ceylon (BOC), Sri Lanka’s leading state-owned commercial bank, is set to create another milestone in the country’s capital market with the launch of Sri Lanka’s largest-ever listed debenture issue, with a maximum issue size of Rs. 30 billion. The bank proposes to initially raise Rs. 10 billion, with an option to increase the issue to Rs. 20 billion in the event of an oversubscription of the initial tranche and a further option to increase the total issue size up to Rs. 30 billion, making it the largest listed debenture issue undertaken in Sri Lanka. The proposed issue comprises Basel III compliant, Tier 2, Listed, Rated, Unsecured, Subordinated, Redeemable debentures with a non-viability write-down feature. The debentures carry an issue rating of AA (Stable) from Lanka Rating Agency, while BOC’s issuer rating stands at AA-(lka)/Stable from Fitch Ratings Lanka Ltd. The debentures will be offered with five-year and seven-year maturities, providing with medium to long-term fixed income investment opportunities. The issue is confined to qualified investors and the minimum subscription for qualified investors is Rs. 10,000, while individual investors are required to apply for at least Rs. 5 million. The debentures are offered in four different types to meet diverse requirements of qualified investors. The fixed coupon rate of the five-year debenture will be 12.75% per annum while the floating coupon rate will be 1.50% above the applicable twelve-month Treasury Bill rate. The Fixed coupon rate of the seven-year debenture will be 13% per annum while the floating coupon rate will be 1.75% above the applicable twelve-month Treasury Bill rate. BOC’s largest debenture issue comes at a significant juncture for the Sri Lankan economy, at a time when the country is prioritising sustainable, investment-led and inclusive economic growth. Against this backdrop, a stronger capital base will further enhance BOC’s capacity to mobilise and channel funds towards productive sectors of the economy, thereby supporting Sri Lanka’s next phase of economic development. This landmark issue therefore represents more than a significant capital-raising exercise for the bank. BOC, as the country’s leading state-owned commercial bank, remains well positioned to play a pivotal role in financing businesses, facilitating investment and supporting the broader development priorities of the country. BOC is a Corporate Finance Advisor licensed by the Securities and Exchange Commission of Sri Lanka. This largest Basel III Debenture issuance was exclusively structured and managed by the Investment Banking team who possess a wealth of expertise in structuring innovative capital market instruments. The issue follows BOC’s pioneering Sustainability Bond issuance, another landmark transaction structured and managed by the bank’s Investment Banking Division, reflecting BOC’s continued leadership in developing innovative capital-market solutions while advancing sustainable finance in Sri Lanka. The Legal Department of BOC acts as the lawyers to the issue, while the Corporate Branch of the bank acts as the bankers to the issue. The Investment Banking Division will also continue to act as the Registrar to the proposed issue, while Hatton National Bank PLC will be the trustee to the issue. The bank is opening the subscription list of the BASEL III Debenture Issue at 9.30 a.m. on 3 November 2026 and will remain open for 14 market days unless the bank decides to close it earlier based on subscription levels. Applications for the debentures will be accepted from qualified investors in accordance with the terms and conditions set out in the Prospectus. The Prospectus and application forms can be downloaded from the web sites of the CSE; www.cse.lk and BOC; www.boc.lk. Duly completed application forms should be enclosed in an envelope marked “BOC Debenture Issue” together with the remittance for the full amount payable on application and delivered to the Investment Banking Division at 7th Floor of BOC Head Office or collection points mentioned in the prospectus. With a long-standing presence in Sri Lanka’s banking industry, Bank of Ceylon has played a significant role in the country’s economic development by mobilising savings, extending credit and supporting individuals, businesses and major economic sectors. The proposed debenture issue is expected to further enhance the bank’s capacity to support corporate, SME, retail and institutional customers while maintaining prudent regulatory capital buffers. Investors are advised to carefully read the Prospectus, including the terms of the debentures, risk factors, non-viability write-down provisions and eligibility requirements, before making an investment decision. Bank of Ceylon invites eligible local and foreign investors to participate in this landmark issue and be a part of the bank’s continuing journey of financial strength and contribution to Sri Lanka’s economic development. At a time when the country is entering a new phase of investment-led growth, the issue represents an opportunity for investors to participate in the growth journey of the nation’s leading state-owned commercial bank while contributing to the broader economic progress of Sri Lanka.

The latest data released by the Sri Lanka Export Development Board (EDB) showed that merchandise exports shipped in September were up 21.66% YoY to over $ 1.38 billion, though estimated service earnings in the month showed a moderate growth of 0.67% YoY to $ 306.17 million.
audit.body: - September total exports up 17.23% to $ 1.69 b; YTD earnings up 5.04% YoY to $ 13.61 b - Jan.-Sept. merchandise exports up 5.35% YoY to $ 10.76 b; services rise 3.88% YoY to $ 2.85 b - EDB Chief Mangala Wijesinghe expresses confidence in recording over $ 18 b export target by year-end Sri Lanka’s export sector posted its highest-ever monthly performance in September 2026, with total earnings surpassing $ 1.69 billion and reflecting a 17.23% year-on-year (YoY) growth driven by strong merchandise shipments, despite the challenges faced by the tensions in the Middle East and its direct impact on overall costs. The latest data released by the Sri Lanka Export Development Board (EDB) showed that merchandise exports shipped in September were up 21.66% YoY to over $ 1.38 billion, though estimated service earnings in the month showed a moderate growth of 0.67% YoY to $ 306.17 million. The September exports registered a 5.6% month-on-month (MoM) increase compared to August 2026. Cumulative exports during the first nine months of 2026 rose by 5.04% YoY to over $ 13.61 billion, also marking the highest recorded level for the period. Merchandise export earnings during January-September increased by 5.35% YoY to over $ 10.76 billion, whilst services exports during the same period were estimated to have surged by 3.88% to $ 2.85 billion. Services exports include sectors such as ICT/BPM, construction, financial services, and transport and logistics. Addressing the media, EDB Chairman and CEO Mangala Wijesinghe described the September outcome as a resilient way towards achieving the country’s annual merchandise export target of over $ 18 billion, whilst commending exporters for navigating external shocks and yet contributing to economic development. “This performance demonstrates the potential of Sri Lankan exporters to strengthen their presence in international markets despite an increasingly competitive global trading environment. As we move forward, our priority must be to sustain this growth momentum by strengthening the competitiveness of existing export sectors while accelerating the development of new products, services and markets,” he said. For 2026, Sri Lanka has set an ambitious export revenue target of $ 20 billion, reflecting an anticipated YoY growth of 10-12%. Merchandise exports are expected to exceed $ 15.7 billion in 2026, while services exports are projected to rise to $ 4.3 billion. The EDB noted that the merchandise exports growth in September was driven largely by improved demand across the agricultural and industrial product categories, while services lagged. Apparel and textile exports rose 3.46% YoY to $ 439.78 million in September 2026, from $ 425.07 million a year earlier. Exports to the US rose 6.33%. Rubber and rubber-based product exports surged 33.68% to $ 99.31 million, up from $ 74.29 million in September 2025. Industrial and surgical rubber glove exports grew 34.38% to $ 31.70 million, while pneumatic and retreaded tyres and tubes increased 39.57% to $ 54.95 million. Exports of spices, essential oils and oleoresins climbed 73.19% to $ 74.73 million. Pepper exports jumped 165.38% to $ 23.46 million, while cinnamon exports rose 68.27% to $ 42.59 million. Coconut fibre-based product exports recorded a 2.99% increase. Activated carbon exports grew 43.52% YoY to $ 25.26 million, reflecting stronger earnings from value-added coconut-based products. Food and beverage exports increased 27.92% to $ 63.77 million in September 2026, compared with $ 49.85 million a year earlier. Electrical and electronic component exports surged 88.35% YoY to $ 68.54 million, supported by a 114.62% increase in insulated wire and cable exports. Seafood exports rose 4.01% to $ 23.61 million, from $ 22.70 million in September 2025. Frozen fish exports increased 15.85% to $ 13.96 million, while shrimp exports surged 207.27% to $ 3.38 million. Meanwhile, transport and logistics services exports were estimated at $ 167.9 million, up 23.32% from $ 136.15 million in September 2025. Cumulative export earnings from key value-added sectors recorded YoY growth during January–September 2026. Rubber-based products rose 8.44%, coconut-based products 3.68%, processed food and beverages 20.9%, electrical and electronic components 61.05%, and spices and concentrates 30.53%. However, apparel and textile exports declined 5.68% YoY to $ 3,783.76 million. Apparel exports fell 5.36% to $ 3,513.37 million, while textile exports dropped 9.66% to $ 270.39 million. Exports to the US, European Union (EU) and the UK decreased by 3.83%, 5.54% and 10.41%, respectively, amid subdued demand in key markets. Tea export earnings fell 6.83% to $ 1,083.58 million. Tea packet exports declined 4.42%, while bulk tea earnings dropped 11.13%. Growth in tea bag exports of 53.39% and instant tea exports of 9.85% was insufficient to offset the overall contraction. Weaker demand in the Middle East further affected performance, with tea exports to the region falling 34.22%. Shipments to the United Arab Emirates, Iran and Iraq declined by 59.66%, 65.80% and 47.72%, respectively. The US, Sri Lanka’s largest export market, accounting for 20.3% of merchandise exports, recorded an 18.06% YoY increase in September 2026, with earnings reaching $ 281.84 million. Cumulative exports to the US rose marginally by 0.05% to $ 2,252.99 million during January–September 2026. India overtook the UK to become Sri Lanka’s second-largest export destination, with cumulative exports increasing 12.3% to $ 889.84 million during the first nine months of 2026. September exports to India surged 29.65% YoY to $ 113.22 million. In contrast, exports to the UK fell 3.17% to $ 71.71 million in September, while cumulative earnings declined 9.33% to $ 654.36 million. Exports to the EU, accounting for 20.12% of Sri Lanka’s merchandise exports, increased 1.92% YoY in September 2026. However, cumulative exports to the bloc declined marginally by 0.15% during January–September 2026, indicating broadly stable performance in the key market.

audit.headline: Nearly Perfect GPA, International Awards, and a Mission to Serve Sri Lanka
audit.summary: COLOMBO (News 1st); A Sri Lankan Navy officer who has spent years breaking barriers is celebrating yet another milestone, this time on the international stage, after graduating with a near-perfect GPA and multiple prestigious awards from a leading United States military university. U.S. Ambassador Eric Meyer presented a Master's degree from the U.S. Naval Postgraduate School (NPS) to Lieutenant Commander Piyumi Kathriarachchi of the Sri Lanka Navy at the American Center in Colombo, marking the completion of an academic journey that has earned recognition both in the United States and Sri Lanka. The ceremony was attended by Rear Admiral Rohan Joseph, Director General of Training, and Commander C.R.P. Walakuluge, Director of Media of the Sri Lanka Navy.
audit.body: COLOMBO (News 1st); A Sri Lankan Navy officer who has spent years breaking barriers is celebrating yet another milestone, this time on the international stage, after graduating with a near-perfect GPA and multiple prestigious awards from a leading United States military university. U.S. Ambassador Eric Meyer presented a Master's degree from the U.S. Naval Postgraduate School (NPS) to Lieutenant Commander Piyumi Kathriarachchi of the Sri Lanka Navy at the American Center in Colombo, marking the completion of an academic journey that has earned recognition both in the United States and Sri Lanka. The ceremony was attended by Rear Admiral Rohan Joseph, Director General of Training, and Commander C.R.P. Walakuluge, Director of Media of the Sri Lanka Navy. Praising her achievement, Ambassador Meyer said Lieutenant Commander Kathriarachchi's success highlights both individual excellence and the long-term value of professional military education. "Lieutenant Commander Kathriarachchi's achievements reflect both her exceptional dedication and the value of world-class American military education. Through U.S.-funded training, she has gained knowledge and skills that she is now bringing home to strengthen Sri Lanka's Navy. Her success demonstrates how investing in the professional development of our partners strengthens our defense cooperation and contributes to a safer, more secure Indian Ocean region," Ambassador Meyer said. Graduating near the top of her class at the U.S. Naval Postgraduate School in Monterey, California, Lieutenant Commander Kathriarachchi completed the Defense Logistics Management programme with honours, achieving an outstanding 3.98 Grade Point Average out of a possible 4.0. Her academic success was accompanied by two major honours: the NPS Outstanding Thesis Award and the Kiwanis Club of Monterey Outstanding International Student Award, an accolade presented to only two international students at the institution each year. Her studies were funded through the U.S. International Military Education and Training (IMET) programme, which supports the professional development of Sri Lankan military personnel while strengthening defence cooperation between Sri Lanka and the United States. Beyond the classroom, her research focused on spare parts procurement challenges faced by the Sri Lanka Navy, producing practical recommendations aimed at improving operational readiness and strengthening naval capabilities. Following the degree presentation, Lieutenant Commander Kathriarachchi engaged with Sri Lankan youth at the American Center, encouraging them to pursue education, develop new skills and seize opportunities that can contribute to the country's future. Reflecting on her experience in the United States, she said: "My time in the United States gave me new tools to tackle real challenges facing our Navy. I look forward to putting that knowledge to work in service of Sri Lanka and hope my experience encourages other young Sri Lankans to pursue opportunities that can make a difference for our country." For Lieutenant Commander Kathriarachchi, international recognition is the latest chapter in a career already defined by historic achievements. A past pupil of Taxila Central College, Horana, she made history in 2013 by becoming the first female midshipman in Sri Lanka Navy history to receive the prestigious Sword of Honour. (Image Provided By U.S. Embassy in Sri Lanka)

audit.body: COLOMBO (News 1st); A new generation of Indian naval leaders arrived in Colombo as three vessels from the Indian Navy's First Training Squadron made a formal visit to Sri Lanka, bringing with them 135 officer under-trainees and a renewed focus on maritime cooperation between the two neighbouring nations. The training ships INS Tir, INS Sujata, and ICGS Sarathi docked in Colombo on October 26 and were welcomed by the Sri Lanka Navy in keeping with longstanding naval traditions. Joseph, INS Sujata, a 103-metre Offshore Patrol Vessel under the command of Commander Jishnu Madhavan, and ICGS Sarathi, a 105-metre Offshore Patrol Vessel commanded by Commandant Kundan Singh. The Commanding Officers of the three vessels called on Commander Western Naval Area Rear Admiral Harsha De Silva at the Western Naval Command Headquarters, where mementoes were exchanged to mark the occasion and reaffirm the cordial relationship between the two navies. During their stay in Sri Lanka, the officers and trainees are scheduled to participate in a range of programmes organised by the Sri Lanka Navy aimed at enhancing bilateral ties, professional engagement and mutual cooperation. Sri Lankan naval personnel will also have the opportunity to board the visiting vessels, observe training operations and exchange professional expertise with their Indian counterparts, providing valuable opportunities for learning and collaboration. Beyond official engagements, the visiting officers and trainees are expected to tour several key locations and places of interest across the island, allowing them to experience Sri Lanka's culture, heritage and maritime significance while further strengthening people-to-people connections between the two countries.

audit.headline: Red Alert: Deep Depression Intensifies into Cyclone 'ARNAB'
audit.summary: COLOMBO — The Department of Meteorology has issued a Red Alert for deep sea areas following the intensification of the deep depression over the Bay of Bengal into Cyclonic Storm ‘ARNAB’. The advisory, issued at 9:30 AM today (Oct 26) and valid for the next 12 hours, warns of extremely strong winds, severe sea turbulence, and heavy thundershowers in the affected maritime regions. According to the department, the system over the East-Central and adjoining Southeast Bay of Bengal is expected to move west-northwestwards and intensify further into a severe cyclonic storm over the West-Central Bay of Bengal by 11:30 PM tonight. Wind speeds in these sea areas could reach 80–100 km/h at times, with wave heights surging to 3–4 meters, making the sea exceptionally rough.

Consequently, naval and fishing communities are strictly advised to refrain from venturing into sea areas bounded by Latitudes 10°N to 20°N and Longitudes 80°E to 95°E until further notice. Those currently operating within these coordinates are strongly urged to navigate to safer waters immediately and stay updated on forthcoming advisories.

audit.body: AIA Sri Lanka has launched iAcademy, a next-generation digital learning platform designed to simplify and modernise the onboarding and training experience for new Wealth Planners, marking another significant milestone in the company’s transformation journey through Project NOVA. Designed to make learning more accessible and engaging, iAcademy transforms traditionally location-based training programs into a digital experience that can be accessed online, anytime and anywhere. AIA Wealth Planners can now progress through their training at their own pace while benefiting from a consistent and structured onboarding experience. The platform provides new Wealth Planners the essential knowledge and capabilities required to begin their careers with AIA. The learning journey includes an introduction to values and culture, together with comprehensive product knowledge, insurance fundamentals, an understanding of the Wealth Planner profession and its benefits, sales processes and best practices, and compliance and regulatory requirements. iAcademy also includes an interactive orientation learning experience, licensing examination guidance, with trilingual language support. Importantly, the platform goes beyond digital learning to help streamline the wider onboarding journey. iAcademy provides real-time visibility of training progress and completion status, and upon the successful completion of all required modules, the onboarding process is automatically advanced. AIA Sri Lanka Deputy CEO /Chief Distribution Officer Upul Wijesinghe said: “By harnessing technology, we are creating a faster, simpler and more accessible onboarding experience that gives our Wealth Planners greater flexibility in how they learn, while equipping them with the knowledge and confidence they need to succeed from day one.” Chief Agency Officer Dimuthu Piyasena said: “Our Wealth Planners are central to the way we connect with and serve our customers. iAcademy allows us to deliver a structured and engaging learning experience while giving new Wealth Planners the flexibility to learn at their own pace.” AIA Sri Lanka said as it continues transformation through Project NOVA, iAcademy represents another step towards building a more digitally enabled agency force, while ensuring new Wealth Planners have the knowledge, tools and confidence to succeed from the outset.

audit.headline: Agentic AI: People and organisations at the crossroads
audit.summary: Ten years ago, I worked as the Chief Commercial Officer of a mid-size software company developing solutions for the BFSI sector. The word fintech was not so popular back then. RPA or Robotic Process Automation software was introduced in Sri Lanka during this time, and we opted to be a distributor for one of the three pioneering brands entered the market namely Blue Prism, UI Path and Automation Anywhere. RPA was ideal to automate processes of banks, insurance firms, and state authorities such as passport and border control handling large volumes of repetitive and rule-based tasks. Fast forward, we now have AI enabled RPA which is an evolutionary leap beyond RPA and popularly known as Agentic AI that is going to make a big revolution in every industry across the world.
audit.body: Ten years ago, I worked as the Chief Commercial Officer of a mid-size software company developing solutions for the BFSI sector. The word fintech was not so popular back then. RPA or Robotic Process Automation software was introduced in Sri Lanka during this time, and we opted to be a distributor for one of the three pioneering brands entered the market namely Blue Prism, UI Path and Automation Anywhere. RPA was ideal to automate processes of banks, insurance firms, and state authorities such as passport and border control handling large volumes of repetitive and rule-based tasks. Fast forward, we now have AI enabled RPA which is an evolutionary leap beyond RPA and popularly known as Agentic AI that is going to make a big revolution in every industry across the world. This article aims to explain benefits, challenges and strategic directions for managers and business firms who will adopt Agentic AI in automating their workflows. The profound use of AI AI has now become an everyday tool for most of the digitally literate individuals and tech savvy firms. Students, researchers, and employees of business firms use AI in their work with varying degrees of consent, competence and confusion. Many business firms allow employees to use AI as it can substantially improve productivity. Hours of coding work done by software engineers now happen in minutes. Teachers caution poor analytical skills and creativity among children due to heavy reliance on AI. Discussions between service providers and customers such as doctors and patients are becoming short and precise. Similarly, people are afraid of losing jobs as AI has become explosive filled with promises and fears. Convergence of automation and AI RPAs were good in doing tasks but lacked thinking capability. AI particularly the LLMs or Large Language Models provide the ability to understand, logical reasoning, and plan. In other words, AI provides the brain. RPAs provide the ability to execute functions such as clicking a button, copying and pasting etc. The convergence of RPA and AI has given us real digital workers known as AI agents who can work like human employees. Agentic AI which comprises of multiple agents, can interact with different applications, manipulate data, manage and control hardware and execute tasks to achieve specific goals. Some argue that humans will work for machines in future. Humans losing control on fully autonomous systems can bring unprecedented threats to the world. Think of an era where power generation, irrigation management, air traffic control, border control etc. happen with no human intervention. Given these capabilities of Agentic AI, you may now think of the fate of BPO and KPO operations, service-oriented organisations and the back-office functions of top brands outsourced from developing countries. Five levels of automation The popular 2025 book by Pascal Bornet and his team on Agentic AI highlights its progress with five levels of automation. Level 1 describes rule-based automation, and this is what we had as RPA. Level 2 refers to intelligent automation. Levels 3 to 5 describe agentic workflows, semi-autonomous and fully autonomous agentic systems respectively. They emphasise the importance of starting automation at a low level in your organisation as it will enable you to be familiar with it, have control and governance mechanisms in place. This also shows the low control managers will have at higher levels of agentic automation and less instructions humans need to give. The Cybercab by Tesla that has no steering wheel, pedals and mirrors is probably the latest and popular example for an autonomous agentic system. Innovations in the era of Agentic AI Unlike inventions, innovations need not to be grand discoveries and brand new to the world. If there is any sensible change, we make to a product or a process that can add value to stakeholders we can explain it as an innovation. It is stunning to see what Agentic AI can do in the wide array of innovation types and processes popularly in use such as incremental, radical, architectural, modular, disruptive, reverse, frugal, outcome driven and open innovation. As Agentic AI learns and improves what it does in each task, what we can expect is a dramatic push in all types of innovations. It is true that creativity is central to invent and innovate and we often tend to question the ability of machines to think creatively. Despite the algorithms and lines of codes or instructions they follow, machines are now capable of thinking. This flexibility in controls may lead to continuous incremental innovations in products and processes. We as human beings can have some protection until AI powered machines explore the exciting and uncertain world of disruptive innovations. Some already highlight the enormous threats the world may face with super intelligence. Dynamic capability embedded to DNA David Teece coined the term dynamic capability to remind organisations of the need to upgrade and update their capabilities in response to changes in the business environment. His latest articles and videos published in 2025 reemphasise the need of reconfiguring the capabilities of an organisation to remain competitive. Managers of all levels of a business firm, especially at the middle level, have this challenge of managing dynamic capabilities to ensure the organisation has an edge over competition and to accelerate innovations. Agentic AI being a practice that necessarily relies on learning from mistakes and constant learning for improvements, the future firms that are empowered with Agentic AI will have dynamic capabilities embedded to its DNA. This is no different to how culture is infused into the blood of an organisation. Organisational inertia to fade away People and organisations generally resist change. The preference to maintain the current equilibrium in the organisation known as the status-quo and rigid processes and procedures lead to organisational inertia that prevents change or makes it challenging. System integration is identified as the most challenging area business firms face when introducing AI Agents. Significant resistance may come from the technical people as the remedial measure involves ‘API first’ architecture. However, with more AI agents in use by business firms, managers may expect low inertia in future. One can argue that the level 3 Agentic workflows which is right now the most seen level of agentic automation will certainly result in low resistance to change. Sustainability AI and Agentic AI require large amounts of resources. As highlighted in the AI Index Report 2026 by Stanford University, this is an industry which is scaling faster than surrounding systems around can adopt. Research and practices that aim to optimise resource utilisation include and are not limited to edge computing, fog computing, AI accelerators etc. Bio-inspired swarm intelligence and socially inspired intelligence are also popular areas for research. Increasing energy and water footprints, especially at data centers have become a major concern for governments and other interest groups. Given the speed of growth of AI, it is becoming important to monitor and regulate its purpose of use, the scope and cost before it is too late and irreversible. Need for policy imperatives We often see in local media multiple initiatives by state authorities and think tanks on the way forward to a digital economy. Given that as a key goal in the national agenda, artificial intelligence particularly Agentic AI should necessarily be a focus area by policy makers and managers. Attempting to be competitive in regional or global markets without leveraging on agentic AI as a value driver will certainly be a costly lesson for everyone. Once again, we prove that we are quite slow in technology adoption as a nation in this massive transformation as well. We are behind many other nations, as highlighted in the AI diffusion report 2025 by Microsoft AI Economy Institute. State authorities, universities and business firms have a major role to play in increasing AI adoption for productive purposes. Ethical perspectives in Agentic AI Top managers will face extremely challenging situations in adopting Agentic AI. The popular utilitarian way of deciding by looking at the consequences of a decision where pleasure for majority and pain for minority is the accepted norm cannot be easily applied here. One might argue that Agentic AI can enhance productivity and the broader society will benefit. Yet, at what cost is the question one needs to answer by looking at multiple stakeholders. A regular question I asked in my MBA classes for many years is who will need driverless cars and at what cost. Agentic AI systems are no different. Cost here is not only the cost of ownership and operations but also the social cost, impact on the environment, use of depleting resources and hidden losses in upstream and downstream activities. Surely, the excitement of a new technology cannot be at the cost of losing your job, water to drink and electricity for daily use. Hypercompetition may prompt business firms to resort to Agentic AI to get ahead. Managers need to think carefully about the quality of the decisions they make and the consequences, especially in the long run. (The author is a Senior Academic Fellow attached to SLIIT Business School. He is a Fellow of the British Computer Society, and holds chartered/corporate memberships of nine other professional institutions in mechanical engineering, computing, psychology, marketing, logistics and innovation. He is an ex-banker with several decades of experience in diverse industry sectors. He has been teaching organisational behavior, strategy and innovation management for over 25 years in postgraduate programs of 25 local and international universities. He could be reached via email [email protected])

audit.headline: Alumex wins Bronze at National AI Awards 2026 for AI-powered manufacturing innovation
audit.summary: Representatives of Alumex PLC holding the award trophy and framed certificate at the National AI Awards 2026 after winning Bronze in the Best AI Solution in Manufacturing & Industry 5.0 category Alumex PLC, a member of the Hayleys Group and a leading manufacturer of aluminium extrusions in Sri Lanka, has won a Bronze award in the ‘Best AI Solution in Manufacturing and Industry 5.0’ category at the National AI Awards 2026 on 30 September. The award was bestowed under the auspices of the Digital Economy Ministry. The award-winning innovation is an extruder production monitoring system and smart real-time energy monitoring and analytics system, featuring an AI-powered golden batch for extrusion digitisation.
audit.body: Representatives of Alumex PLC holding the award trophy and framed certificate at the National AI Awards 2026 after winning Bronze in the Best AI Solution in Manufacturing & Industry 5.0 category Alumex PLC, a member of the Hayleys Group and a leading manufacturer of aluminium extrusions in Sri Lanka, has won a Bronze award in the ‘Best AI Solution in Manufacturing and Industry 5.0’ category at the National AI Awards 2026 on 30 September. The award was bestowed under the auspices of the Digital Economy Ministry. The award-winning innovation is an extruder production monitoring system and smart real-time energy monitoring and analytics system, featuring an AI-powered golden batch for extrusion digitisation. This recognition acknowledges the company’s application of AI and data analytics to improve production monitoring alongside process consistency and energy management across its manufacturing operations. In addition, the solution provides real-time visibility into extrusion operations and production performance, while through its AI-powered golden batch, production data is analysed to identify process variations, improve batch consistency and support faster, data-driven decisions. The Bronze award marks a significant step in the company’s continued advancement in smart manufacturing, reflecting its focus on integrating digital capabilities into its operations and building more connected, responsive and technology-enabled manufacturing processes. Alumex PLC remains committed to exploring innovative applications of technology across its operations.
