For a pre-commercial venture still validating its first structuring corridor, membership is a useful credential when courting design-partner law firms and institutional investors. Fernando, Managing Director of Melbourne-based STF Corporate Advisory, joined Sententia.ai as Corporate Advisor in September and now serves as Investor and Board Advisor. His career spans HSBC Investment Banking, Dresdner Kleinwort and Goldman Sachs, with his work covering mergers and acquisitions, capital raising and cross-border mandates. The venture positions itself beyond conventional legal automation. It argues that the future of law and finance lies in systems capable of understanding transaction architecture and navigating regulatory complexity. “We are building a neural network for undertaking transactions, transforming complex cross-border requirements into structured investment models, fund structures, risk intelligence, and execution-ready workflows,” the company noted. “Our vision is to make global capital programmable,” it added. Sententia.ai was conceptualised by Shayant Bhattacharjee, a law student at Maharashtra National Law University (MNLU), Nagpur, whose paralegal work on FDI and cross-border M&A mandates at Tier-1 law firms shaped the founding premise. He is joined by fellow MNLU students Prakhar Mishra and Navya Y., while Sanidhya Jain, who studies at Drexel University, Philadelphia, leads the venture’s AI architecture as Chief Technology Officer. Cambridge-trained corporate and TMT lawyer Rupal Chhaya sits on its advisory board. Meanwhile, the company said the Inception membership would support its efforts as it continues building what it describes as “the intelligence layer for global transactions.”

audit.headline: A practical guide to internships for Sri Lankan students
audit.summary: An internship is not a holiday from learning. It is learning of a different kind, and the students who extract the most from it are those who treat every task, including the routine ones, as an opportunity to understand how a professional environment actually functions. The intern who updates a spreadsheet with full attention to accuracy is building a reputation. The one who does it carelessly is building a different one. H ere is the contradiction that every Sri Lankan student eventually runs into: you cannot get a job without experience, and you cannot get experience without a job. It is one of the most frustrating closed loops in professional life, and it is especially acute in a country where 43 percent of tertiary-educated young people aged 15 to 24 are currently unemployed, the highest rate in Asia according to IMF data published in September 2026.
audit.body: An internship is not a holiday from learning. It is learning of a different kind, and the students who extract the most from it are those who treat every task, including the routine ones, as an opportunity to understand how a professional environment actually functions. The intern who updates a spreadsheet with full attention to accuracy is building a reputation. The one who does it carelessly is building a different one. H ere is the contradiction that every Sri Lankan student eventually runs into: you cannot get a job without experience, and you cannot get experience without a job. It is one of the most frustrating closed loops in professional life, and it is especially acute in a country where 43 percent of tertiary-educated young people aged 15 to 24 are currently unemployed, the highest rate in Asia according to IMF data published in September 2026. The internship is, quite simply, the most practical tool available to break that loop before you graduate, and the students who understand this and act on it early are the ones who arrive at the job market with something that a degree alone cannot give them: proof and practice. An internship is a structured, time-limited period of work experience within an organisation, usually undertaken while you are still studying, that gives you exposure to professional environments, real tasks and real accountability. It is not merely unpaid labour in exchange for a certificate. Done well, it is one of the most valuable investments of time you can make during your university years, and the research bears this out with considerable clarity. Beyond the skills and experience gained, an internship does something specific and measurable for your professional profile: it signals to future employers that someone trusted you with real work before they did, and found you worth the investment. 72 percent of employers globally say they use internships to identify candidates who are a good fit for their organisation, according to a 2024 survey. 54 percent of interns report using their internship experience directly to improve their resume and interview performance. And completing an internship programme makes you 32 percent more likely to receive a full-time job offer, according to research by the National Association of Colleges and Employers. The Global Employability University Ranking and Survey for 2025, drawing on recruiter responses across 29 countries, found that employers are increasingly prioritising work experience and internships when evaluating candidates above almost every other graduate attribute. A peer-reviewed paper published in the Journal of Applied Research in Higher Education in 2026, examining graduate employability across developing and developed economies, found that approximately 38 percent of graduates in Asia are underemployed, and identified work-integrated learning, specifically internships and applied projects, as among the most significant interventions for reducing that figure. Closer to home, the CareerLK 2026 internship guide for Sri Lankan students confirms that the best placements at Sri Lanka’s leading companies, including John Keells Holdings, MAS Holdings, Dialog Axiata, WSO2, Commercial Bank and the Big Four accounting firms, are competitive and fill up months in advance. This is not a reason to be discouraged; it’s a reason to start earlier than you think you need to. The good news is that internship opportunities in Sri Lanka have grown significantly across technology, finance, marketing, engineering, hospitality and HR in recent years. The challenge for most students is knowing where to look consistently and systematically rather than waiting to hear about an opening through a family connection, which remains the dominant informal channel but is not available to everyone equally. The most reliable starting points are dedicated platforms. InternJobs.lk was created specifically to list internship, trainee and school leaver opportunities across Sri Lanka and is updated daily. ITPro.lk lists technology and software internships specifically, with 250 or more positions active at any given time. XpressJobs carries a broader range. LinkedIn, particularly with location set to Sri Lanka and job type filtered to internship, surfaces opportunities from multinationals and locally listed companies simultaneously. Your university’s career centre is a resource that is consistently underused by students and consistently valuable to those who do use it. Most Sri Lankan universities maintain active relationships with employer partners who offer placements specifically to students from that institution. Edith Cowan University in Sri Lanka, for instance, matches student CVs directly to partner companies through its internship placement service. Sri Lanka Technology Campus has a formal partnership with XpressJobs for the same purpose. Attending your university’s career fair, even in your first or second year before you need an internship, builds familiarity with the employers who recruit from your campus and gives you a head start on the relationships that matter. Company career pages are worth checking directly and regularly, particularly for Dialog, Unilever, Hayleys, Sampath Bank, Hatton National Bank and the technology firms IFS, Virtusa and 99x, all of which run structured programmes with competitive stipends and, in many cases, direct pathways to graduate employment. The application process for most Sri Lankan internships follows a recognisable sequence: CV submission, a cover letter or application form, sometimes an assessment or aptitude test, and one or two rounds of interviews. The CV for an internship application should be one page, clean and tailored to the role you are applying for rather than sent as a generic document to every vacancy simultaneously. It should lead with your academic background, include any relevant projects, research, volunteer work or part-time experience, and be completely free of errors, because an error-riddled CV from someone asking to be trusted with professional responsibility is a contradiction that hiring managers notice immediately. The cover letter, which many students omit and should not, is your opportunity to demonstrate that you have actually read about the organisation and have a specific reason for wanting to work there rather than simply needing an internship to fulfil a degree requirement. One paragraph explaining what draws you to that company, one paragraph on what you bring and one paragraph on what you hope to learn is sufficient and effective. If you require assistance for developing your portfolio or CV preparation for ingtersnip application, FitForWork Pvt. Ltd. can help you (fitforworksl.com). Apply to between ten and fifteen well-chosen opportunities rather than sending the same application to fifty at once. Successful candidates in Sri Lanka’s internship market, according to InternJobs.lk guidance, tend to apply consistently and strategically over several weeks, revisiting platforms regularly rather than doing a single application sprint and waiting. The first week of any internship is disorienting for almost everyone, and this is entirely normal. You will not know the systems, the culture, the unwritten rules or the expectations, and you will feel more uncertain than your degree perhaps prepared you to feel. The most important thing you can do in that first week is observe carefully, ask questions rather than guess, and demonstrate that you are the kind of person an organisation can trust with increasingly responsible work. An internship is not a holiday from learning. It is learning of a different kind, and the students who extract the most from it are those who treat every task, including the routine ones, as an opportunity to understand how a professional environment actually functions. The intern who updates a spreadsheet with full attention to accuracy is building a reputation. The one who does it carelessly is building a different one. Ask for feedback before you leave, along with a recommendation letter from your Team Lead or supervisor. Build at least two or three genuine professional relationships during your placement. Connect with your supervisor and colleagues on LinkedIn before your last day. These connections are not simply names in a network; they are the people who will be your references, your referrals and, sometimes, your future employers. In a Sri Lankan job market where the gap between educated graduates and available employment has never been more visible, the internship is not a nice-to-have. It is the most practical intervention available to a student who wants to arrive at graduation already in motion rather than starting from zero. Begin looking in your second year. Apply in your third. Treat the placement as seriously as any examination. The results will be more durable than most marks you have ever received. It will set the tone for the rest of your career ahead. The author is the founder of the social enterprise initiative FitForWork in Sri Lanka (fitforworksl.com) that offers intelligent and proactive solutions to enable dignified re-entry to work.She has a career history of two decades in development practice, working to enhance economic and social dignity of women and children.

audit.headline: BBDO Sri Lanka’s Wajinie Mahanama named among ‘Campaign Asia-Pacific’s Women to Watch 2026’
audit.summary: BBDO Group Sri Lanka Associate Vice President and Client Servicing Director Wajinie Mahanama has been named among Campaign Asia-Pacific’s Women to Watch 2026 , recognising her contribution to the advertising industry through sustained business growth, trusted client relationships and a leadership approach grounded in accountability and purpose. Now in its 14th year, the regional recognition celebrates 25 women across 12 markets whose expertise, business performance and influence are shaping Asia Pacific’s marketing and communications landscape. Wajinie’s selection reflects a career spanning 15 years in advertising, during which she has led major client portfolios, driven business growth and championed work that creates meaningful social impact.
audit.body: BBDO Group Sri Lanka Associate Vice President and Client Servicing Director Wajinie Mahanama has been named among Campaign Asia-Pacific’s Women to Watch 2026 , recognising her contribution to the advertising industry through sustained business growth, trusted client relationships and a leadership approach grounded in accountability and purpose. Now in its 14th year, the regional recognition celebrates 25 women across 12 markets whose expertise, business performance and influence are shaping Asia Pacific’s marketing and communications landscape. Wajinie’s selection reflects a career spanning 15 years in advertising, during which she has led major client portfolios, driven business growth and championed work that creates meaningful social impact. BBDO Group Sri Lanka, Executive Chairman Thayalan Bartlett said; “Wajinie’s recognition reflects the kind of leadership that builds lasting value for clients, businesses and the industry. Her ability to combine commercial discipline with a deep understanding of people and brands has made her a trusted leader within our organisation. She represents the strength of Sri Lankan talent on the regional stage, and we look forward to seeing her continue to do BIG things.” Throughout her career, Wajinie has built enduring client partnerships while leading brands across diverse sectors. Her portfolio includes campaigns and initiatives that extend beyond commercial objectives, including work supporting social awareness and behavioural change through brands such as Eva Sanitary Napkins and Atlas Sipsavi Scholarship programme. Her leadership also places importance on mentoring colleagues, supporting young talent and creating an inclusive workplace. “Being named among Campaign Asia-Pacific’s Women to Watch is a meaningful milestone in a journey shaped by continuous learning, resilience and the people who have challenged and supported me. I believe lasting leadership comes from staying curious, honouring commitments and remaining willing to evolve. This recognition encourages me to keep contributing to the industry, supporting others and creating work that makes a difference,” said Wajinie Mahanama, Associate Vice President, Client Servicing Director, BBDO Group Sri Lanka. Wajinie’s regional recognition is complemented by her selection in the ‘Outstanding Leadership in Advertising’ category at the Women Icon Awards powered by Times Women, India, where she was the only recipient from Sri Lanka in the category. Together, these recognitions highlight her contribution to an industry where effective leadership increasingly calls for commercial strength, adaptability and a commitment to people and purpose.

audit.headline: Bangladesh: At least 187 killed in mob violence in nine months
audit.summary: At least 187 people were killed and 401 injured in 398 incidents of mob violence across Bangladesh in the first nine months of 2026, according to a Human Rights Support Society (HRSS) report. The death toll was more than two-and-a-half times the 73 deaths recorded in political clashes during the same period. The incidents of mob violence reportedly stemmed from allegations of theft, robbery, mugging, rape and hurting religious sentiments, as well as attempts to establish dominance. The report, signed by HRSS Executive Director Ijajul Islam, was compiled using reports from 16 national dailies and the organisation’s investigations. According to the report, 1,013 incidents of political violence left 73 dead and 6,473 injured. Of these, 931 incidents, or 91 percent, involved BNP infighting or clashes with rival parties.

BNP infighting alone accounted for 342 incidents, leaving 40 dead and 2,632 injured. Among the 73 people killed in political violence, 46 were from the BNP, eight from Jamaat-e-Islami and six from the Awami League. (Daily Star)

audit.headline: Brazil’s left-wing President Lula wins fourth term in surprise victory over Flávio Bolsonaro
audit.summary: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva was elected to a fourth term after defeating Senator Flávio Bolsonaro in the runoff of Brazil’s presidential election. With 98.87% of ballot boxes counted, Brazil’s electoral court (TSE) declared Lula mathematically elected. The incumbent president secured 51.76% of the vote against Bolsonaro’s 48.24%, a wider margin than his victory over Flávio’s father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, in 2022. The result came as a surprise, marking the first time since Brazil’s return to democracy that a candidate who lost the first round managed to overturn the result and win the presidency. It followed a massive campaign by Lula’s supporters on social media and street demonstrations that drew hundreds of thousands of people to Brazil’s main cities, including Rio de Janeiro and São Paulo.
audit.body: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva was elected to a fourth term after defeating Senator Flávio Bolsonaro in the runoff of Brazil’s presidential election. With 98.87% of ballot boxes counted, Brazil’s electoral court (TSE) declared Lula mathematically elected. The incumbent president secured 51.76% of the vote against Bolsonaro’s 48.24%, a wider margin than his victory over Flávio’s father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, in 2022. The result came as a surprise, marking the first time since Brazil’s return to democracy that a candidate who lost the first round managed to overturn the result and win the presidency. It followed a massive campaign by Lula’s supporters on social media and street demonstrations that drew hundreds of thousands of people to Brazil’s main cities, including Rio de Janeiro and São Paulo. Election day was also marked by high voter turnout, with the largest drop in abstention between the first and second rounds of a presidential election in democratic elections since 1989. The day, however, was marred by controversy, with Lula’s campaign alleging voter suppression after a shortage of buses left voters struggling to reach polling stations in several cities, including São Paulo and Salvador, in north-eastern Brazil. Flávio Bolsonaro’s campaign also called for an extension of voting hours because of adverse weather conditions in southern Brazil. The Supreme Court eventually extended voting by two hours. Jair Bolsonaro is currently under arrest after being convicted in September 2025 of attempting a coup d’état after losing the 2022 elections against Lula. Lula becomes the first president in Brazilian history to win a fourth term and will remain in office until 2030. BBC

audit.headline: British Airways returns to Sri Lanka after 11 years
audit.summary: British Airways has resumed services to Sri Lanka after an 11-year absence, signalling renewed confidence in the country’s tourism potential and creating fresh opportunities to strengthen trade, business and people-to-people connections between Sri Lanka and the United Kingdom. Speaking at a media round table in Colombo on Saturday (24), British Airways General Manager for South Asia David Wright said the airline’s return reflected its commitment to Sri Lanka and optimism about the country’s prospects. “This is a true demonstration of our commitment and optimism for this incredible country,” Wright said, highlighting the potential of the resumed service to support tourism, trade and closer ties between the two countries. The airline has scheduled three flights a week between London Gatwick and Colombo, with the service forming part of its network expansion for the winter season.
audit.body: British Airways has resumed services to Sri Lanka after an 11-year absence, signalling renewed confidence in the country’s tourism potential and creating fresh opportunities to strengthen trade, business and people-to-people connections between Sri Lanka and the United Kingdom. Speaking at a media round table in Colombo on Saturday (24), British Airways General Manager for South Asia David Wright said the airline’s return reflected its commitment to Sri Lanka and optimism about the country’s prospects. “This is a true demonstration of our commitment and optimism for this incredible country,” Wright said, highlighting the potential of the resumed service to support tourism, trade and closer ties between the two countries. The airline has scheduled three flights a week between London Gatwick and Colombo, with the service forming part of its network expansion for the winter season. Wright said British Airways had been encouraged by the initial market response, noting that demand extended beyond British tourists visiting Sri Lanka to include Sri Lankan travellers heading to the UK, business travellers and people visiting family and friends. Tourism from the UK remains a key consideration in the airline’s business case, given Sri Lanka’s appeal as a destination for international travellers. However, the positive response across different passenger segments also points to the importance of the route for business and personal travel. The airline has introduced a promotional return fare of £225, inclusive of taxes and charges. Wright described the price as a tactical introductory offer available for the next few weeks, adding that the airline would monitor its performance and market response. Explaining the decision to operate from Gatwick rather than Heathrow, Wright said the airline was pleased with the offering available at Gatwick, which serves London and its surrounding areas. He also noted that British Airways was continuing to review its network and adjust operations in response to changing conditions, including the situation in the Middle East. The resumption of the Colombo service comes as Sri Lanka seeks to strengthen international air connectivity and attract more visitors to support tourism earnings and wider economic activity. British Airways’ return is expected to provide travellers with another direct air link between Sri Lanka and the UK, while improving connectivity for tourism, business and family travel. The airline said it was entering an exciting phase of transformation, with a stronger focus on placing customers at the centre of its operations.

audit.headline: Can focused deterrence reduce violent crime?
audit.summary: Police forces face many challenges, as criminal evolve. Mitigating crime requires planning, sufficient police budgets and precise action. It requires bold and practical police leadership- at many levels of operations. Focused deterrence strategies combine law enforcement and community mobilization in an attempt to reduce offending behavior for specific crime types. The British Metropolitan Police, the FBI and other foreign police agencies have found that “focused deterrence strategies” which target organized criminal gangs (by monitoring and evaluating threat levels) can help the police to engage in “preventive” action rather than delayed intervention. Unfortunately, Sri Lanka Police often responds only after a serious crime has taken place.
audit.body: Police forces face many challenges, as criminal evolve. Mitigating crime requires planning, sufficient police budgets and precise action. It requires bold and practical police leadership- at many levels of operations. Focused deterrence strategies combine law enforcement and community mobilization in an attempt to reduce offending behavior for specific crime types. The British Metropolitan Police, the FBI and other foreign police agencies have found that “focused deterrence strategies” which target organized criminal gangs (by monitoring and evaluating threat levels) can help the police to engage in “preventive” action rather than delayed intervention. Unfortunately, Sri Lanka Police often responds only after a serious crime has taken place. In my training sessions to the police and the STF- I have always stressed the need for proactive, preventive and real time intelligence based police duty. L ast week a serious shooting incident occurred in the Soysapura Flats area, where a man was brutally gunned down inside his own restaurant. The shooters who came by car, opened fire with a T-56 assault rifle, firing with rage. They left the crime scene driving amidst traffic and encountered a vehicle malfunction. They then fired at a lorry driver, hoping to stop and take over the vehicle. When that failed, they fired again into the air to intimidate a motorcyclist and stole his motorbike. They fled the scene, just like in an action movie. Interestingly this same restaurant was fired upon in 2020. Today thousands of Sri Lankans are asking where was the police? Indeed law abiding citizens have a right to ask. This article is written in the interest of public safety. Over the past 10 years Sri Lanka has seen an increase in violent gang related shooting. Many such crimes are classified as “revenge killings”- when Organised Crime Gangs (OCG) compete for control of the illegal drug mafia. However this is not a “crime wave”- a distorted term loosely used in mainstream media. This is an increase of violent shootings, among rival drug mafia. It is an increase in the use of automatic (military grade) weapons by organised criminals. It does not mean an increase in all other crimes. It’s an emerging “criminal trend” as organized criminals exploit weaknesses, which have existed for about thirty years. The primary reason for Sri Lanka to face this type of criminal violence is the impact of dirty politics- a sad reality. The Sri Lanka Police was highly politicised. Honest and diligent police officers were not allowed to work due to political interference. These corrupt politicians violated the peoples trust and the law. Secondly the criminal gangs began dealing in drugs, with the support of certain politicians. This is seen often in media reports, of links to key crime figures and corrupt politicians. This is a global trend. The third is the issue of military deserters and their involvement in violent crime. Many police investigations have revealed that military deserters have taken “contracts” to shoot and kill. Such deserters are a disgrace, and tarnish the image of the Armed Forces who fought with courage and altruism to protect Sri Lanka. The final issue is within the Sri Lanka Police itself and will be discussed later in this article. Police forces face many challenges, as criminal evolve. Mitigating crime requires planning, sufficient police budgets and precise action. It requires bold and practical police leadership- at many levels of operations. Focused deterrence strategies combine law enforcement and community mobilisation in an attempt to reduce offending behaviour for specific crime types. The British Metropolitan Police, the FBI and other foreign police agencies have found that “focused deterrence strategies” which target organised criminal gangs (by monitoring and evaluating threat levels) can help the police to engage in “preventive” action rather than delayed intervention. Unfortunately, Sri Lanka Police often responds only after a serious crime has taken place. In my training sessions to the police and the STF- I have always stressed the need for proactive, preventive and real time intelligence based police duty. The present “anti-crime” trend used globally is predictive policing. This means that all local police stations, through systematic analysis of crime (especially firearms and narcotics related) understand and anticipate to a certain extent where the next crime will take place. They will be marked as crime “hot spots” in police operation maps. It is not a 100% accurate prediction but must be seen as a method of “active deterrence”- with a strong police presence. This sends a clear message to criminals and even terrorists that they can’t engage in their desired actions. In countries like USA and UK the police use advanced “crime mapping” data and technology to get a realistic picture of current crime trends. The concept of “predictive” policing requires a strong bond between local residents and police officers. It will also enhance public confidence in the police, which in turn creates a more secure society. Licensed weapons must be periodically monitored. Sri Lanka Police must maintain updated records of weapons missing from police or military armouries and track those weapons as a top priority. This is a serious offence. I have written previously of weapons from the war period (1983-2009) later moving into the hands of criminal gangs across Sri Lanka. Sometimes 1 assault rifle can be passed on between different shooters, of a big crime network. I spoke to SSP Athula Daulagala (retired Deputy Commandant, STF). He is a UK qualified Counter- Terrorism officer who has experience with INTERPOL and UN police missions. He explained” Sri Lanka Police is a very capable force. If focused deterrence is implemented it identifies violent criminal groups. We must integrate incident reports, firearm and ballistic evidence, vehicle details, case histories, warrant status and verified gang relationships into a case-linkage platform. To stop contract-killings we must establish a joint threat-assessment process for credible threats. It’s vital to review threats, prior violence, access to firearms and recent hostile acts. Police must prioritize CCTV cameras at violence prone hotspots and use police drones for incident-scene awareness and search operations. Police must build consistent national firearms tracing and forensic linkage workflows. The objective is not simply to arrest the gunman after a contract killing: but to identify and disrupt the network which ordered, financed, armed and enabled the attack”. Crime identification and analysis are the first steps in determining which crime strategies are prioritized and how police resources are deployed. Our communities need to believe that the police will listen to them. Public trust becomes an important issue. Crime suppression- is a key factor in future police effectiveness. Sri Lanka Police must ensure technology system staffing levels are sufficient (CID and CRD), having the capacity to generate crime data that are actionable, in the “prevention and deterrence” police approach. The police must urgently enhance their capacity to identify dangerous organized crime patterns and future crime trends. Police criminal records data is of less value, if it dosent help crime prevention. Police patrol is typically the largest function in police agencies around the world. In the course of their duties investigating crime and bringing offenders to justice, there is a deterrent effect on future offending. Increasing preventive patrol activities has the potential to reduce crime in large areas. The serious shortage of active duty police, affects police patrolling. Sri Lanka Police must increase patrols, especially at night. It’s sad to see an entire police division covered by just 1 car or 1 jeep with three officers, for night rounds. How can they respond to multiple emergency calls? This creates a serious gap in Public Security measures. Sri Lanka Police must increase their emergency response vehicle fleet as a top priority, with focus on durable motorbikes capable of high speed chase- to intercept criminal shooters. The STF must be given light-armoured vehicles for rapid response in urban areas. I have written before, asking that all police officers on field duty be provided with a walkie-talkie (2 way radio) and side firearm. All traffic policemen must have a handgun- they are always on the street, and become first responders. Citing finances is not valid today. All police gear is an investment in crime prevention and also for the safety of the police officer. Police officers making high profile arrests or engaging in high risk duty need bullet proof vests. The police officers life is important to his family and colleagues. Safety cannot be compromised. Sri Lankan police officers need to carry Taser guns- there is no need for a debate citing culture or religious views. Religion has nothing to do with police duty. Globally, Taser guns (classified as less lethal weapons) are official police gear. It’s better to “destabilize” a violent criminal for a few seconds and arrest him- rather than fatally shooting him and then face human rights court cases. I also spoke to ASP Fredrick Wootler (LLB, Director Police Media Division). He explained “Sri Lanka Police is committed to combating organized crime. Under the guidance of the IGP we have many programmes in action. In October 2025 we began the National Campaign against Narcotics. We want to eradicate narcotic drugs and protect our youth. Under the directives of the IGP we have arrested 42 hardcore drug dealers who were hiding overseas- with assistance from foreign police agencies. We have obtained INTERPOL red notices to arrest and deport another 97 identified Sri Lankan criminals hiding overseas. Illegal assets of criminals have been frozen. From 2025 to date the police and STF have recovered a significant number of illegal weapons.” ASP Wootler also added “Regarding police patrolling, we admit there are some challenges due to the shortage of active duty officers. We try our best to respond to the 119 emergency calls. Our command center receives around 8000 calls per day. However about 5000 calls are not directly related to a police emergency. We kindly ask the public to call this number for genuine police emergency help. Finally the IGP has implemented a special Cordon and Search Unit in all Police Divisions, to rapidly respond to violent crimes and drive by shootings. Police is committed to protect the public. We ask the public to support us with information that will help prevent crime”. The Sri Lanka Police has a proud history of 160 years. The service has faced many challenges and seen its share of tragedies and triumphs. There are thousands of honest and diligent officers who deserve our appreciation. 3100 police officers have bravely died in the line of duty. Thankfully many developments have been made in many police branches, but there is room for strategic development. There must be an overall change in police efficiency and police attitude towards “preventive” policing. This process will take time. The emphasis placed on professionalism, integrity and honesty is important in establishing a service oriented police culture in Sri Lanka. The public must also support the police to combat crime and gun violence. People have an obligation to help protect their communities. When duly empowered and given modern resources and training Sri Lanka Police can rise to face these existing challenges. (The writer is author of Target Secured- Police Special Task Force)

audit.headline: DTNA calls for international investigation into ethnic conflict
audit.summary: Democratic Tamil National Alliance (DTNA) Vanni District MP Selvam Adaikalanathan told Parliament that past Governments have failed to provide any guarantees for the safety of human lives and this remains the case even today. Addressing the House on Friday (23) during the debate on the Bill for the Elimination of Rabies and the Registration of Dogs, he demanded an international investigation into the ethnic conflict and the human rights violations that have occurred, saying the Government’s proposal for an internal investigation cannot be accepted. “In our country, animals like elephants and dogs are accorded more importance than human beings. Past Governments have failed to provide any guarantees for the safety of human lives, and this remains the case even today.
audit.body: Democratic Tamil National Alliance (DTNA) Vanni District MP Selvam Adaikalanathan told Parliament that past Governments have failed to provide any guarantees for the safety of human lives and this remains the case even today. Addressing the House on Friday (23) during the debate on the Bill for the Elimination of Rabies and the Registration of Dogs, he demanded an international investigation into the ethnic conflict and the human rights violations that have occurred, saying the Government’s proposal for an internal investigation cannot be accepted. “In our country, animals like elephants and dogs are accorded more importance than human beings. Past Governments have failed to provide any guarantees for the safety of human lives, and this remains the case even today. Regarding the Chemmani mass grave site specifically, the report submitted by archaeologist Raj Somadeva is inconsistent with the truth. His expertise is limited to soil analysis. It would be possible to conduct a scientific analysis of the human remains ranging from children to adults found buried there to determine exactly what transpired. However, his report offers no basis upon which we can reach any definitive conclusion,’’ he said. Adaikalanathan went on to say that ‘’during the war, military checkpoints were established in numerous locations. Simply managing to pass through one of these checkpoints alive was, in itself, a significant outcome. We witnessed many such incidents firsthand during the conflict. People migrating from Jaffna to the Vanni region, and those returning, were subjected to inspections at military checkpoints such as the one near the coast in Kalmunai. People did not travel alone, they moved in groups. They would be detained and subjected to interrogation, often for periods exceeding ten days. If the military suspected even one or two individuals within a group, they would refuse to release the entire group, fearing that letting them go would pose a security risk. Such was the reality of the situation at that time.’’

audit.headline: Depression in Bay of Bengal to intensify into cyclonic storm
audit.summary: A low-pressure area near the North Andaman Islands has intensified into a depression and is projected to rapidly develop into a severe cyclonic storm by tomorrow (27). While meteorologists expect the storm to bypass Sri Lanka without a direct hit, its associated wind flows will bring increased rainfall, strong winds, and heavy thundershowers to broad sections of the country. According to the Meteorology Department, the system moving west-northwestward, is expected to strengthen into a deep depression over the east-central and adjoining southeast Bay of Bengal. It is forecasted to intensify into a cyclonic storm by morning today (26) and reach severe cyclonic storm status over the west-central Bay of Bengal by tomorrow (27) morning.
audit.body: A low-pressure area near the North Andaman Islands has intensified into a depression and is projected to rapidly develop into a severe cyclonic storm by tomorrow (27). While meteorologists expect the storm to bypass Sri Lanka without a direct hit, its associated wind flows will bring increased rainfall, strong winds, and heavy thundershowers to broad sections of the country. According to the Meteorology Department, the system moving west-northwestward, is expected to strengthen into a deep depression over the east-central and adjoining southeast Bay of Bengal. It is forecasted to intensify into a cyclonic storm by morning today (26) and reach severe cyclonic storm status over the west-central Bay of Bengal by tomorrow (27) morning. Although direct impacts are unlikely, the system’s extending wind profile is expected to enhance rainfall, particularly across the southwestern parts of the country. Showers or thundershowers will occur across the Western, Sabaragamuwa, Southern, North Western, and Northern Provinces, as well as the Kandy, Nuwara -Eliya, and Anuradhapura Districts. Heavy rainfall exceeding 100 mm is likely at isolated locations in these regions. In the Uva Province, along with the Ampara and Batticaloa Districts, scattered showers or thundershowers are expected to develop after 1:00 pm. Fairly strong winds ranging between 40 and 50 km/h are anticipated over the western slopes of the Central Hills, the Northern, North Central, and North Western Provinces, as well as the Trincomalee, Hambantota, and Matale Districts. Disaster management authorities and the Meteorology Department advise the public to take necessary precautions to safeguard against damage caused by temporary localised strong winds and severe lightning during thundershowers.

audit.headline: HNB FINANCE, Toyota Lanka forge partnership to expand vehicle-leasing solutions
audit.summary: HNB FINANCE PLC and Toyota Lanka (Private) Limited have entered into a partnership to offer competitive leasing solutions for customers purchasing brand-new Toyota vehicles and Toyota Sure Certified Used Vehicles. The partnership was recently formalised through a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU), reinforcing the commitment of both parties to collaborate on this initiative. Under the agreement, HNB FINANCE will provide leasing facilities for eligible Toyota customers, combining access to formal financing with a package of after-sales and ownership benefits offered by Toyota Lanka. HNB FINANCE Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer Chaminda Prabhath said the partnership supports the company’s focus on widening access to structured vehicle financing.
audit.body: HNB FINANCE PLC and Toyota Lanka (Private) Limited have entered into a partnership to offer competitive leasing solutions for customers purchasing brand-new Toyota vehicles and Toyota Sure Certified Used Vehicles. The partnership was recently formalised through a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU), reinforcing the commitment of both parties to collaborate on this initiative. Under the agreement, HNB FINANCE will provide leasing facilities for eligible Toyota customers, combining access to formal financing with a package of after-sales and ownership benefits offered by Toyota Lanka. HNB FINANCE Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer Chaminda Prabhath said the partnership supports the company’s focus on widening access to structured vehicle financing. “Reliable access to vehicle finance is important not only for individual mobility, but also for business activity and broader economic participation. Through this partnership with Toyota Lanka, we are looking to offer customers competitive financing options together with the assurance of a globally recognised automotive brand and strong after-sales support,” Prabhath said. He added that HNB FINANCE would continue to strengthen financing solutions that are more accessible, convenient and responsive to changing customer needs. Customers purchasing eligible Toyota vehicles under the partnership will receive free vehicle registration from Toyota Lanka, along with a comprehensive warranty covering the engine and gearbox for three years or 100,000 kilometres, whichever comes first. Toyota forklift customers will receive a warranty of two years or 6,000 operating hours, whichever occurs first. The partnership also offers three complimentary services for Toyota vehicles and three complimentary labour services for Toyota forklifts.The MoU was exchanged in the presence of senior representatives of both companies. Toyota Lanka was represented by Chairman Masaaki Kawabata and Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer Manohara Atukorala. HNB FINANCE was represented by Managing Director/CEO Chaminda Prabhath, Deputy General Manager/Chief Credit Officer Aruna Somasiri, Assistant General Manager/Head of Channel Management Pathum Sampath, Head of Leasing Saman Premarathna, Chief Manager/Head of Marketing Communications and Digital Business Madura Wijeratne and Senior Manager – Marketing RuwanIndika.

audit.headline: Initiative to recruit qualified, skilled personnel into education system – PM
audit.summary: Prime Minister, Education, Higher Education and Vocational Education Minister Dr. Harini Amarasuriya stated that a formal procedure is being developed not only to improve infrastructure in schools but also to recruit qualified and skilled personnel into the education system. The Prime Minister made these remarks while participating in the ceremony to hand over the newly constructed two-storey building at Kadawalawawa Maha Vidyalaya to students on Saturday (24). The Government has invested nearly Rs. 55 million in the construction of this building, which comprises eight primary classrooms. Following the opening ceremony, attended by the Prime Minister, she engaged in a cordial conversation with students and visited the classrooms.
audit.body: Prime Minister, Education, Higher Education and Vocational Education Minister Dr. Harini Amarasuriya stated that a formal procedure is being developed not only to improve infrastructure in schools but also to recruit qualified and skilled personnel into the education system. The Prime Minister made these remarks while participating in the ceremony to hand over the newly constructed two-storey building at Kadawalawawa Maha Vidyalaya to students on Saturday (24). The Government has invested nearly Rs. 55 million in the construction of this building, which comprises eight primary classrooms. Following the opening ceremony, attended by the Prime Minister, she engaged in a cordial conversation with students and visited the classrooms. Addressing the occasion, the Prime Minister stated: “The primary objective of the education reforms we are implementing from this year is to nurture citizens equipped with knowledge, skills and values. Until now, our education system has only placed emphasis on imparting knowledge to children and preparing them for examinations. However, what we want is to nurture a generation of children who can apply the knowledge they acquire in practical situations, solve problems in society and create innovations. In order to achieve this, we are implementing a range of initiatives, including the introduction of new curricula, teacher training and the development of school infrastructure. We also expect to make an investment in transforming education in 2027. We are also working to further strengthen the education system by resuming teacher and principal recruitment, which had been delayed for many years, while giving priority to skills and competencies. The greatest hope of parents is to provide their children with a good education and enable them to progress further than they themselves have. Therefore, while easing the burden borne by parents in providing their children with an education, the Government must also take responsibility for a share of that commitment. Our children possess talents and abilities. Our aim is to provide them with the opportunities they need to develop these talents and contribute to the future development of the country. It is with this objective that we are implementing these education reforms”. Housing, Construction and Water Supply Deputy Minister T. B. Sarath, Polonnaruwa district MP Padmasiri Bandara, Polonnaruwa Municipal Council Mayor Lalith Tissa Kumara and Polonnaruwa Pradeshiya Sabha Chairman Wasantha Kumara attended the occasion. Provincial and zonal education officials, principals, teachers, parents and students were also present.

audit.headline: Iranian plots to kill US officials in Middle East have reached ‘advanced stages,’ intel memo warns
audit.summary: Iran has increased efforts to target U.S. personnel in the Middle East and other countries, according to a memo sent by the Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton to Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Friday. The memo warned that “the lethal plotting efforts by the Iranians against U.S. citizens have reached advanced stages.” A U.S. official confirmed the authenticity of the memo first reported by Axios. The intelligence comes days after sources told NBC News the U.S. military has been quietly scaling back its troop presence at bases across the Middle East. The State Department ordered a further reduction in staff at multiple diplomatic posts in the region, including in Lebanon, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar and Jordan, according to a State Department official.
audit.body: Iran has increased efforts to target U.S. personnel in the Middle East and other countries, according to a memo sent by the Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton to Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Friday. The memo warned that “the lethal plotting efforts by the Iranians against U.S. citizens have reached advanced stages.” A U.S. official confirmed the authenticity of the memo first reported by Axios. The intelligence comes days after sources told NBC News the U.S. military has been quietly scaling back its troop presence at bases across the Middle East. The State Department ordered a further reduction in staff at multiple diplomatic posts in the region, including in Lebanon, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar and Jordan, according to a State Department official. Those posts have already been placed on a “restricted operations” status and have been functioning with limited staffing since the start of the war. Clayton told Rubio in the memo that the risk is “relevant to more individuals than are currently cleared to receive this information,” adding: “We will make every effort to downgrade as much intelligence as possible so you can share it with State Department personnel at your discretion.” The reduction of American forces and diplomatic personnel is similar to drawdowns at bases and embassies that the Defence Department and the State Department initiated around the start of the war with Iran in February. “When it comes to our staffing at embassies, we constantly evaluate new information about the security environment,” a U.S. official said. “The threat of Houthi attacks and of Iranian terror plots targeting U.S. officials are informing our decisions on staffing adjustments for embassies on Restricted Status in the region.” (NBC)

audit.headline: Lanka’s Asian Para Heroes return home today
audit.summary: After a successful Asian Para Games in Nagoya Japan Sri Lankan medal winners are scheduled to return home today (26) evening. 21-year-old Janani Dhananjana was the most successful Sri Lankan Para athlete this time around with the silver medal in T – 47 200m and the gold medal with a new games record in T47 long jump. Dhanajana entered the long-jump competition following an impressive performance in the women’s T-47 200m final, where she clocked a personal-best time of 25.80 seconds to claim the silver medal. The silver-medal finish was particularly significant because the 200m race was Dhanajana’s first international appearance in the event. She has shown her ability to adapt to a new competitive challenge and immediately contend for a medal at one of Asia’s biggest Para sport competitions.
audit.body: After a successful Asian Para Games in Nagoya Japan Sri Lankan medal winners are scheduled to return home today (26) evening. 21-year-old Janani Dhananjana was the most successful Sri Lankan Para athlete this time around with the silver medal in T – 47 200m and the gold medal with a new games record in T47 long jump. Dhanajana entered the long-jump competition following an impressive performance in the women’s T-47 200m final, where she clocked a personal-best time of 25.80 seconds to claim the silver medal. The silver-medal finish was particularly significant because the 200m race was Dhanajana’s first international appearance in the event. She has shown her ability to adapt to a new competitive challenge and immediately contend for a medal at one of Asia’s biggest Para sport competitions. Janani Dhananjana, the most successful Sri Lankan Para athlete with Paralympic High Performance Committee Head Lt Colonel Deepal Herath From her debut 200m silver into a gold-medal performance in her key event long jump with a 5.52m leap established a new Asian Para Games record in the women’s T47 long jump, underlining her ability to deliver on the continental stage. The head of the Para Athletes High Performance Committee and immediate President of the National Paralympic Committee Lt Colonel Deepal Herath said; “I was lucky to witness young Dhananjana’s performance in this Asian Para Games. She has improved a lot in her sprint and long jump event both”. She won the silver medal in the women’s T-47 long jump with a distance of 4.89 metres at previous Asian Para Games in Hangzhou, China, in 2023. Her improvement from 4.89m in Hangzhou to 5.52m in Aichi-Nagoya shows an increase of 63 centimetres. The progress reflects her development since her previous appearance at the continental championship and culminates in a record-breaking gold medal,” added former President of the NPC. Her back to back medals in Asian Para Games give big boost to her future International events and she is already focused on next Paralympics. Meanwhile middle distance athlete Pradeep Somasiri led Sri Lanka’s medal-winning performances with a historic victory in the men’s T-46 1500m, clocking 4:03.25 to claim the gold and established a new Games Record. His outstanding performance further confirmed his position among Asia’s leading Para athletes in the event. Somasiri’s latest triumph was particularly significant as he had also won the gold in the same event at the 2023 Asian Para Games in Hangzhou, China, where he set a Games Record of 4:05.14. His performance in Nagoya improved that previous mark by 1.89 seconds, demonstrating his continued progress at the highest level of Asian Para athletics. Apart from the two gold medals Sri Lankan won 4 silver and 3 bronze medals to bag 9 medals. Nuwan Indika Gamage added a silver medal to Sri Lanka’s tally in the men’s T44 100m, recording a season’s best time of 11.58 seconds. Although he could not repeat his gold-medal achievement from Hangzhou, Indika’s performance highlighted his continued competitiveness at the Asian level. Sri Lanka’s Galina Basanayake secured the silver medal in the women’s S9 Freestyle swimming final at the Asian Para Games 2026, clocking an impressive time of 4:59.58. She improved significantly on her previous timing of 5:08.47, reducing it by 8.89 seconds. Naveed Rasheen won the bronze medal in the S9 100m Butterfly stroke with a time of 1:03.29 seconds. Sri Lanka fielded 20 Para athletes for this Asian Para Games and won nine medals including two gold, four silver and three bronze medals giving real boost to Para athletes. Sri Lanka also narrowly missed 3-4 medals and this is also a good inspiration for them. Especially Sri Lankans finished at 16th place at the Medal Table while China ranked on top with 435 medals including 207 golds followed by Japan (64 golds) and Uzbekistan (45 golds). Sri Lanka’s medal winners at Asian Para Games 2026: Janani Dhananjana T-47 long jump gold and T- 47 200m silver, Pradeep Somasiri T-46 1500m gold, Palitha Bandara F-42 shot put silver, Nuwan Indika T-44 100m silver, Galina Basnayake women’s 400m freestyle S9 silver, Mohammad Safran T-47 long jump bronze, Maduranga Subasinghe T-47 400m bronze, Naveed Rasheen men’s 100m Butterfly S9 bronze

audit.headline: Learning from the war
audit.summary: In early 2026 Sri Lankans were lucky, in contrast to other countries that had suppliers on the other side of Hormuz. The country’s largest LPG distributor had entered into a contract that sourced supplies from the US. The closure of the Strait had no impact. It is reported that the new contract is with a supplier from Oman. Good to go with the lowest-cost supplier in terms of cost, insurance and freight (CIF). But should we not contract more than one supplier in the current volatile environment, even if some of the supply is more expensive? That is what derisking means. T he world would be in a better place had President Trump not attacked Iran; had he not torn up the 2015 Iran nuclear agreement, formally known as the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action (JCPOA), an agreement between Iran and several world powers, including the United States.
audit.body: In early 2026 Sri Lankans were lucky, in contrast to other countries that had suppliers on the other side of Hormuz. The country’s largest LPG distributor had entered into a contract that sourced supplies from the US. The closure of the Strait had no impact. It is reported that the new contract is with a supplier from Oman. Good to go with the lowest-cost supplier in terms of cost, insurance and freight (CIF). But should we not contract more than one supplier in the current volatile environment, even if some of the supply is more expensive? That is what derisking means. T he world would be in a better place had President Trump not attacked Iran; had he not torn up the 2015 Iran nuclear agreement, formally known as the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action (JCPOA), an agreement between Iran and several world powers, including the United States. But these things were done and the world is in a bad place. As a small country with no diplomatic clout, we must live with the fallout. We have no alternative but to adjust. We can also learn. Many lessons can be learned, but here the focus is on the learnings for how to approach the import of essential inputs: energy and fertiliser. The most important lesson is that we must deriskenergy and fertiliser imports. Self-sufficiency is a familiar slogan that warms our hearts. But it is unrealistic for a modern populace with complex needs. There was a time we went to sleep early,turning off the Petromax lamp (in my case an Aladdin),and cooked using firewood. That world cannot be brought back. Across the country, only 1.6 percent of households used kerosene for lighting; 98 percent relied on the grid, according to the 2024 Census. Among urban dwellers 82.1 percent cook with gas. Gas shortages in the urban areas triggered the 2022 protests.Even more striking is the change between 2012 and 2024 for rural dwellers and those listed as estate-rural. In the case of the rural, it increased from 11.6 to 35.1 percent, more than threefold. In the estates, the increase was close to fivefold: 3.7 to 15.3 percent. We should be happy that more women are protected from damage to their lungs. But the Government should be keenly aware of the consequences of depriving families of the ability to cook their food. For the 2026 Yala season, there were some shortfalls in the NPK [Nitrogen, Phosphorus, Potassium] fertiliser supply, but the bulk had been purchased before the war started. Theharvest decreased only by 12.8 percent from the 2025 Yala yield. Rice wasprioritised over other crops. Reports of declines in tea production are coming in. Fertiliser supplies for the more important Maha season are said to be significantly short. When President Gotabaya Rajapaksa banned chemical fertiliser overnight in 2021, rice harvests dropped by 32 percent, tea production fell by 18 percent, and the resulting agricultural collapse triggered widespread food insecurity and economic losses, including an estimated USD 425 millionloss in tea exports alone. Five years later, the decline in nutrition has not been fully reversed. Sri Lanka imports almost all the fertiliser that supplies NPK in absorbable form. Single Super Phosphate (SSP) production started in 2026. Sri Lanka was significantly dependent on fertiliser shipped through the Strait of Hormuz (36 percent, according to UNCTAD) but obtained more from China (more than 50 percent, according to 2025 Customs data). There is already significant derisking. Increasing refinery capacity with just the Sri Lankan market in mind is not the solution for energy security. India and China have massive refineries (one of them can supply all of Sri Lanka’s requirements and have output left), but their dependence takes a different form: not refined product but crude oil. The Sapugaskanda refinery is uneconomical and inadequate. The solution is not expending taxpayer money to upgrade it or even doing it through a Public Private Partnership (PPP). Modern, efficient refineries are massive, have lower unit costs than this 1970s plant. Best would be to build a refinery that optimises economies of scale. Such a plant can supply part of the domestic demand and export. The quantum of the domestic take-up obligation is what appears to have stalled the Sinopec refinery project in Hambantota. Ideally, Sinopec should not receive a guaranteed domestic quota. They can use their cost advantages to supply one or more of the distributors through competitive bidding. Proximity of the refinery to the Hambantota Port and thereby to a major sea lane are massive advantages. India’s IOC, the parent of Lanka IOC, does not wish to build a refinery here. It wants to develop Trincomalee as a regional energy centre under the Sri Lanka-India-UAE energy framework. A pipeline across the Palk Strait that would allow low-costimports is the key element. One spur would go to the storage tanks in Trinco and the other would come down to Colombo where most of the domestic demand is. The costs of building the storage (Trinco’s ancient oil tanks need a lot of work) and the costs of storage (keeping fuel unsold is not costless) would be in the hands of LIOC. But just the pipeline and the refurbished tanks will not make an energy centre. The jetty would have to be rebuilt to accommodate vessels of the appropriate size. It would be ideal if all this can be done with minimal impact on the Treasury and with no guaranteed domestic purchases. Ceylon Petroleum Storage and Terminals Company (CPSTL) must be rescued from its current dysfunctional state and restructured so that common facilities can be expanded and cannot be used to distort the market. An empowered independent regulator must have authority over the pricing of and access to common facilities.The Government must allow distributors, including the state-owned Ceypetco, to operate as commercial entities. Subsidies, if any, must be targeted, time-bound, and competitively neutral.Formula-based pricing should be designed to prevent the passing costs of inefficiency and corruption through to captive consumers and used very sparingly, perhaps only for the major supplier. A policy approach centred on deriskingthe supply of fuel will not seek to chase out the private-sector distributors. The proposals to restore Ceypetco’s dominance are short-sighted. To go along with self-serving union suggestions is to ignore the lessons of 2021-22 where Ceypetcocould notmobilise payments or bank credit necessary for uninterrupted imports. Investing in the electricity grid to make it possible to efficiently absorb more renewables should be a priority. Streamlining approvals for wind and solar farms will complement the build out of the grid to the remote locations where they will be sited. Ideally, the investors in wind or solar will also be permitted to invest in the grid extensions. What will be allowed will be seen once the Final Transfer Plan for the CEB successor companies is approved. The best way to reduce reliance on fossil fuel is to generate more of the electricity that is used by industry and by households from wind and solar sources. If we can move the transport sector which is the biggest consumer of imported oilto electricity, the combined result would be a massive reduction of the risks associated with imported fossil fuel. It is true that the solar panels would still have to be imported from China and the wind turbines from India, which one may argue are still forms of dependency. But that dependency is qualitatively better than dependence on the next diesel or LPG or coal shipment.Solar and wind equipment are one-off purchases. If we reach or exceed the target of 70 percent of electricity from renewable sources and ensure that the grid is stable (this means significant investments in the grid), the focus can then shift to reducing the use of petrol and diesel in transportation. The best way is to develop public transportation, not increase the number of electric vehicles on the roads, though that cannot be avoided in the medium term. Beyond diversifying sources of fertiliser imports, it would be good to use the Eppawala Phosphate deposit, starting from the manufacture of Single Super Phosphate this year. India’s promotion of slow-release fertiliser is worthy of emulation. Lowest cost can no longer be the sole consideration in deciding how essential inputs are obtained. The prudent course of action in the current international context is to always give greater weight toderisking by diversifying sources and ensuring that action is taken to reduce the vulnerabilities caused by known chokepoints or single points of failure, including state monopolies.

audit.headline: Ministry issues urgent alert over critical global PHP vulnerabilities
audit.summary: In response to an escalating worldwide cybersecurity threat, the Digital Economy Ministry has ordered government institutions to take immediate, emergency action to secure critical vulnerabilities found in the widely used PHP software framework commonly used to develop websites and web applications, following an official statement issued by Sri Lanka CERT. In a formal circular, the Ministry warned that the vulnerabilities, tracked globally as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, pose a severe risk of unauthorised system access, data theft, and catastrophic operational disruption. The directive mandates swift compliance across all ministries, Provincial Councils, independent commissions, government departments, State corporations, statutory bodies, and government-owned enterprises.
audit.body: In response to an escalating worldwide cybersecurity threat, the Digital Economy Ministry has ordered government institutions to take immediate, emergency action to secure critical vulnerabilities found in the widely used PHP software framework commonly used to develop websites and web applications, following an official statement issued by Sri Lanka CERT. In a formal circular, the Ministry warned that the vulnerabilities, tracked globally as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, pose a severe risk of unauthorised system access, data theft, and catastrophic operational disruption. The directive mandates swift compliance across all ministries, Provincial Councils, independent commissions, government departments, State corporations, statutory bodies, and government-owned enterprises. The local warning comes against the backdrop of a high global threat level surrounding these vulnerabilities. Rated with critical CVSS severity scores, the security flaws have triggered millions of automated exploitation attempts worldwide. Cybersecurity monitoring agencies globally report active target scanning of unpatched web infrastructure, forcing governments and enterprise networks across multiple continents to temporarily restrict internet access to sensitive portals while applying urgent emergency fixes. To mitigate the threat locally, the Ministry has instructed state agencies to immediately audit all digital applications to identify running PHP versions and follow the official update instructions available at www.php.net. In addition, IT administrators must thoroughly examine system logs for suspicious activity and isolate or disconnect any high-risk internet-facing systems that cannot be patched immediately. As an additional measure, GovTech Sri Lanka, which operates under the Digital Economy Ministry, has developed a vulnerability detection tool to help identify PHP-related security weaknesses in websites. The tool is available at www.govtech.lk/cvesecure. Technical personnel responsible for relevant websites are encouraged to use this facility to check for potential vulnerabilities and seek technical assistance from Sri Lanka CERT where necessary. Technical teams across all public sector organisations are expected to run scans using this facility and work in close coordination with Sri Lanka CERT to resolve weaknesses and protect the country’s digital infrastructure. Government institutions are urged to treat this matter as a priority and take the necessary corrective measures promptly to protect their digital infrastructure, safeguard information assets and minimise the risk of cyber incidents. For further information and technical assistance, the following contacts are available: GovTech Sri Lanka on 011 249 7900, Email: samithnp@govtech.lk, Website: www.govtech.lk/cvesecure and Sri Lanka CERTon 011 269 1692 and Email: info@ncsoc.gov.lk. PHP (Hypertext Preprocessor) is an open-source programming language used to build websites and web applications. Created in the early 1990s, it works behind the scenes on web servers. When you visit a website, PHP processes information on the server and builds the dynamic page you see on your screen. It is currently maintained by the PHP Foundation, a non-profit organisation dedicated to keeping the language updated and reliable. PHP remains a major backbone of the internet today; it powers roughly 70 percent of all websites, including Wikipedia, online shopping stores, and WordPress. Developers also rely on popular PHP-based tools and frameworks like Laravel, Symfony, and Drupal to build software faster. However, cybersecurity researchers at Wiz and Calif recently discovered two major security flaws (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) built into PHP versions released over the last decade. Rated a critical 9.2 out of 10 in severity, these flaws could allow hackers to take complete control of vulnerable web servers and steal private data across millions of exposed websites. Authorities in Europe, Asia and other continents have temporarily taken some government websites offline to protect against newly discovered security vulnerabilities in PHP. Vulnerabilities in the PHP programming language prompted a rare public warning from the United States National Security Agency (NSA), which advised taking websites offline if they could not be updated immediately.

audit.headline: Namal Rajapaksa marks 50 days in jail
audit.summary: Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna (SLPP) MP Namal Rajapaksa has accused the Government of using his detention to divert attention from pressing economic and social grievances, marking the 50th day of his imprisonment with an open letter released from Parliament. In the letter dated October 23, the eldest son of former President Mahinda Rajapaksa framed his incarceration as a political distraction during a period of widespread public hardship. He questioned Government claims of economic stability, noting that citizens have yet to receive meaningful relief despite assertions of a recovering treasury. “Although prison walls surround me, I know that beyond those walls stands a wall of people,” Rajapaksa wrote, adding that he would willingly accept 500 days in prison if it guaranteed lower utility costs, reduced taxes on essential goods, and tangible public relief.

He questioned Government claims of economic stability, noting that citizens have yet to receive meaningful relief despite assertions of a recovering treasury. “Although prison walls surround me, I know that beyond those walls stands a wall of people,” Rajapaksa wrote, adding that he would willingly accept 500 days in prison if it guaranteed lower utility costs, reduced taxes on essential goods, and tangible public relief. The Parliamentarian maintained his innocence, stating he expects full acquittal by the courts. He also used the statement to praise his father’s political legacy, express concern over the country’s cultural and natural heritage, and caution against public discourse that insults religious traditions. Concluding his message, Rajapaksa asserted that while he remains behind bars, his detention cannot suppress the aspirations of his political supporters.

audit.headline: Narcotics with street value of Rs. 97 Bn seized this year
audit.summary: Deputy Defence Minister Major General Aruna Jayasekara (Retd) noted that over the past year, joint efforts by the Navy and Coast Guard have led to the seizure of narcotics with an estimated street value of Rs. 97 billion. He added that joint operations involving the Armed Forces, Police, PNB, Special Task Force, and local and foreign intelligence agencies will continue to prevent narcotics from entering the country. The Deputy Minister urged the public to support law enforcement agencies by sharing information through the dedicated hotlines 1818 or 1997, while acknowledging the role played by the media in raising public awareness about substance abuse. He was addressing the media following the seizure of over 475kg of methamphetamine and heroin at Naotunna beach, Thalalla on Saturday.
audit.body: Deputy Defence Minister Major General Aruna Jayasekara (Retd) noted that over the past year, joint efforts by the Navy and Coast Guard have led to the seizure of narcotics with an estimated street value of Rs. 97 billion. He added that joint operations involving the Armed Forces, Police, PNB, Special Task Force, and local and foreign intelligence agencies will continue to prevent narcotics from entering the country. The Deputy Minister urged the public to support law enforcement agencies by sharing information through the dedicated hotlines 1818 or 1997, while acknowledging the role played by the media in raising public awareness about substance abuse. He was addressing the media following the seizure of over 475kg of methamphetamine and heroin at Naotunna beach, Thalalla on Saturday. The Sri Lanka Navy and Coast Guard seized 21 sacks and travel bags containing over 475kg of methamphetamine (Ice) and heroin during a joint operation conducted in the coastal area of Naotunna in Thalalla, Matara. The coordinated operation was mounted following credible information received by the Sri Lanka Coast Guard. During the operation, search teams recovered 10 sacks and 11 travel bags suspected of containing narcotics, on the beach, alongside a dinghy believed to have been used to smuggle the consignment. Subsequent examinations conducted with the assistance of the Police Narcotic Bureau (PNB) confirmed the presence of over 200kg of Ice in 200 packages and over 257kg of heroin in 275 packs. The seized narcotics and the dinghy will be handed over to the PNB for further legal proceedings. Public Security Minister Ananda Wijepala and along with Navy Commander Vice Admiral Damian Fernando, Southern Naval Area Commander Rear Admiral HNS Perera, Sri Lanka Coast Guard Director General Rear Admiral Ruwan Rupasena and Operations Director General Rear Admiral Chaminda Karunasena were also present to inspect the seized narcotic consignment.
