audit.body: T he Cabinet has approved the introduction of a new law to promote public-private partnership enterprises. The law provides the necessary legal framework for their operation, and establish the National Agency for Public-Private Partnership Enterprises. This Bill is important specifically in terms of Sri Lanka’s health service. The private healthcare is prohibitively expensive and beyond the reach of many people. Since the economic crisis that hit Sri Lanka in early and mid-2022, charges across the private healthcare sector have seen an unimaginable rise. Private hospitals and other private healthcare institutions have continued to impose exorbitant fees on patients. The cost of various services provided by private hospitals has increased significantly since the COVID-19 pandemic and the economic crisis. There is a considerable gap between the actual cost of providing these services and the prices charged to patients. The Government needs to address this disparity through strict regulation of private hospitals. Effective regulation, alongside public-private partnerships, could offer a way forward. Different private hospitals charge widely varying prices for the same service. For example, a CT scan of the head costs between Rs. 29,790 and Rs. 49,850 at different private hospitals. The difference exceeds Rs. 20,000 and is close to Rs. 25,000. Such disparities raise questions about pricing practices in the private healthcare sector and underline the need for greater transparency and effective regulation. Five or six years ago, a patient admitted to a private hospital for a relatively minor illness, such as flu, would receive a total bill of around Rs. 100,000 to Rs. 200,000 for a stay of about three days. Certain outpatient procedures, including minor surgery and medical tests, cost less than Rs. 100,000. Today, however, patients may have to pay more than Rs. 100,000 a day for hospital services alone, excluding treatment costs. With treatment included, the bill can rise to Rs. 300,000 or Rs. 400,000. A hospital stay of a few days, without surgery or complicated treatment, can now cost close to or more than Rs. 1 million. With even minor surgery and medical treatment, the total can exceed Rs. 1.5 million. The procedure to crush kidney stones, including a 24-hour hospital stay, costs more than Rs. 500,000. The bed linen in some private hospitals seems to cost more than if it were made of gold! What needs to be done is to make private healthcare affordable to ordinary people through partnerships involving State hospitals and other institutions. This could provide a practical way for lower-middle-class families to access private healthcare, particularly inpatient treatment, without facing an unbearable financial burden. The establishment of private wards in State hospitals has long been a dream of the lower-middle class. The proposed Bill could help turn that dream into reality by creating a framework for public-private partnerships in healthcare. What ordinary Sri Lankans, particularly those in the lower-middle-income group, are asking for is simple: access to private medical care at an affordable price. Another sector that could benefit from public-private partnerships is the railway service. Sri Lanka Railways (SLR), formerly known as the Ceylon Government Railway, is a government department operating under the Ministry of Transport. Its broad-gauge network spans approximately 1,436 to 1,508 kilometres across 10 main and branch lines radiating from Colombo. The State-run service operates around 396 trains daily and carries more than 3.7 million passengers, despite severe overcrowding during peak hours, ageing infrastructure and the ongoing restoration of lines damaged by disasters. Its operating fleet includes approximately 72 locomotives, 78 power sets and 565 passenger carriages. Whenever there is a railway strike, a train delay or a cancellation, passengers voice their frustration. Some would even for the complete privatisation of the service. Public-private partnerships could offer an alternative way to improve Sri Lanka’s railway service. This proposed Act could provide the legal framework needed to facilitate such an initiative. There are several ways in which private-sector participation could help improve the service without necessarily transferring the entire railway network to private ownership. Private companies could be permitted to advertise on trains and contribute towards upgrading carriages and facilities. The number of first- and second-class compartments could be increased, with fares adjusted to reflect the improved facilities while keeping ordinary travel affordable. At present, many trains are in poor condition, with broken window shutters, defective fans and damaged hand straps for standing passengers. There are also insufficient first- and second-class compartments on many services, while cleanliness remains a serious concern. With appropriate agreements and effective oversight, private-sector investment could help address these shortcomings, improve passenger comfort and maintain better standards of cleanliness and maintenance. A well-planned public-private partnership could therefore help bring Sri Lanka’s railway service up to a standard that passengers deserve.

audit.headline: Over 1,000 arrested as clashes follow another day of mass protests across France
audit.summary: Over 1,000 arrests were made as hundreds of thousands of people took part in another day of protests across France, which were followed by some clashes late on Saturday, officials have said. After a day of largely peaceful demonstrations, Police fired tear gas and water cannon to disperse protesters in a number of cities including Paris, while barricades were set alight in Marseille and people ripped boards from a shop in Bordeaux. But officials have so far managed to avoid rioting and looting on the scale seen last weekend, which resulted in some of the worst scenes of disorder in France’s modern history. The Interior Ministry said an estimated 410,000 people protested on Saturday, while the unions put the number at about 800,000.
audit.body: Over 1,000 arrests were made as hundreds of thousands of people took part in another day of protests across France, which were followed by some clashes late on Saturday, officials have said. After a day of largely peaceful demonstrations, Police fired tear gas and water cannon to disperse protesters in a number of cities including Paris, while barricades were set alight in Marseille and people ripped boards from a shop in Bordeaux. But officials have so far managed to avoid rioting and looting on the scale seen last weekend, which resulted in some of the worst scenes of disorder in France’s modern history. The Interior Ministry said an estimated 410,000 people protested on Saturday, while the unions put the number at about 800,000. Some 70,000 Police officers were deployed and restrictions imposed in several cities to prevent the latest protests over the Cost of Living and poor school conditions from descending into the kind of chaos which saw officers outnumbered, hundreds of businesses looted and buildings torched. President Emmanuel Macron had decreed earlier this week that only demonstrations organised by a recognised trade unions would be permitted. Hundreds of people have been jailed for vandalism, arson and looting after fast-track court hearings in recent days. (BBC)

audit.headline: Paddler Senura qualifies for World Championship
audit.summary: Senura Silva became the first ever Sri Lankan to qualify for the ITTF World TT Championship 2027 in Kazakhstan. The 21-year-Senura who won the National title in 2020, is currently based in the USA, where he has been performing well in Major League Table Tennis. He returned to Sri Lanka side after laps of 4 years for the recently concluded Asian Table Championships, which played in Tashkent, Uzbekistan. Senura was a member of the four-member men’s team and he beat Hong Kong opponent in a hard fought 3-2 game. It was the men’s singles position 17-32 match and his performance paved the way to qualify for World TT Championship. The eldest son of former National Champion Deepika Radrigo and Indika Prasad came up with best performance among Sri Lankans at the Asian Championship.

audit.headline: Police advise caution when interacting with strangers online
audit.summary: A rising wave of financial fraud linked to online dating applications and messaging platforms has prompted Police to issue an urgent warning, calling on the public to exercise extreme caution when interacting with strangers online. Cybercriminals are increasingly using persuasive messages and deceptive tactics to exploit victims financially. Fraudsters frequently initiate contact on popular social media and messaging services, including Facebook, WhatsApp, and Telegram. Under the guise of seeking friendship, romance, marriage, or offering companionship, these individuals spend time building trust with their targets before launching sophisticated financial scams. A particularly alarming trend involves the distribution of malicious Android application package (APK) files masquerading as legitimate dating apps.
audit.body: A rising wave of financial fraud linked to online dating applications and messaging platforms has prompted Police to issue an urgent warning, calling on the public to exercise extreme caution when interacting with strangers online. Cybercriminals are increasingly using persuasive messages and deceptive tactics to exploit victims financially. Fraudsters frequently initiate contact on popular social media and messaging services, including Facebook, WhatsApp, and Telegram. Under the guise of seeking friendship, romance, marriage, or offering companionship, these individuals spend time building trust with their targets before launching sophisticated financial scams. A particularly alarming trend involves the distribution of malicious Android application package (APK) files masquerading as legitimate dating apps. Scammers often pressure or persuade victims to download and install these unfamiliar files from shared links under the promise of face-to-face meetings or deeper romantic connections. Once installed, the hidden malware compromises the victim’s mobile device, allowing perpetrators to monitor online activity, steal login credentials, and gain unauthorised access to bank accounts. Criminals then use this access to siphon funds and execute fraudulent transactions without the account holder’s knowledge, Police issuing a statement said. Authorities emphasise that safeguarding personal assets requires constant vigilance and sound judgment. Members of the public are strongly advised against downloading unknown applications, clicking suspicious links, or transferring money at the request of unverified online contacts. Furthermore, sensitive financial details, such as account passwords, PINs, and one-time passwords (OTPs), as well as personal photos or videos should never be shared, as they can be weaponised for blackmail or identity theft. Anyone who suspects they have installed a malicious application or compromised their banking credentials should immediately contact their financial institution to lock their accounts and report the incident to local Police authorities.

audit.headline: President reviews project
audit.summary: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake visited the Anuradhapura Sacred Area recently to review the progress of the proposed development project. The Anuradhapura Sacred Area Development Project aims to renovate access roads, improve facilities for devotees and local and foreign tourists, and enhance waste management, while safeguarding the historic character, antiquity and religious significance of the Anuradhapura Sacred City. The National Physical Planning Department has prepared a structural plan, which was gazetted as the Anuradhapura Sacred Area Planning Scheme. On February 27, 2026, an updated Anuradhapura Sacred Area Development Plan, together with the criteria to be followed in carrying out development activities, was published in the Gazette. The Government of India has agreed to provide funding for the project, which has an estimated total cost of Rs. 7.7 billion.

The Anuradhapura Sacred Area Development Project aims to renovate access roads, improve facilities for devotees and local and foreign tourists, and enhance waste management, while safeguarding the historic character, antiquity and religious significance of the Anuradhapura Sacred City. The Government of India has agreed to provide funding for the project, which has an estimated total cost of Rs. 7.7 billion. Upon arriving at the Anuradhapura Sacred City, the President walked through the area to inspect the sites and plans relating to the development activities. He also held discussions with officials and inquired about the progress of the work. The President inspected road development work in the vicinity of the three historic ponds in the Anuradhapura Sacred City, as well as archaeological excavations at the Western Monastery complex. He subsequently inspected the site proposed for the construction of a car park in the Atamasthana area, near the Ruwanwelisaya, and reviewed the sites and plans relating to the proposed development projects. The President stressed the importance of carrying out all development activities in a manner that safeguards the antiquity and religious significance of the historic Anuradhapura Sacred Area. audit.headline: Rain and health
audit.summary: H eavy or prolonged rainfall often triggers a cascade of physical and psychological health challenges. Understanding these diverse impacts allows us to better protect our health during changing weather patterns. The public need to pay special attention towards dengue, rat fever, diarrhea etc during this rainy condition, Consultant Epidemiologists, Virologists and General Physicians say. According to them, rain plays a fascinating, two-sided role in respiratory health. In the short term, rainfall acts as a natural air purifier. It scrubs the atmosphere by washing down particulate matter, smoke, dust, and pollen grains, providing immense relief to individuals suffering from seasonal allergies and urban smog. However, high humidity and moisture accompanying rain create ideal breeding grounds for indoor mold and dust mites.
audit.body: H eavy or prolonged rainfall often triggers a cascade of physical and psychological health challenges. Understanding these diverse impacts allows us to better protect our health during changing weather patterns. The public need to pay special attention towards dengue, rat fever, diarrhea etc during this rainy condition, Consultant Epidemiologists, Virologists and General Physicians say. According to them, rain plays a fascinating, two-sided role in respiratory health. In the short term, rainfall acts as a natural air purifier. It scrubs the atmosphere by washing down particulate matter, smoke, dust, and pollen grains, providing immense relief to individuals suffering from seasonal allergies and urban smog. However, high humidity and moisture accompanying rain create ideal breeding grounds for indoor mold and dust mites. Damp walls and poorly ventilated spaces foster fungal spores that can exacerbate asthma, trigger allergic rhinitis, and cause chronic respiratory irritation. Furthermore, a phenomenon known as “thunderstorm asthma” can occur during specific weather conditions, where high winds and moisture rupture pollen grains into micro-particles that penetrate deep into the lungs, triggering severe asthma attacks, they say. Stagnant water left in the wake of heavy rains provides the ultimate breeding habitat for mosquitoes, drastically increasing the transmission rates of vector-borne illnesses such as Dengue fever, Malaria, Chikungunya, Rat Fever etc. Public health authorities consistently emphasize clearing blocked gutters and standing water around homes during rainy seasons to mitigate this risk. Sri Lanka has just recovered from an increased number of Dengue patients, they pointed out. According to the Consultant doctors, heavy rainfall and urban flooding frequently overwhelm drainage and sewage systems, leading to the contamination of local water supplies. This increases the incidence of waterborne diseases like leptospirosis (often contracted through floodwaters interacting with broken skin or animal urine), typhoid, and Diarrhea, making access to clean drinking water a critical public health priority. Many people report an increase in joint stiffness and muscular aches when it rains. This is largely due to drops in barometric (atmospheric) pressure that precede and accompany storms. When atmospheric pressure falls, it causes the tissues surrounding joints to expand slightly, placing pressure on the nerves and triggering pain particularly in individuals with osteoarthritis, arthritis, or old joint injuries. Therefore the patients who suffer from those diseases need to take extra care themselves during rainy conditions, they say. The psychological impact of rain varies widely depending on duration, personal preference, and sunlight exposure. On one hand, overcast, gloomy days can reduce Vitamin D synthesis and disrupt circadian rhythms, occasionally leading to lethargy, low mood, or symptoms associated with Seasonal Affective Disorder (SAD). But these conditions are rare in tropical countries such as Sri Lanka. Many people experience a calming psychological effect from rain. The rhythmic sound of raindrops falling acts as white noise, which can lower cortisol levels, promote relaxation, and enhance deep sleep. Furthermore, rain increases the concentration of negative ions in the atmosphere, which are scientifically linked to improved mood and elevated serotonin levels in the brain, says scientific journals.

audit.headline: Rainfall to increase in several parts of the island over next few days

Showers or thundershowers are also expected at several places in the Uva Province and in the Ampara and Batticaloa districts after 1.00 p.m. Strong winds of 40–50 kmph are expected at times over the western slopes of the Central Hills, the Northern, North-Central and North-Western provinces, and the Trincomalee and Hambantota districts.

audit.headline: Rare loggerhead turtle released after year-long treatment
audit.summary: A critically injured loggerhead turtle, one of the rarest turtle species recorded along Sri Lanka’s coastline, has been released back into the sea after a year of treatment at a sea turtle conservation centre in Urawatta, Ambalangoda. The turtle, scientifically known as Caretta caretta, was rescued after becoming entangled in a fishing net, which caused injuries to all four of its limbs. It was brought to the conservation centre, operated by local fishermen in the Urawatta area, where it received treatment for approximately one year. After making a full recovery, the turtle was released into the sea off Urawatta beach. The release took place in the presence of foreign tourists visiting the conservation centre. Loggerhead turtles are found in various parts of the world, including waters around Australia and Turkey.

The turtle, scientifically known as Caretta caretta, was rescued after becoming entangled in a fishing net, which caused injuries to all four of its limbs. It was brought to the conservation centre, operated by local fishermen in the Urawatta area, where it received treatment for approximately one year. After making a full recovery, the turtle was released into the sea off Urawatta beach. The release took place in the presence of foreign tourists visiting the conservation centre. Loggerhead turtles are found in various parts of the world, including waters around Australia and Turkey. In Sri Lanka, they are considered a rare species and generally visit the island’s coastal waters between September and March to lay their eggs. With an estimated lifespan of 70 to 80 years, loggerhead turtles face growing threats from fishing nets, coastal human activities and hunting for their meat. The species is protected under Sri Lanka’s Fauna and Flora Protection Ordinance, which provides legal safeguards for wildlife. The successful rehabilitation and release highlight the role of community-based conservation initiatives in protecting endangered marine wildlife and reducing the impact of human activities on vulnerable species.

audit.headline: Rs. 350 Mn worth ‘Comfort Care Home’ for palliative patients opened in Chavakachcheri, Jaffna
audit.summary: A modern palliative care centre, the ‘Comfort Care Home,’ was inaugurated in Sarasalai, Chavakachcheri on Saturday, within the Jaffna district, by Health and Mass Media Minister Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa. The facility aims to provide compassionate end-of-life care, pain management and dignity to patients navigating the most difficult phases of illness. The home features 20 private rooms dedicated to palliative patients, offering round-the-clock nursing services, pain relief therapies, oxygen support, and tailored nutritional meals under medical supervision. To promote mental and emotional well-being, the centre also includes a dedicated spiritual garden. All services at the centre will be provided completely free of charge to patients in need. Constructed at a cost over Rs. 350 million, the project was financed through donations from local and international benefactors.

audit.headline: SL to focus on growth, commends India’s financial assistance
audit.summary: Industry and Entrepreneurship Development Deputy Minister Chathuranga Abeysinghe thanked India for its financial assistance during Sri Lanka’s economic crisis, saying New Delhi stood by Colombo through some of its most difficult years. Speaking at the NDTV World Summit, Abeysinghe acknowledged India’s role in helping Sri Lanka navigate the crisis that began in 2022, when severe shortages of fuel and other essentials, soaring inflation and a collapse in foreign currency reserves triggered widespread public anger and political upheaval. “I would like to thank the Indian Government and its people for being there for us at this difficult stage,” Abeysinghe said. “We came out of the economic crisis since 2022, and India greatly supported us with a lot of financial assistance and being there for us in all these difficult years”.
audit.body: Industry and Entrepreneurship Development Deputy Minister Chathuranga Abeysinghe thanked India for its financial assistance during Sri Lanka’s economic crisis, saying New Delhi stood by Colombo through some of its most difficult years. Speaking at the NDTV World Summit, Abeysinghe acknowledged India’s role in helping Sri Lanka navigate the crisis that began in 2022, when severe shortages of fuel and other essentials, soaring inflation and a collapse in foreign currency reserves triggered widespread public anger and political upheaval. “I would like to thank the Indian Government and its people for being there for us at this difficult stage,” Abeysinghe said. “We came out of the economic crisis since 2022, and India greatly supported us with a lot of financial assistance and being there for us in all these difficult years”. Asked what the transition from recovery to economic transformation would mean for Sri Lanka over the next three to five years, Abeysinghe said the Government had concentrated on restoring financial stability, restructuring debt and introducing reforms intended to prevent a repeat of the crisis. “We don’t see any risk in future in our debt repayments. And lastly, the legal peace that was supposed to be made in structural reforms, we have done. So the things that we are facing now with the global crisis are a reduction in our growth trajectory and also the reforms that we are doing. Some of them are taking time. So that’s why they have mentioned that even though we have recovered, we have stabilised. There’s more to do. So, in terms of the next few years, the real change that’s going to come from the efforts that we are putting to get our infrastructure right, because for growth, we are moving from stability to growth now,” he told NDTV. The next stage, he added, would focus on moving beyond economic stability towards expansion, with infrastructure development expected to play a central role. According to Abeysinghe, many infrastructure projects had remained stalled for nearly six years, beginning in 2019, but the Government had now restarted them and was working to accelerate their implementation. He cited India’s experience of gradually opening its markets during the 1990s as an example Sri Lanka could learn from as it sought to integrate more closely with the global economy. “I think India did this in the 1990s, slowly opening markets to the world to connect to the rest of the world. So the para-tariffs are being removed, and the trade adjustments are taking place. And I think with that, we will be able to go for FTAs, more FTAs, and that is, these are the reforms that are going to change Sri Lanka within the next three to fivr years. And I think from an industrial perspective and an economic perspective, we are eagerly, keenly looking for partnerships because that’s what’s going to make this change for us,” Abeysinghe told NDTV. He said Sri Lanka’s exports were worth nearly US$ 18 billion, with about a quarter going to the United States and a fifth to Europe. “We are also an energy-dependent country, so basically everything adjusts based on the energy prices. Within this year, energy prices have escalated three times, and it has impacted us with higher inflation and also pushed our cost of manufacturing up. So what we are doing now is, given the fiscal consolidation we have, the Government is continuing to maintain a fiscal buffer. So we were able to adjust to a certain level,” he said.

audit.headline: Saving taxpayers’ money
audit.summary: Engaging in positive, visible work allows offenders to build pro-social habits and make meaningful restitution to society. This public contribution helps soften community stigma surrounding former offenders, easing their eventual transition back into civilian life and fostering a stronger sense of civic belonging. A lot of people go into prison because they are unable to pay fines. The most pathetic situation is that the taxpayers’ money is being wasted on looking after these individuals who can actively contribute towards the development of the country and towards the upliftment of many services. This is a pure waste of man hours. Therefore the proposal made in connection with amending the Community Based Corrections Act of 1999 is highly commendable. This is one of the demands of ordinary people which they presented to all previous regimes.
audit.body: Engaging in positive, visible work allows offenders to build pro-social habits and make meaningful restitution to society. This public contribution helps soften community stigma surrounding former offenders, easing their eventual transition back into civilian life and fostering a stronger sense of civic belonging. A lot of people go into prison because they are unable to pay fines. The most pathetic situation is that the taxpayers’ money is being wasted on looking after these individuals who can actively contribute towards the development of the country and towards the upliftment of many services. This is a pure waste of man hours. Therefore the proposal made in connection with amending the Community Based Corrections Act of 1999 is highly commendable. This is one of the demands of ordinary people which they presented to all previous regimes. But those regimes turned a blind eye and a deaf ear to their demand. Sri Lanka has proposed the Community Based Corrections (Amendment) Bill to expand alternative sentencing. Under this proposed reform to the Community Based Corrections Act of 1999, eligible minor offenders may be ordered to complete 50 to 300 hours of unpaid community work instead of serving a prison sentence. There are key features in this proposal. One of those key features is that the offenders can be assigned between 50 and 300 hours of unpaid service depending on the nature of the sentence or fine. Courts will refer eligible individuals to a community corrections officer to explain the program before the offender has a continuous period of 48 hours (excluding weekends and public holidays) to consent. This is another key feature of the proposed act. The maximum fine for violating terms under the existing framework rises from Rs. 5,000 to Rs. 25,000. This is one of the significant features of the bill which is extremely relevant to the current situation that exists in the society. The bill aims to help decongest Sri Lankan prisons, which hold over 33,000 inmates against a design capacity of roughly 12,000. The bill was published in a Gazette supplement on October 13, 2026, and needed to receive parliamentary approval before becoming law. Community-based corrections have already operated under the Community Based Corrections Act, No. 46 of 1999 and the Probation of Offenders Ordinance of 1944, alongside ongoing parliamentary reviews to reduce custodial populations for petty and minor drug-related offenses. Under the proposal, courts will refer eligible offenders to a community corrections officer, who will explain the benefits of a community-based correction order before the offender decides whether to consent. Offenders will be given a continuous period of 48 hours to communicate their decision to the court, excluding Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays. The bill also proposes increasing the maximum fine under Section 14 of the existing Act from Rs. 5,000 to Rs. 25,000. The proposal also introduces a revised schedule specifying the number of hours offenders may be required to perform unpaid community work, depending on the length of imprisonment or the amount of the fine involved. Under the proposed schedule offenders facing imprisonment of one year or more may be assigned 200 to 300 hours of unpaid community work over one year while those facing imprisonment of six months to less than one year may be assigned 100 to 200 hours over six months. The offenders who are facing imprisonment of less than six months may be assigned 50 to 100 hours over three months while offenders facing a fine of Rs. 50,000 may be assigned 200 to 300 hours of community work over two years. The offenders who are facing fines below Rs. 20,000 may be assigned 50 to 75 hours over three months. Appointing community correction officers is also proposed. These officers will be responsible for supervising offenders, conducting inquiries and assisting courts in implementing community-based correction orders. Sri Lanka does not have a single, unified statutory sentencing code; instead, judicial sentencing is governed by wide judicial discretion under the Code of Criminal Procedure Act No. 15 of 1979 and evolving case law guided by a mix of retribution, deterrence, and rehabilitation. Alternatives to imprisonment (also called alternative sanctions or community corrections) are legal punishments, supervision models, or treatment programs used in place of traditional jail or prison time. These approaches aim to address the root causes of crime, promote accountability, support rehabilitation, and reduce mass incarceration. Alternatives to jail time include pre-trial diversion programs, probation, house arrest, and community service, depending on the offender’s charge and jurisdiction. Community service means completing a set number of unpaid hours working for local non-profits or public agencies. House Arrest and Electronic Monitoring means confine the culprit to his/her home using a GPS ankle monitor, typically allowed to leave only for work, school, or medical care. Keeping healthy and young individuals confined in correctional facilities without engaging them in community service programs leads to significant socioeconomic, psychological, and institutional disadvantages. Full-time incarceration without structured community work creates a heavy financial burden on taxpayers. Governments spend substantial public funds on food, security, medical care, and facility maintenance. When offenders remain idle, these expenses produce zero economic return, whereas community service allows low-risk offenders to contribute directly to infrastructure repairs, environmental cleanup, and public maintenance projects. When it comes to prisoners, idleness within prison walls severely hinders rehabilitation and re-entry. Without meaningful work, offenders lack opportunities to develop discipline, job skills, civic responsibility, and a sense of routine. Prolonged inactivity often breeds frustration, mental health deterioration, and institutional dependency, increasing the likelihood of reoffending upon release. In contrast, community service fosters social integration, empathy, and accountability by giving inmates a chance to make amends to the society they harmed. Therefore the measure can also be introduced for prisoners. Unutilised prison labour exacerbates chronic facility overcrowding and worsens prison conditions. Engaging eligible, non-violent offenders in community service relieves pressure on correctional staff, reduces internal tension, and allows wardens to allocate security resources more effectively. Deploying offenders for community service offers significant advantages by transforming incarceration from passive punishment into active rehabilitation and civic contribution. Incarceration places a heavy financial burden on state budgets. Utilizing supervised offenders’ labor for civic maintenance alleviates operational costs for local governments and public organisations, allowing taxpayer money to be redirected toward essential social services, education, and infrastructure. Community service provides incarcerated individuals with structured routine, practical work experience, and tangible skills in areas such as landscaping, construction, maintenance, and public sanitation. These experiences foster personal accountability, boost self-esteem, and significantly enhance post-release employability, reducing recidivism rates. Communities benefit directly from public work projects that might otherwise lack funding or manpower. Prisoners can assist in clearing public parks, repairing civic facilities, restoring natural environments, and supporting disaster relief efforts effectively turning a societal loss into a valuable public asset. Implementing any new project or a programme is a huge challenge in Sri Lanka because there is opposition no matter whether it is good or bad for the society. The new proposal will be another `topic’ for the opposition politicians to hang on for some time. The typical politicians in Sri Lanka are NOT focused on the well-being of people and they are ONLY focused on their own well-being. Because of this single reason local politicians ALWAYS mislead people no matter what the proposal is. Therefore implementing any new strategy is a huge challenge in Sri Lanka. The other significant fact that needs to be mentioned about the current NPP Government is their efficiency. These amendments should have been done to the law of the land a long time ago and not now. A lot of issues should have been avoided if it happened at that time. But unfortunately the duty of the Parliament is put at the bottom of the priority list by all previous regimes. There are a lot more amendments that need to be done for other laws in other subject areas such as consumer protection, environmental protection etc.

audit.body: Sri Lanka Insurance Life, for over six decades, has built its strength through financial resilience, customer centricity, disciplined governance, nationwide reach and a continuous commitment to creating long-term value for its policyholders. Strength in life insurance is built over time, through the ability to honour commitments, protect policyholders, respond to changing needs and remain resilient. With a legacy spanning more than six decades, Sri Lanka Insurance Life today stands on a strong financial foundation, anchored by the largest Life Fund in Sri Lanka’s life insurance industry at Rs. 247 billionand anasset base of Rs. 275 billion. Its disciplined fund management and longterm investment approach continue to create value for policyholders. This strength is reflected in its longstanding bonus track record. The latest declaration of Rs. 14.68 billion in bonuses for its policyholders in 2025, bringing cumulative bonuses declared since 2006 to Rs. 131.28 billion, further demonstrates the Company’s commitment to delivering longterm value to participating policyholders. “Sri Lanka Insurance Life continues to demonstrate resilience, strength, and long term stability. These achievements are a reflection of the dedication and commitment of our people, whose efforts have been instrumental in delivering sustainable growth while contributing meaningfully to national economic progress,” said Mr. Nusith Kumaratunga, Chairman of Sri Lanka Insurance Life. The strength of an insurer extends beyond its financial foundation. At SLIC Life, customer centricity is at the heart of the organisation’s approach, influencing how products are developed, services are delivered and relationships with policyholders are strengthened. With more than 230 customer touchpoints across the country, comprising its branch network and other customer service locations, SLIC Life maintains a strong presence close to the communities it serves. This reach, supported by its agency and bancassurance channels, enables Sri Lanka Insurance Life to remain accessible to customers across Sri Lanka. Customer centricity is also driving SLIC Life’s digital transformation. Investments in eKYC, digital signatures, document management, core systems and automation are streamlining customer journeys and service delivery. Building on these developments, SLIC Life has enhanced and reintroduced its customer mobile application as SLIC Life Pulse, while its Customer Portal has been refreshed with a new look and feel and enhanced features, providing customers with greater convenience and easier access to their insurance services. “Our continued focus on customer centricity and operational excellence has positioned us strongly for sustained growth in the years ahead. We remain committed to delivering long term value to customers, stakeholders and the nation,” said Dr. Sameera Dharmasena, Chief Executive Officer of Sri Lanka Insurance Life. For SLIC Life, strength is also grounded in the way it conducts its business. Strong governance, accountability, regulatory discipline and responsible business practices remain fundamental to the organisation’s operations, supported by internationally recognised certifications including ISO 9001:2015, ISO/IEC 27001:2022 and ISO 14064-1:2018. As the national Life Insurer, SLIC Life carries a responsibility that extends beyond its commercial role. Through Pasal Piriyatha Surakimu, which has benefited more than 3,365 underprivileged schools, and the Suba Pathum Scholarship Programme, which has awarded more than 2,425 scholarships valued at over Rs. 265 million, SLIC Life continues to invest in the future of the country. Its annual World Children’s Day initiative, which provides free life insurance cover to parents of newborns, further reflects its commitment to strengthening financial security for families. The strength of SLIC Life, therefore, is not built on one achievement alone. It is built through financial resilience, customer centricity, prudent management, strong governance, nationwide accessibility, digital progress, internationally recognised standards and a commitment to the communities it serves. As Sri Lanka Insurance Life looks to the future, it remains focused on strengthening customer confidence, delivering enduring value and continuing to stand alongside Sri Lankan families through every stage of life.

audit.headline: Sri Lanka climb to sixth in ODI rankings
audit.summary: Sri Lanka cricket team once again came up with good performances when they climbed to sixth place in the ICC Men’s ODI Team Rankings, moving ahead of England following their historic victory over the English side in Rawalpindi. According to the latest ICC rankings, Sri Lanka have accumulated 3,896 points from 41 matches, with a rating of 95. Sri Lanka are now ahead of Afghanistan, who are seventh with a rating of 94 and England who have slipped to eighth with a rating of 93. India lead the rankings with a rating of 115, followed by New Zealand (109), South Africa (104), Pakistan (103) and Australia (102). The rankings come after Sri Lanka successfully chased a target of 430 against England at Rawalpindi recording the second-highest successful run chase in men’s ODI history. The latest rankings, updated on October 23, confirm Sri Lanka’s sixth-place.

audit.headline: Sri Lankan exporters to gain lower-cost access to Chinese market
audit.summary: Sri Lankan exporters are set to benefit from reduced export costs and improved access to the Chinese market under a new trade cooperation agreement with China’s Yunnan Province, offering free warehousing, exhibition space and access to online marketplaces. The agreement was signed at the Sri Lanka–Yunnan Province Special Products Promotion Conference and Business Meeting held in Colombo on Friday (23), jointly organised by the Department of Commerce of Sri Lanka and its counterpart in Yunnan Province. The Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) was signed by Acting Director General of Sri Lanka’s Department of Commerce Somasena Mahadiulwewa and Director General of the Department of Commerce of Yunnan Province Li Chaowei.

The agreement was signed at the Sri Lanka–Yunnan Province Special Products Promotion Conference and Business Meeting held in Colombo on Friday (23), jointly organised by the Department of Commerce of Sri Lanka and its counterpart in Yunnan Province. The Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) was signed by Acting Director General of Sri Lanka’s Department of Commerce Somasena Mahadiulwewa and Director General of the Department of Commerce of Yunnan Province Li Chaowei. Under the “Three Free and Three Facilitations” framework, Sri Lankan entrepreneurs will receive facilities including free warehousing, permanent exhibition stalls, access to online marketplaces, customs clearance and transportation support, helping reduce the costs associated with entering the Chinese market. A Chinese delegation led by Li Chaowei, comprising representatives of more than 30 business enterprises, attended the conference alongside Sri Lankan government officials and business representatives. Addressing the event virtually, Trade, Commerce, Food Security and Cooperative Development Minister Wasantha Samarasinghe stressed the importance of bilateral cooperation and the need to strengthen the presence of Sri Lankan products in China. A Letter of Intent was also signed by Charitha Yattogoda, Director of the Department of Commerce, and Li Mingyu, Director of the Exhibition Services Center, confirming Sri Lankan companies’ participation in the 11th China-South Asia Expo in 2027. The expo is expected to promote key Sri Lankan exports, including Ceylon tea, spices, coconut products, seafood, gems and jewellery, food and beverages, and handicrafts. The conference concluded with business-to-business networking sessions connecting Sri Lankan entrepreneurs with the visiting Chinese delegation, creating opportunities for trade partnerships and market expansion.

audit.headline: TechCERT becomes Lanka’s only recipient of ASOCIO AI in Cybersecurity Award
audit.summary: TechCERT has received the ASOCIO AI in Cybersecurity Award 2026, becoming the only Sri Lankan organisation recognised in the cybersecurity category at the ASOCIO Digital and AI Awards 2026. The recognition highlights TechCERT’s development of ARGUS AI, an internal cybersecurity intelligence platform designed to support security analysis while keeping sensitive client data within its own environment. The award ceremony took place on October 6, at Swissôtel Jakarta PIK Avenue, Indonesia, during the ASOCIO Digital & AI Summit 2026. One of eight categories under the awards programme, the AI in Cybersecurity Award recognises organisations applying artificial intelligence to proactively identify, prevent and respond to cybersecurity risks across digital and enterprise environments.
audit.body: TechCERT has received the ASOCIO AI in Cybersecurity Award 2026, becoming the only Sri Lankan organisation recognised in the cybersecurity category at the ASOCIO Digital and AI Awards 2026. The recognition highlights TechCERT’s development of ARGUS AI, an internal cybersecurity intelligence platform designed to support security analysis while keeping sensitive client data within its own environment. The award ceremony took place on October 6, at Swissôtel Jakarta PIK Avenue, Indonesia, during the ASOCIO Digital & AI Summit 2026. One of eight categories under the awards programme, the AI in Cybersecurity Award recognises organisations applying artificial intelligence to proactively identify, prevent and respond to cybersecurity risks across digital and enterprise environments. Developed by TechCERT, ARGUS AI addresses a practical challenge faced by cybersecurity teams: processing large volumes of vulnerability findings from multiple tools and platforms. Differences in data formats, manual correlation of findings, research into known exploits and preparation of client reports can consume considerable analyst time. ARGUS AI automatically gathers vulnerability data from TechCERT’s internal platforms and security tools, then correlates findings with exploit intelligence. This helps TechCERT Engineers to analyze whether a vulnerability has a known exploit and understand how it could be abused and identify relevant attack techniques. These specialised AI models also support tasks including report rewriting, vulnerability analysis and summarization and reasoning about potential attack chains within authorized penetration testing engagements. Privacy is central to the platform’s design. ARGUS AI operates internally within TechCERT’s environment, allowing client information to be processed without sending it to external cloud AI services. The platform also supports rapid searches across more than 200,000 exploit and security intelligence entries. According to TechCERT’s internal measurements, searches take approximately 15–40 milliseconds. Using semantic search, ARGUS AI retrieves information based on the meaning and context of a vulnerability, helping TechCERT Engineers find relevant intelligence beyond exact keyword matches. Human oversight remains integral to its use. Security analysts review AI-generated analysis, recommendations and potential attack paths before incorporating them into client-facing work. Final decisions remain with qualified security professionals, preserving accountability and professional judgement. As Sri Lanka’s sole recipient in this ASOCIO award category, TechCERT’s achievement brings regional attention to locally developed cybersecurity innovation. It demonstrates a practical approach to adopting AI in cyber security operations while retaining control over client data and the quality of professional analysis.

audit.headline: Ten students injured after their bus collides with train
audit.summary: Ten students were admitted to the Karapitiya National Hospital after a bus carrying tuition class students collided with a train travelling from Matara to Colombo yesterday afternoon (25) near the Martin Wickramasinghe Folk Museum in Koggala. Habaraduwa Police stated that two of the injured students are in critical condition. The accident occurred when a private bus carrying around 60 students from a tuition class in Kottawa was returning after visiting the Martin Wickramasinghe Folk Museum. A student who was on board stated that as the bus left the cultural centre and attempted to cross the railway crossing, students inside the bus and bystanders shouted at the driver to stop the bus due to an oncoming train. However, ignoring the warnings, the driver proceeded forward, resulting in the rear portion of the bus being hit by the train.

audit.headline: US-listed global terrorist Sarwar dies in Pakistan
audit.summary: Muhammad Sarwar, designated as a global terrorist by the US Treasury Department, died in Pakistan’s Lahore on Sunday. “Pakistan Markazi Muslim League (PMML) Punjab President Muhammad Sarwar has passed away. He was on his way from home to the mosque to offer prayers when he collapsed and died,” a PMML spokesperson said in a statement. The exact cause of his death has not been specified by PMML. However, 24NewsHD TV Channel reported that Sarwar died “due to a head injury sustained after falling down the stairs”. PMML is a political offshoot of Mumbai attack mastermind Hafiz Saeed’s Jamaat-ud-Dawa. Saeed has been in Lahore’s Kot Lakhpat Jail since 2019 in multiple terror financing cases, for which he was convicted for multiple years, as per officials.

audit.headline: ‘Sri Lanka turning page toward sustainable, long-term transformation’
audit.summary: Moving decisively past the economic meltdown of recent years, Sri Lanka is positioning itself as a vibrant regional hub for trade, industry, technology, and investment. That was the core message delivered by Chathuranga Abeysinghe, Deputy Minister of Industry and Entrepreneurship Development, during a high-profile conversation at the NDTV World Summit 2026 in New Delhi. Participating in a session titled “Sri Lanka’s Economic Reset: Recovery, Resilience and the Road Ahead,” the Deputy Minister expressed profound gratitude to the government and people of India for standing firmly by Sri Lanka during its severe economic crisis in 2022. However, he emphasized that the island nation is now turning the page toward sustainable, long-term transformation.
audit.body: Moving decisively past the economic meltdown of recent years, Sri Lanka is positioning itself as a vibrant regional hub for trade, industry, technology, and investment. That was the core message delivered by Chathuranga Abeysinghe, Deputy Minister of Industry and Entrepreneurship Development, during a high-profile conversation at the NDTV World Summit 2026 in New Delhi. Participating in a session titled “Sri Lanka’s Economic Reset: Recovery, Resilience and the Road Ahead,” the Deputy Minister expressed profound gratitude to the government and people of India for standing firmly by Sri Lanka during its severe economic crisis in 2022. However, he emphasized that the island nation is now turning the page toward sustainable, long-term transformation. Reflecting on Sri Lanka’s economic trajectory after recording multiple consecutive quarters of growth, Deputy Minister Abeysinghe acknowledged that international bodies like the IMF and World Bank still view the recovery as somewhat uneven due to global economic uncertainties. To insulate the economy against external shocks, such as volatile energy prices and shifting tax structures in major Western export markets the government has successfully executed crucial fiscal consolidation and debt restructuring. “We have done that pretty perfectly, and we won’t get into an issue in the fiscal space going forward… the debt restructuring has taken place, we don’t see any risk in future in our debt repayments,” Abeysinghe said. Over the next 3 to 5 years, the government’s strategy centers on aggressive infrastructure revival, legal and governance reforms, and comprehensive trade liberalization. Drawing a parallel to India’s economic opening in the 1990s, Sri Lanka is actively dismantling para tariffs and expanding its network of Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) to better connect with global markets. The Deputy Minister said to accommodate incoming businesses, Sri Lanka is rapidly scaling up its industrial footprint. The government is spearheading the establishment of 18 new industrial zones,11 under the Ministry of Industry and Entrepreneurship Development and seven through the Board of Investment (BOI), to alleviate land constraints and expand manufacturing capacity While these dedicated economic zones take shape over the next one to two years, the Deputy Minister encouraged international investors to pursue immediate “quick wins” by forming partnerships with established Sri Lankan enterprises. Collaborating with local firms gives foreign investors immediate access to existing infrastructure, machinery, and established export channels to the US, Europe, and Britain. Recognizing past investor concerns regarding policy predictability and red tape, Abeysinghe assured the business community that the current administration is actively rectifying regulatory bottlenecks. He said key institutional reforms include enacting clear legislative frameworks like the Strategic Investment Act and refining regulations surrounding the Port City, establishing an Investment Support Unit directly under the President’s office to handhold investors, partnering heavily with India to build a robust digital ID backbone and digitize 27 public agencies and paving the way for a single-window digital clearance system for trade and investment within the next two years, Closing the conversation the Deputy Minister offered strong institutional guarantees regarding the permanence of Sri Lanka’s economic discipline and governance reforms. His message to the international business community remains unequivocal: “Don’t just support Sri Lanka’s recovery — be part of its growth.”

audit.headline: “Trust a National Asset”: IMF Chief Information Officer
audit.summary: Marking a milestone in the history of financial governance, the Central Bank of Sri Lanka (CBSL) celebrated its 76th anniversary on October 23 with a forward-looking oration delivered by the International Monetary Fund’s Chief Information Officer, Shirin Hamid. Addressing leaders, policymakers, and technologists, her keynote speech bridged the lessons of Sri Lanka’s arduous economic recovery with the pressing, high-stakes challenges of the artificial intelligence era. Tracing the institution’s origins back to 1950, Hamid reminded the audience that central banks were founded not merely as economic policy bodies, but as foundational institutions of trust, security, and public confidence. A central theme of the address was a direct acknowledgment of Sri Lanka’s remarkable resilience following the severe economic crisis of 2022, which saw inflation soar above 60 percent.
audit.body: Marking a milestone in the history of financial governance, the Central Bank of Sri Lanka (CBSL) celebrated its 76th anniversary on October 23 with a forward-looking oration delivered by the International Monetary Fund’s Chief Information Officer, Shirin Hamid. Addressing leaders, policymakers, and technologists, her keynote speech bridged the lessons of Sri Lanka’s arduous economic recovery with the pressing, high-stakes challenges of the artificial intelligence era. Tracing the institution’s origins back to 1950, Hamid reminded the audience that central banks were founded not merely as economic policy bodies, but as foundational institutions of trust, security, and public confidence. A central theme of the address was a direct acknowledgment of Sri Lanka’s remarkable resilience following the severe economic crisis of 2022, which saw inflation soar above 60 percent. “That progress was earned through the discipline of this institution and the patience of the Sri Lankan people,” Hamid stated. “It is one of the most impressive restorations of monetary trust anywhere in the world in this decade and it deserves to be recognized plainly.” Emphasizing that trust, once rebuilt, becomes both a national asset and a heavy responsibility, she noted that the country’s hard-won stability provides a solid foundation for embracing the next wave of technological evolution. Shifting focus to the intersection of artificial intelligence and central banking, Hamid issued a stark warning about how modern AI amplifies traditional risks and creates entirely new threat vectors for the financial sector. Pointing to vulnerabilities where internal AI assistants or widely used sales chatbots are compromised via indirect prompt injections, she noted that attackers can effectively become the trusted assistant, bypassing traditional firewalls entirely. Rather than advocating for an avoidance of technology, Hamid argued that central banks must evolve into “intelligent, AI-assisted institutions”. She introduced five non-negotiable adjectives that must govern every AI application touching financial systems: explainable, Governed, Secure, Ethical and Human-supervised. Sharing the IMF’s own institutional experiences, she highlighted how the organization built StatGPT—a specialized tool designed not to let AI memorize and guess complex economic figures (such as GDP data, which standard generative models hallucinate up to two-thirds of the time), but to query authoritative databases and provide transparent reasoning for human validation. In her closing observations, Hamid commended Sri Lanka’s ongoing digital transformation efforts, including the expansion of interbank electronic fund transfers, robust digital government revenue collection, the upcoming rollout of the Sri Lanka Unique Digital Identity (SLUDI), and active fintech engagement. She observed that being a newer and more agile economy gives Sri Lanka a unique advantage over nations bogged down by decades of legacy banking infrastructure. Concluding her Oration, she reiterated that the ultimate mission of an intelligent central bank remains unchanged across the decades: moving trust forward from the vault to the algorithm, ensuring that technology serves to preserve confidence in money, markets, and society.

audit.body: COLOMBO (News 1st); The sleek silhouette of the USS Canberra (LCS 30) has once again become part of Colombo's waterfront, with the advanced U.S. Navy warship arriving in Sri Lanka for its second port call of the year. Having previously visited Colombo in June, the arrival of the Independence-variant Littoral Combat Ship marks another chapter in the continuing relationship between the U.S. Navy and the Sri Lanka Navy, a partnership increasingly focused on maritime security, regional cooperation and stability across the Indian Ocean. The U.S. Embassy in Sri Lanka expressed appreciation for the welcome extended to the vessel and its crew, emphasizing the importance of regular naval engagements between the two countries. "We appreciate the Sri Lanka Navy's professionalism and support in making these visits smooth and efficient. Each visit reinforces the strength of our naval partnership, built on trust, and our shared commitment to maintaining security and stability across the Indian Ocean," said U.S. Ambassador Eric Meyer. For many at the harbour, USS Canberra is more than just another military vessel. Designed for speed, agility and flexibility, the ship represents a new generation of naval capability. Built in Mobile, Alabama, it is equipped to operate in both shallow coastal waters and the open ocean, carrying advanced mission systems that allow it to conduct maritime security operations, counter sea mines and support naval presence missions across the Indo-Pacific. Its arrival also serves as a reminder of the growing strategic importance of the Indian Ocean, one of the world's busiest maritime corridors and a region where cooperation between navies has become increasingly important. Yet what makes USS Canberra stand out is not only its technology, but also the story behind its name. In 2018, then U.S. President Donald Trump announced that the vessel would be named in honour of HMAS Canberra, the Australian warship lost while fighting alongside American forces during the Battle of Savo Island in 1942 during World War II. That legacy of shared sacrifice made history once again in July 2023 when USS Canberra became the first U.S. Navy warship ever commissioned in an allied nation. The landmark ceremony took place at the Royal Australian Navy's Fleet Base East in Sydney, further strengthening the symbolism carried by the vessel's name. Now moored in Colombo for the second time this year, USS Canberra arrives not simply as a visiting warship, but as a floating symbol of partnership, cooperation and a maritime legacy that stretches from the battlefields of World War II to the shipping lanes of the modern Indo-Pacific.

audit.headline: Cyclone Arnab Gains Strength, Fishermen Told to Stay Away
audit.summary: COLOMBO (News 1st); The Department of Meteorology says the deep depression that was located over the east-central Bay of Bengal and adjoining southeastern sea areas has intensified into a cyclonic storm, which has been named Arnab. Forecasters expect the system to continue tracking generally west to northwest, with further intensification likely as it moves across the west-central Bay of Bengal. According to the Department of Meteorology, Arnab could strengthen into a severe cyclonic storm by around 11.30 p.m. today, increasing the risk of hazardous marine conditions across a large section of the Bay. Meteorologists warn that wind speeds in the affected sea areas could increase to between 80 and 100 kilometres per hour at times, while thunderstorms and heavy weather conditions are also expected.

Forecasters expect the system to continue tracking generally west to northwest, with further intensification likely as it moves across the west-central Bay of Bengal. According to the Department of Meteorology, Arnab could strengthen into a severe cyclonic storm by around 11.30 p.m. today, increasing the risk of hazardous marine conditions across a large section of the Bay. Meteorologists warn that wind speeds in the affected sea areas could increase to between 80 and 100 kilometres per hour at times, while thunderstorms and heavy weather conditions are also expected. Sea conditions are forecast to deteriorate significantly, with wave heights likely to reach between three and four metres. Authorities say the affected sea areas could become very rough and dangerous for navigation. Fishermen and maritime communities currently operating in the affected regions have also been urged to move their vessels to safer locations immediately as the storm continues to strengthen.

The highest rainfall recorded in Sri Lanka between 8.30 a.m. yesterday and 3 a.m. today was reported from Pooneryn in the Kilinochchi District, which received a rainfall of 163 millimetres.

audit.headline: Keheliya Released on Bail After Court Reviews Compensation Dispute
audit.summary: COLOMBO (News 1st); Former Health Minister Keheliya Rambukwella and three other respondents, including former Health Ministry Secretary Janaka Chandragupta, were today released on bail by the Supreme Court after it was informed that compensation ordered by the court had not yet been paid in full. The order was made after a motion filed by Transparency International Sri Lanka was taken up before court. A three-judge bench of the Supreme Court, headed by Chief Justice Preethi Padman Surasena, also imposed an overseas travel ban on the respondents. The case originates from a Supreme Court ruling delivered in March, which found that fundamental rights had been violated in connection with the importation of substandard medicines during the tenure of the previous government.
audit.body: COLOMBO (News 1st); Former Health Minister Keheliya Rambukwella and three other respondents, including former Health Ministry Secretary Janaka Chandragupta, were today released on bail by the Supreme Court after it was informed that compensation ordered by the court had not yet been paid in full. The order was made after a motion filed by Transparency International Sri Lanka was taken up before court. A three-judge bench of the Supreme Court, headed by Chief Justice Preethi Padman Surasena, also imposed an overseas travel ban on the respondents. The case originates from a Supreme Court ruling delivered in March, which found that fundamental rights had been violated in connection with the importation of substandard medicines during the tenure of the previous government. At the time, the Supreme Court directed five respondents, including former Minister Keheliya Rambukwella, to pay compensation after they were named as respondents in the fundamental rights case. During today's proceedings, counsel appearing for Rambukwella informed the court that his client had already paid Rs. 20 million out of the Rs. 75 million compensation ordered by the court. The latest application was filed on the grounds that former Minister Keheliya Rambukwella and the other respondents had allegedly committed contempt of court by failing to fully comply with the compensation payment order issued by the Supreme Court.

audit.headline: Police Issue Warning Over Scams Through Dating Apps
audit.summary: COLOMBO (News 1st) - The Police Media Division has urged the public to exercise extreme caution when using online dating apps. Police warned that scammers are approaching online friendship, romantic relationshiops and marriage proposals to defraud individuals into various financial scams. The public has also been advised not to install unfamiliar or suspicious applications on their mobile phones. The Police Media Division further warned people against sharing bank details, OTPs, passwords or other personal information, as well as photographs and videos, with strangers.

audit.headline: SLNS Gajabahu Departs for India for Inaugural BIMSTEC-2026 Maritime Exercise
audit.summary: COLOMBO (News 1st) - Sri Lanka Naval Ship (SLNS) Gajabahu has departed for India to participate in the inaugural BIMSTEC Maritime Security Exercise. The inaugural BIMSTEC Maritime Security Exercise, organised by the Indian Navy, is scheduled to be held from October 30 to November 3. Naval forces and coast guard agencies from BIMSTEC member states Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Thailand are expected to participate in the event. The exercise will focus on enhancing maritime domain awareness, improving operational coordination in the Bay of Bengal region and strengthening regional maritime security cooperation.

audit.headline: Several Reservoirs Spill Amid Heavy Rains Across Sri Lanka
audit.summary: COLOMBO (News 1st) - The Department of Irrigation says several reservoirs across the country are currently spilling over due to heavy rainfall. Two spill gates of the Polgolla Mahaweli Dam were opened this morning. The water released from the dam flows into the Victoria Reservoir. Meanwhile, the engineer in charge of the Victoria Reservoir says it is nearing its maximum capacity. Due to the prevailing rainfall, two spill gates of the Kukule Ganga Reservoir were also opened early this morning. The water released from the reservoir flows into the Kuda Ganga. Meanwhile, one spill gate of the Dambulla Ibbankatuwa Reservoir was opened this morning. A water flow of 100 cubic feet per second is being released through the Dambulu Oya into the Kala Wewa Reservoir. Two spill gates of the Kala Wewa Reservoir have also been opened by six inches each.

Meanwhile, eight spill gates of the Rajanganaya Reservoir have been opened so far.

audit.headline: Suspect in Kalutara Double Murder Shot While Fleeing Arrest
audit.summary: COLOMBO (News 1st) - A police operation in Kalutara has led to the arrest of a man suspected of supplying the firearm used in the shocking double murder of a restaurant owner and his wife in Nagoda earlier this month. According to Police, the suspect was travelling in a three-wheeler when officers attempted to arrest him. However, he allegedly ignored police orders to stop and tried to flee, triggering a pursuit that ended with police opening fire. Police Spokesman, Assistant Superintendent of Police F.U. Wootler, said the operation was launched this morning based on information uncovered during the interrogation of the alleged gunman linked to the double murder. Investigators believe the arrested individual is the person who provided the firearm used in the attack that claimed the lives of the couple in Nagoda.

According to Police, the suspect was travelling in a three-wheeler when officers attempted to arrest him. However, he allegedly ignored police orders to stop and tried to flee, triggering a pursuit that ended with police opening fire. Police Spokesman, Assistant Superintendent of Police F.U. Wootler, said the operation was launched this morning based on information uncovered during the interrogation of the alleged gunman linked to the double murder. Investigators believe the arrested individual is the person who provided the firearm used in the attack that claimed the lives of the couple in Nagoda. During the attempt to evade arrest, police fired at the suspect, injuring him in the heel before taking him into custody. The suspect has been identified as 28-year-old Rajawatte Sanju, a man whom police say is linked to several criminal activities. He is currently receiving treatment under police guard at the Kalutara Nagoda Hospital. Police said the suspect is scheduled to be produced before the Kalutara Magistrate's Court today. Authorities also plan to obtain detention orders in order to question him further as investigations continue into the murder case. The double murder that stunned the Kalutara area took place on the 9th of this month, when a restaurant owner and his wife were shot dead in Nagoda, Kalutara.

audit.headline: ‘People Cannot Be Fooled’: AKD Reacts to Lula’s Victory
audit.summary: COLOMBO (News 1st); Sri Lanka's President Anura Kumara Dissanayake has congratulated Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva on his historic election victory in Brazil, describing the result as a triumph for democracy and a rejection of corruption, division and political deception. Lula secured a fourth non-consecutive term as Brazil's president after defeating Senator Flávio Bolsonaro in the presidential runoff election. In a message shared on social media shortly after the election result, President Dissanayake praised the Brazilian electorate for what he described as a decisive stand against political forces that sought to divide the country.
audit.body: COLOMBO (News 1st); Sri Lanka's President Anura Kumara Dissanayake has congratulated Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva on his historic election victory in Brazil, describing the result as a triumph for democracy and a rejection of corruption, division and political deception. Lula secured a fourth non-consecutive term as Brazil's president after defeating Senator Flávio Bolsonaro in the presidential runoff election. In a message shared on social media shortly after the election result, President Dissanayake praised the Brazilian electorate for what he described as a decisive stand against political forces that sought to divide the country. "Today, the people of Brazil did not just win an election; they defeated the forces of corruption, division and political lies." The Sri Lankan President said Lula's victory carried significance far beyond the ballot box, portraying it as a reaffirmation of the power of people to shape their own future. "Comrade Lula's historic victory in Brazil shows that the people cannot be fooled by bankrupt political dynasties and the ghosts of the past who believe might is greater than right." President Dissanayake also extended his congratulations to the Brazilian leader, commending him for once again securing the confidence of the people and returning to lead one of the world's largest democracies. "Many congratulations, companheiro, for leading the march of progress yet again!" The message came amid a wave of international reactions following Lula's election victory, with leaders across the world congratulating the Brazilian President after he secured a fourth term in office in a closely watched contest.

audit.headline: ADB approves $100 million programme to strengthen social protection and expand economic opportunities in Sri Lanka
audit.summary: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) has approved $100 million in financing to support reforms and investments that will strengthen social protection, economic inclusion, and well-being and resilience among the poor and elderly in Sri Lanka. The financing comprises a $50 million policy-based loan and a $50 million project loan. The Promoting Resilience and Opportunity for Inclusive Recovery Sector Development Program will help the Government of Sri Lanka expand livelihood and employment opportunities for low-income households, improve eldercare services, and boost the effectiveness and responsiveness of the country’s social protection system. “Sri Lanka’s economic recovery must translate into meaningful improvements in the lives and livelihoods of vulnerable people,” said ADB Country Director for Sri Lanka Shannon Cowlin.
audit.body: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) has approved $100 million in financing to support reforms and investments that will strengthen social protection, economic inclusion, and well-being and resilience among the poor and elderly in Sri Lanka. The financing comprises a $50 million policy-based loan and a $50 million project loan. The Promoting Resilience and Opportunity for Inclusive Recovery Sector Development Program will help the Government of Sri Lanka expand livelihood and employment opportunities for low-income households, improve eldercare services, and boost the effectiveness and responsiveness of the country’s social protection system. “Sri Lanka’s economic recovery must translate into meaningful improvements in the lives and livelihoods of vulnerable people,” said ADB Country Director for Sri Lanka Shannon Cowlin. “This program will help expand economic opportunities for poor households, strengthen social care services for an aging population, and build a more inclusive, responsive, and resilient social protection system that supports long-term recovery and shared prosperity.” Despite Sri Lanka’s continued economic recovery, poverty and vulnerability to shocks remain high, particularly among women, the young, the elderly, persons with disabilities, and populations in rural and disadvantaged regions. The program will address these challenges through policy reforms, institutional strengthening, and investments in livelihoods and care services. The program will support the implementation of the government’s National Empowerment Program, providing 30,000 households identified through the Aswesuma social registry across six districts, including women and youth, with livelihood grants, employment and business support, skills development and financial literacy training, and access to reliable markets. The program will strengthen the policy and regulatory framework for eldercare services and establish five model elderly day care centers in poorer districts. The centers will provide integrated care and support services while serving as demonstration sites to test and refine eldercare models that can be scaled up nationwide. The program will also strengthen social protection delivery by enhancing monitoring and evaluation systems, digital platforms, case management, and data governance. These investments will be complemented by measures to strengthen the system’s shock responsiveness, including institutional arrangements and coordination mechanisms to ensure timely and effective support during shocks related to the changing climate and other emergencies.

audit.headline: AI: The more we outsource thinking ….
audit.summary: Opinion Published on By Share Tweet Artificial Intelligence is making inroads faster than most ordinary people expected. It is now used to cheat in the classroom and to help faculty generate papers, but also for positive purposes, such as making PowerPoint presentations more concise and generating practice questions. I have used ChatGPT to edit and proof-read my assignments. I have also given it old assignments and asked it to generate new ones of similar difficulty. I use it to generate nested-loop practice questions similar to those I wrote from scratch during my years as a full-time lecturer at the University of Oklahoma. In industry and government, including warfare, weapons systems, and hiring, AI is taking a massive role in logistics, operations, and decision-making. Will it lead to more layoffs? Is it making people intellectually lazy?
